Boating with your family is a fun-filled activity. It’s a great way to slow down, cruise to new destinations, and create lasting memories. Taking them sailing can even be a rewarding and educational experience, especially if it’s their first time in the open the sea.
Before you search for , however, keep child safety precautions at the forefront of your mind. Fortunately, the process is no different from beach visits or amusement park visits. By preparing for the trip and establishing reasonable ground rules, you can have fun knowing that your family is safe.
boat rentals in Smyrna Beach, FL
At Sand Dollar Boat Rentals, we want you to make the most of your boating experience. Here are some safety tips you can follow to ensure everyone stays happy and secure on board.
A U.S. Coast Guard-approved lifejacket is a must for children 13 years old and below. Wearing them on the boat guarantees extra safety. Look for an age-appropriate design that comes with string waist and crotch snaps, a handle on the collar, and head support.
Take the kids along with you when you buy the lifejacket to make sure their gear fits them properly. Regardless of whether you’re on the dock or the cockpit of the boat, tell your kids to wear their lifejackets in case they fall into the water.
Making sure a boat is a child-friendly area before your little ones even set foot in it is crucial. This entails stowing breakable and dangerous items on board. Equipment like gear boxes, winches, windlasses, and ground tackles should be out of reach. Moreover, be sure to tell your children that areas where ropes are located out of bounds because it could cause injuries or slips.
Keep safety gear like flare guns and EPIRBS away from the children, as well. Don’t lock them away, though, since you’ll need to access them quickly in case of an emergency.
Restless or bored kids can cause trouble on board. So, keep them occupied during the cruise; let them sit at the helm of the boat with the captain, for instance. This way, you can keep watch over them easily, as well. It also helps to point out landmarks and teach them how to follow maps as you navigate the waters.
Just like rush hour traffic, waterways have primetime boating hours, as well. Often, boaters head to the ocean around mid- to late morning then stay out until the late afternoon or the early evening. To avoid boat traffic, start your trip as early as possible or wait until fellow boaters have made their way back to the dock in the late afternoon. Early mornings and evenings provide cooler temperatures and smoother waves — the ideal conditions for boating with children.
At Sand Dollar Boat Rentals, we stress the importance of boat safety as a family. With the right protection, you can have an enjoyable experience out of the water. to reserve your boat today.

TITLE: BUI Initiatives - Sanddollar Boat Rentals
August 05, 2017
Did you know:
A boat operator is likely to become impaired more quickly than a driver, drink for drink?
The penalties for BUI can include large fines, revocation of operator privileges and serious jail terms?
The use of alcohol is involved in about a third of all recreational boating fatalities?
Every boater needs to understand the risks of boating under the influence of alcohol or drugs (BUI). It is illegal to operate a boat while under the influence of alcohol or drugs in every state. The Coast Guard also enforces a federal law that prohibits BUI. This law pertains to ALL boats (from canoes and rowboats to the largest ships) and includes foreign vessels that operate in U.S. waters, as well as U.S. vessels on the high seas.
Dangers of BUI
Alcohol affects judgment, vision, balance and coordination. These impairments increase the likelihood of accidents afloat for both passengers and boat operators. U.S. Coast Guard data shows that in boating deaths involving alcohol use, over half the victims capsized their boats and/or fell overboard.
Alcohol is even more hazardous on the water than on land. The marine environment motion, vibration, engine noise, sun, wind and spray accelerates a drinker’s impairment. These stressors cause fatigue that makes a boat operator’s coordination, judgment and reaction time decline even faster when using alcohol.
Alcohol can also be more dangerous to boaters because boat operators are often less experienced and less confident on the water than on the highway. Recreational boaters don’t have the benefit of experiencing daily boat operation. In fact, boaters average only 110 hours on the water per year.
Alcohol Effects
Alcohol has many physical effects that directly threaten safety and well-being on the water.
When a boater or passenger drinks, the following occur:
Cognitive abilities and judgment deteriorate, making it harder to process information, assess situations, and make good choices.
Physical performance is impaired – evidenced by balance problems, lack of coordination, and increased reaction time.
Vision is affected, including decreased peripheral vision, reduced depth perception, decreased night vision, poor focus, and difficulty in distinguishing colors (particularly red and green).
Inner ear disturbances can make it impossible for a person who falls into the water to distinguish up from down.
Alcohol creates a physical sensation of warmth – which may prevent a person in cold water from getting out before hypothermia sets in.
As a result of these factors, a boat operator with a blood alcohol concentration above .10 percent is estimated to be more than 10 times as likely to die in a boating accident than an operator with zero blood alcohol concentration. Passengers are also at greatly increased risk for injury and death – especially if they are also using alcohol.
Estimating Impairment
This table gives a guide to average impacts of alcohol consumption. However, many factors, including prescription medications and fatigue, can affect an individual’s response to alcohol, and impairment can occur much more quickly as a result. There is NO safe threshold for drinking and operating a boat, so do not assume you are safe just because you fall into the “rarely” or “possibly” influenced categories.

Enforcement and Penalties
The Coast Guard and every state have stringent penalties for violating BUI laws. Penalties can include large fines, suspension or revocation of boat operator privileges, and jail terms. The Coast Guard and the states cooperate fully in enforcement in order to remove impaired boat operators from the waters.
In waters that are overseen solely by the states, the states have the authority to enforce their own BUI statutes. In state waters that are also subject to U.S. jurisdiction, there is concurrent jurisdiction. That means if a boater is apprehended under Federal law in these waters, the Coast Guard will (unless precluded by state law) request that state law enforcement officers take the intoxicated boater into custody.
When the Coast Guard determines that an operator is impaired, the voyage may be terminated. The vessel will be brought to mooring by the Coast Guard or a competent and un-intoxicated person on board the recreational vessel. Depending on the circumstances, the Coast Guard may arrest the operator, detain the operator until sober, or turn the operator over to state or local authorities.
Tips for Avoiding BUI
Boating, fishing and other water sports are fun in their own right. Alcohol can turn a great day on the water into the tragedy of a lifetime.
Consider these alternatives to using alcohol while afloat:
Take along a variety of cool drinks, such as sodas, water, iced tea, lemonade or non-alcoholic beer.
Bring plenty of food and snacks.
Wear clothes that will help keep you and your passengers cool.
Plan to limit your trip to a reasonable time to avoid fatigue. Remember that it’s common to become tired more quickly on the water.
If you want to make alcohol part of your day’s entertainment, plan to have a party ashore at the dock, in a picnic area, at a boating club, or in your backyard. Choose a location where you’ll have time between the fun and getting back into your car or boat.
If you dock somewhere for lunch or dinner and drink alcohol with your meal, wait a reasonable time (estimated at a minimum of an hour per drink) before operating your boat.
Having no alcohol while aboard is the safest way to enjoy the water intoxicated passengers are also at risk of injury and falls overboard.
Spread the word on the dangers of BUI. Many recreational boaters forget that a boat is a vehicle – and that safe operation is a legal and personal responsibility.

Galveston Flounder Fishing
All of our Galveston bays offer great flounder fishing, reaching its peak in the months of October and November. The cuts and sandy points along the Texas Gulf Coast are flounder heaven especially during October and November. Many of us have landed flounder by sure luck while targeting other game fish like trout and redfish.
A flounder trip is different in that it specifically targets these sought after gamefish. Your captain will use the weather, tides and season to determine the best method to ensure you land a decent share of flounder.
Flounder fish are masters of camouflage and will bury themselves in the sand or mud. They blend perfectly while buried in the sand or mud waiting for anything to swim close enough to feed on. These elusive fish dart instantly form their hiding spots to devour baitfish or passing shrimp with impressive speed for such a strangely shaped fish. Cancellation Policy
Below is the cancellation policy for each or our charter boat types if you choose not to purchase Travel Protection. The cancellation policy does change with the purchase of Travel Protection at the time you book your charter boat.
24’ – 28’ Powerboats – We require a $100 non-refundable deposit to make your reservation. The remaining balance of the boat becomes due and non-refundable 2 weeks prior.
33’ Deluxe Powerboat – We require a $200 non-refundable deposit to make your reservation. The remaining balance of the boat becomes due and non-refundable 2 weeks prior.
40’ “Vivid Dreams” party boat – We require a $500 non-refundable deposit to make your reservation. The remaining balance of the boat becomes due and non-refundable 1 month prior.

Holiday Periods – Full payment becomes due and non-refundable 1 month prior.
Travel Protection
We provide optional Travel Protection for 10% of the charter boat rate. This allows you to cancel for any reason up to 48 hours prior and get a full refund on the boat rate. Travel Protection itself is non-refundable.
We highly recommend purchasing Travel Protection so that you can get a refund on your charter boat if you need to cancel for any reason. This includes illness, death, Covid- 19, lodging cancellations, change in vacation destination, flight cancellations or delays, poor weather forecast, poor air quality forecast due to smoke or fires, road closures, or any other reason that is not the responsibility of Lake Tahoe Boat Rides.
If your Captain cancels due to weather safety, then you will get a full refund. Please note that this decision is very often a last minute decision as the weather in Lake Tahoe changes quickly. The forecast you see is only a forecast. Lake Tahoe is very big and a poor forecast often does not affect the part of the lake that we operate out of.
If you do not purchase Travel Protection and you do cancel for an acceptable reason and with enough notice, then we can issue you a credit for future use (gift card) this season.
Please communicate with us as early as possible regarding any cancellations and rescheduling so that we can do our best to accommodate you.

=== PAGE: https://www.tahoeboatrides.com/unique-things-to-do-in-lake-tahoe/
TITLE: Unique Things to Do in Lake Tahoe | Tahoe Boat Rides
Lake Tahoe offers far more than beaches and gondola rides. Its most distinctive experiences combine outdoor adventure, local history, creative stops, and access to places that cannot be reached from shore.
Explore Emerald Bay beneath the surface on California’s maritime heritage underwater trail, or travel by water to Fannette Island’s historic teahouse.
Build a private watersports day around tubing, waterskiing, wakeboarding, swimming, snorkeling, and sightseeing with a local captain.
Try an unusual aerial or alpine adventure by launching in a hot air balloon from a boat or climbing Tahoe’s only via ferrata.
Discover lesser-known indoor experiences through pottery painting, candle making, science exhibits, and an intimate dinner-and-magic show.
Plan around season, weather, travel time, and reservation requirements, especially for boat charters, guided climbs, balloon flights, and specialty tours.
Finding genuinely unique things to do in Lake Tahoe takes more digging than choosing a beach day or riding a gondola. The lake has underwater history, unusual creative spaces, high-alpine climbing routes, and experiences that begin from the deck of a boat.
This guide is designed for first-time visitors who want more than the standard itinerary and returning travelers ready to see Tahoe differently. If you’re seeking truly unique things to do in South Lake Tahoe, these experiences reveal sides of the region that many visitors miss.
1. Dive Through Lake Tahoe’s Underwater History
Emerald Bay holds more than scenery beneath its surface. California’s first maritime heritage underwater trail connects four dive sites containing historic boats and barges from Tahoe’s early recreational era. Interpretive panels help divers understand what they are seeing at depths ranging from approximately 10 to 60 feet.
Experienced scuba divers can explore the complete . Snorkelers may be able to view shallower features, depending on visibility and current conditions. Cold-water experience and proper equipment are essential.
underwater trail
2. Travel by Water to Fannette Island’s Teahouse
Fannette Island is Lake Tahoe’s only island, and watercraft provide the only way to reach it. A short but steep path leads from the rocky shore to the remains of a stone teahouse built for Vikingsholm owner Lora Josephine Knight.
The island offers a perspective on Emerald Bay that cannot be reached from its highway overlook. Visitors should use an appropriate small watercraft and check park restrictions before going. California State Parks closes the island during April and May to protect breeding wildlife.
3. Design a Private Water-Sports Day
Among the most memorable unique outdoor activities South Lake Tahoe offers is a captained powerboat outing built around your group. Start with sightseeing near Emerald Bay, then head toward open . Wakeboarding may suit more experienced riders, and calmer coves can provide time for swimming or snorkeling.
water for tubing or waterskiing
A local captain handles navigation and watches the lake conditions, leaving your group free to participate at its own pace. Longer charters give you more room to combine active time with a relaxed cruise.
4. Launch a Hot Air Balloon from a Boat
Lake Tahoe Balloons begins its sunrise flights from the Tahoe Flyer, a purpose-built vessel that carries passengers and the balloon onto the lake. The crew inflates the balloon on the launch deck before sending it over the water and surrounding Sierra Nevada.
Flights generally operate during the warmer months and depend heavily on weather. Reservations are required. This unusual air-and-water excursion also appears among Tahoe captains’ .
local favorites
5. Climb Tahoe’s Only Via Ferrata
A via ferrata uses fixed cables and built-in climbing features to help participants cross steep mountain terrain. At Palisades Tahoe, guided climbers ascend the Tram Face using steel rungs, suspension bridges, and protected routes above Olympic Valley.
No previous rock-climbing experience is required for many trips, yet participants should be comfortable hiking for several hours at elevation. The experience combines technical movement with wide alpine views that ordinary hiking trails cannot provide.
6. Enter the Secret Tunnels of Thunderbird Lodge
Thunderbird Lodge preserves the eccentric estate of George Whittell Jr. on Lake Tahoe’s Nevada shoreline. Guided tours may include the historic residence, underground passageways, card house, and boathouse. The famous Thunderbird yacht can also be viewed when available.
Reservations are typically required because visitors cannot simply drive onto the private estate. Some tours arrive by water at the lodge’s dock, adding another layer to one of the more unusual historical experiences around the lake.
7. Paint Pottery or Pour a Custom Candle
An afternoon indoors can be welcome after several days of hiking or strong mountain sun. The Hot Spot Studios in South Lake Tahoe offers drop-in creative projects that include pottery painting and candle making.
Choose a functional piece you will use at home rather than another standard souvenir. This is also a useful option when smoke, rain, or high winds change your outdoor plans. Check finishing and pickup requirements before choosing pottery near the end of your trip.
8. See the Lake Through a Scientist’s Eyes
The in Incline Village explains what happens beneath Lake Tahoe’s blue surface. UC Davis researchers use interactive exhibits to explore water clarity, ecology, microplastics, and environmental change.
Tahoe Science Center
Depending on current programming, visitors may also find docent-led experiences or 3D presentations. The center gives greater context to the landscape you have been boating beside or hiking above, making it a smart addition to a family trip or a poor-weather day.
9. Catch a Golden Trout at a Historic Fish Farm
Tahoe Trout Farm has operated in South Lake Tahoe since 1946. Visitors receive basic fishing equipment and bait, then pay for the fish they catch. No fishing license is required at the private ponds.
The farm is known for its Golden Lightning Trout and maintains a no-catch-and-release policy, so plan to cook or transport your fish afterward. It is a quirky, approachable alternative for children or adults who want to try fishing without committing to a full guided excursion.
10. Pair Dinner with an Intimate Magic Show
The Loft in Heavenly Village combines small-plate dining with Magic Fusion, an intimate comedy-and-magic production featuring rotating performers. Its compact theater creates a much closer experience than a large casino showroom.
Showtimes and age recommendations vary, with some performances designed for families and others intended for adults. Reserve the show first, then plan dinner around the scheduled performance.
11. Watch Fireworks from the Lake
When holiday fireworks return to South Lake Tahoe, viewing them from a boat changes the entire experience. The bursts reflect across the water, and your group avoids searching for a crowded shoreline viewing spot.
A private may begin with sightseeing or a sunset ride before the captain positions the boat for the show. Dates, launch locations, and local event schedules can change, so confirm the current display before booking travel around it.
fireworks cruise
How to Choose Among Lake Tahoe Unique Tours and Experiences
The right choice depends on your season, comfort level, and available time. Reserve boat-based activities early during summer because group size and charter length affect your options. Some experiences, like via ferrata climbing and hot air ballooning, also have weather limitations.
Keep one flexible activity in your itinerary. A pottery session, science-center visit, or evening magic show can rescue a day disrupted by wind or an afternoon storm. Lake Tahoe’s unique activities span the entire basin, so account for mountain traffic before combining north-shore and south-shore plans.

TITLE: Napa Valley Balloons - Conditions & Cancellation Policy
Cancellation Policy
48 Hours - You must cancel or reschedule a minimum of 48 hours prior to the departure time to avoid being charged in-full.
Ballooning is weather dependent and your flight may be cancelled because of inclement weather. Pilots base these decisions on the safety of passengers, crew, and pedestrians as well as applicable regulations.
If we don’t feel we can fly safely or legally, we will not fly. Should this occur, we will make every effort to reschedule you for a future date.
If we cancel your flight for any reason there is no charge.
Chargeback Policy
We are a small business. Last minutes cancellations and no shows affect our ability to provide our services and also inconvenience others who are not able to enjoy the experience. We take a zero-tolerance approach to chargeback fraud. By placing a booking through our payment platform, you acknowledge that you have the authority to use the credit card(s) used to place the reservation.
Chargebacks occur when your credit card provider requests that we return monies on a transaction which you dispute or claim is fraudulent. We recognize that chargebacks can happen for a variety of reasons. However, if you make a credit card payment through us in respect of a booking, and you or any member of your party later disputes this legitimate charge by raising a chargeback without merit (in our sole discretion), whether fraudulently or otherwise, we may take steps to recover any expenses resulting from such an unmerited chargeback from you or such party directly, including legal fees and other expenses.
Furthermore, in the event of any unmerited chargeback requests, we reserve the right to recover any monies by all legal means available to us, including using a third-party debt collection agency, or any other lawful means to recover funds successfully charged back to you in such circumstances.
Any intentional misuse of credit card to obtain goods or services may also result in criminal prosecution. Note that pursuant to applicable law, credit or debit card fraud may be a felony punishable by imprisonment and significant fines. We appreciate your understanding.
Physical Requirements
A hot air balloon ride is a safe and fun activity for people of almost all ages, but it is an outdoor adventure and there are some individuals for whom ballooning may not be appropriate.
Climb into and out of the basket
Stand without assistance for an hour or more
Walk through tall grass or uneven terrain back to the shuttle vehicles, etc.
Bend their knees, hang on and absorb shock under your own strength. A safe bet is if you cannot jump from a kitchen chair, a hot air balloon ride may not be appropriate or safe for you.
Infants or young children(under the age of 6years/48 inches tall)
Pregnant women
Individuals who have done a deep scuba dive within the past few days
People suffering from chronic pain, have a recent injury or who have recently had major surgery, anyone who is unable to stand without assistance for more than an hour
Someone who requires assistance walking or who cannot climb stairs.
Please understand that we will always err on the side of caution and in some cases may ask a guest to refrain from flying. If our staff cancels you because they feel they cannot fly you safely, you will not be charged and any charges will be refunded. If you have a medical problem that could cause discomfort or be aggravated during flight, please consult your physician in advance.
If you are unsure if ballooning is appropriate for you, please call us at 707-944-0228

TITLE: Illuminations Light Show - Niagara Falls State Park
Niagara Falls Illuminations
Every night shines
You know what’s pretty brilliant? Hundreds of LED lights are housed in three locations across the Niagara Gorge in Niagara Falls, Ontario. Together, these lights work to create a breathtaking view not to be missed. They are illuminated every night of the year beginning at dusk.
Throughout the year, Niagara Falls is illuminated for holidays and significant occasions, as determined by the Niagara Falls Illumination Board (NFIB). The Falls is also lit in custom colors for short durations to mark significant dates in support of charitable causes. A schedule of upcoming special illuminations is shown below.
The Falls Illumination
In 2016, almost 20 years since the last major investment in Falls lighting, the existing xenon lights were replaced with new, energy-efficient LED lighting technology. These new lights provide more than twice the previous lighting levels, programmable lighting and a wider spectrum of color. The LED lights also fill gaps to provide a more consistent lighting effect.
2026 Falls Illumination Schedule
7pm – 2am
6:30pm – 2am
6:15pm – 2am
6pm – 2am
4:30pm – 2am
How to Submit Special Niagara Falls Lighting Requests
A tradition that has now lasted for nearly a century, the Niagara Falls light show provides visitors a chance to see the Falls in a whole new way.
Since 1925, the Niagara Falls Illumination Board (NFIB) has provided nightly illumination of Niagara Falls for all to enjoy. This illumination includes a range of colors that alternate throughout the evening and shine over all of Niagara Falls.
Special Niagara Falls Lighting Requests
The NFIB has also helped to raise awareness for hundreds of charities and special causes through special Niagara Falls light show requests.
Special illuminations are limited to one 15-minute block per night at 10pm, unless otherwise specified by the Niagara Falls Illumination Board.
Governance
Niagara Falls illuminations are governed by the bi-national Niagara Falls Illumination Board. The Niagara Parks Commission (NPC) administers all special color illumination requests within the NFIB policy and current guidelines approved by the NFIB Board.
Eligibility
In addition to illuminations for annual holidays, internationally recognized signature dates and other significant occasions as determined by the NFIB Board, the NFIB accepts requests from non-denominational, non-political registered or nonprofit charities. The request must be significant to the cause and recognized bi-nationally or internationally.
Please note that special color illumination requests cannot be considered for:
Commercial requests (e.g., product launches)
Personal occasions (e.g., birthdays, marriage proposals, etc.)
Religious or political events or observations
Institutions or professions (e.g., hospitals, schools, etc.)
How to Apply
To be considered, all requests must be:
Received in writing by full completion of the Niagara Falls Illumination Board’s Special Illumination Request form
available online
Completed and signed by a management representative of the official organization making the request
Received by NPC at least 30 days in advance of the illumination date requested

Discover sea creatures
Go on an aquatic adventure at Niagara’s other “water wonder,” the Aquarium of Niagara, which is perfect for kids and anyone who is fascinated by aquatic animals.
At the Aquarium, one ticket grants you access to two buildings – one that features exotic species from around the world, and another that highlights hyperlocal species that are native to the Great Lakes.
You’ll meet playful penguins, rescued seals and sea lions, mesmerizing jellyfish, lots of fish, reptiles and amphibians, insects, and more!
Exhibits and Experiences
The Aquarium’s educational exhibits feature more than 1,500 animals in diverse ecosystems. Roll up your sleeves and enjoy hands-on animal experiences at two touch pools. Learn about the threats challenging animals in their natural habitats, and leave equipped with tangible ways to positively impact wildlife.
Interact with the Aquarium’s knowledgeable staff and charismatic animal ambassadors through animal feedings, educational presentations, and expert talks. A full schedule of programming is included with general admission.
Location and More
Western New York wildlife is front and center at Great Lakes 360, a living museum just 500 feet from the main Aquarium building that opened in 2024. View the fish, amphibians and reptiles that live right in Buffalo Niagara’s backyard at 16 immersive exhibits. Here, you can learn about native species like the musk turtle and eastern newt and even touch a massive lake sturgeon.
Located in Niagara Falls State Park, the Aquarium is accessible by the in-park Niagara Scenic Trolley (seasonal) or by taking a leisurely stroll along park trails.

FAQs
Boat FAQ's
How far are you from Islamorada sandbar? Can we take the boat to the Sandbar?
Yes you can take our boats to the World Famous sandbar is right behind our marina less that 1 mile boat ride.
Why you don’t offer OVERNIGHT rentals?
While you still responsible for the vessel, to many things can go wrong at night when the vessel is not being supervised. Here’s few good reasons, – Vessel sink due to dead battery / Most stolen Vessels, Engines and electronics happen at night / As a rented Vessel you are not allowed to use the Vessel after sunset so no sense to have the responsibility for the Vessel if you can not use it at night.
Can I keep the boat overnight?
Unfortunately we do not allow or offer overnight rentals. All boats must be returned by 6:00 PM everyday.
I've never driven a boat, how hard is it?
It’s actually very simple, if you can drive a car then you should have no problem driving a boat. Our staff will provide complete and thorough instructions prior to your rental. We also provide you with a customized map of the area that will make it easy.
Do you deliver boats?
No we don’t.
Do you rent fishing poles or snorkel gear?
Yes! Please check out our Boat Rental page for more details.
How could I lose my security deposit?
99% of our customers receive a full refund of their deposit. Deposit charges on boat rentals are most commonly propeller related caused by operating in shallow waters (depth colors are outlined in our maps and chart). Using common sense, listening to instructions, operating safely, and maintaining safe distances and water depths are smart ways to ensure a fun, yet safe, rental with no unfortunate complications.
When is the security deposit returned?

How much is the security deposit?

Do you offer insurance on the boats?

Is the cost per passenger?

Pets are allowed onboard?
yes, absolutely!
How much do you charge for tax and gas on boat rentals?
The Florida Department of Revenue regulates sales tax at 7.5% in Monroe County. Several gas options will be presented prior to your rentals including prepaying or paying at return.
What if I have a problem or need help?
All of our boats are equipped with VHF radios, VHF channels are constantly monitored by our staff, the United States Coast Guard, local marine police and almost every other boat on the water.
Where are some good fishing spots?

What is your cancellation policy?

Do we have to wear life jackets?
life jackets are provided and required to be on-board, and passengers ages 6 and under must wear a life jacket at all times.

Do I need a license to operate a Jet Ski?

Government issued ID with birth date clearly visible, credit card for guarantee, cash for gratuity, sunscreen, and a big smile to have some fun!!!
What is the best time to rent?
The earlier the better. Mornings start of slow and progressively get busier as the day goes on, with peak times early to late afternoon.
Are there any other costs?

Does the guide drive slow?

Have Questions About Your First Jump?
Want to skydive Georgia, but have questions? We’ve highlighted some of the most frequently asked skydiving questions below. Take a moment to review the skydiving FAQs below and if you still have questions, feel free to contact us directly. We’d love to speak with you about skydiving Atlanta! General Questions
How long has Skydive Monroe been in business?
Skydive Monroe was established in 1993. We’re proud to be the best location to skydive Georgia!
How do I find Skydive Monroe's location?
Our physical mailing address is 535 Towler Street, Monroe, GA 30655. Not all GPS systems have our mailing address programmed, so please verify this before beginning your trip. Please visit our for turn by turn directions to Skydive Monroe.
directions link
Are pets allowed at Skydive Monroe?
Pets are not permitted at Skydive Monroe at any time.
Is there a place where we can purchase food at Skydive Monroe?
At this time, we do not offer food services at Skydive Monroe. Vending machines for drinks and snacks are available on-site, so we do recommend bringing lunch as you’ll be with us for 5 to 6 hours for your Atlanta skydiving experience.
First-Time Skydiver Questions
What should I wear for my skydive?
Dress for skydiving so that you are comfortable for the temperatures on the ground. If it will be a warm day, then a T-shirt, shorts and tennis shoes will be best. If it’s going to be a chilly day, then jeans, a long-sleeved T-shirt and tennis shoes are recommended. If it’s particularly cold then we recommend long-johns or Under Armour wear (works particularly well). We will be providing you with a jumpsuit to put on over your clothing, so please do not wear anything too bulky (heavy jackets). Tennis shoes or ‘sneakers’ is recommended for footwear. Boots are not recommended. Ladies can also read our article for tips on .
how to wear your hair for skydiving
Should I arrive earlier than my scheduled time?
No. Arrival time is your booking time. You will be at the DZ for approximately 5-6 hours. Please prepare for this as there is some downtime between your training and actually boarding the plane. There is much happening behind the scenes by-way of re-packing parachutes etc. Please be patient and prepare for one of the best experiences of your life!
Should I eat before I jump?
Skydiving is not like being on a roller coaster so you will not feel sick while in freefall. Ideally, we wish you to be hydrated and to eat normally. Guests often feel nauseated after the skydiving experience if they’ve eaten nothing at all because of the surge of adrenaline during the experience. So, make sure to !
eat before skydiving
Why will I be at Skydive Monroe for between 5 and 6 hours?
Skydive Monroe is fortunate to fly a large, 14 passenger aircraft that takes passengers up to 14,000 feet allowing for the best skydiving experience. Because of the major expense of operating a large aircraft, heavy volume is required to fly. The design of our booking schedule is to allow customers to be with us for between 5 and 6 hours. The wait time is created by having to pack parachutes for both tandem and videographer parachutes alike.
Much is happening behind the scenes, so please be patient and stay relaxed for the experience of a lifetime. Wait times are greatly reduced for those scheduled early in the mornings (8:00 and 9:00am).
The weight restriction for men is 225 lbs and 170 lbs for women, how strict are you on this weight requirement?
Regrettably, not everyone can skydive. There are many variables to skydiving and weight is just one of them. Our parachute systems have a maximum designed weight limit. On a tandem jump, the combined weight of the passenger, gear, the tandem instructor are factored to ensure we are within the set forth by the equipment manufacturer.
weight restrictions
Even if you are within the weight limit, your Body Mass Index and your body shape make any skydive more of a risk to you.
On Tandem Skydives a pear shaped or apple shaped individual typically has a lot of weight sitting on the thighs which can be extremely uncomfortable for the ride under parachute. This can result in nausea, loss of circulation and even unconsciousness.
Exceptions can be made for the women’s category of 170 lbs based on fitness levels.
We recognize that issues of weight are sensitive and they are handled with discretion. If in doubt, please give us a call; we would be happy to discuss these details with you or have you visit the dropzone prior to your scheduled jump to assess the fit of the skydiving harness and your safety.
Ultimately, our primary focus is the safety of our guests. Skydive Monroe reserves the right to refuse service to anyone for the safety of our guests and instructors. Learn more about restrictions and why they are in place.
skydiving weight limit
If I have friends and family coming to watch, what time should they arrive?
Unless your booking time is for either 8:00 or 9:00 AM, we recommend that spectators arrive approximately an hour and a half after your reservation time. If you have an 8 or 9 AM time, please have your guests come with you or within 30 minutes of your scheduled arrival time so they don’t miss your experience skydiving Atlanta.
Please note that all children 12 years and under must be under adult supervision at all times.
Should I tip my instructor or videographer, what is standard procedure?

TITLE: Skydiving FAQs | Commonly asked Questions | Skydive Monroe
AFF Training Questions
What is AFF?
The AFF training program is a comprehensive seven jump program designed to train an individual with a strong foundation to become a solo, certified skydiver by developing safe freefall and canopy skills. From your first jump, you will be skydiving with individual parachute equipment and will be responsible for its operation.
There are seven levels in the AFF program; each level features targeted learning skills for you to master. The jumps allow you to practice basic freefall awareness.
After deploying your parachute at approximately 4500 feet, you will be assisted with canopy control via ground to air communication.
AFF is the most commonly employed path to becoming a licensed skydiver. What are you waiting for, call to book your first skydive today at Georgia’s finest drop zone!
You should plan to wear comfortable season appropriate clothing and athletic shoes (no open toes).
You will be asked to wear a jump suit and head gear to protect your clothes from wear and tear.
There are of 225 lbs for men and 170 for women.*
*Some exceptions will be made based on an assessment of your fitness. Skydive Monroe also maintains the right to refuse service to anybody deemed unfit or in cases where you and/or the instructors safety would be put in jeopardy.
Am I required to do a tandem skydive in order to enroll in AFF?
No, tandem skydiving is not required to begin the AFF program, however it can aid in better awareness during your first skydive. Each level within the AFF program requires an individual to achieve different skill sets while in freefall. If the feeling of freefall has never been experienced, it can be a distraction as your senses process this new feeling. A tandem skydive allows you to experience freefall and will give you a better understanding if solo skydiving is an activity you would enjoy pursuing. It is encouraged, but not a requirement.
What is entailed with the First Jump Course?
The first jump course involves six hours of classroom training followed by a level one jump in the afternoon. The first jump course will identify the parachute gear and how it works, correct freefall body position, identifying and handling emergency procedures, and flying the canopy. The level one jump will include two freefall instructors alongside you while in freefall until the time of deployment. Once under canopy, a member of the ground crew will instruct you on proper flying techniques and landing via wireless radio.
What is involved with each level?
Each level represents a skill set the student is required to learn and demonstrate while in freefall. Advancement to the next level will not occur until each student properly demonstrates that he / she can execute the specific skills introduced for the particular level. Failure to demonstrate this skill set may require the student to repeat the level.
How often should I be jumping while enrolled in the AFF program?
Students are encouraged to stay as current as possible and not allow too much time to elapse between jumps. Ideally, the more jumps one can make in a shorter period of time, the better. This helps improve confidence and allows you to progress more quickly. Students who go beyond 30 days from their last jump will be required to repeat their last, successfully completed level. Students who surpass 90 days since their last completed jump will be required to sit through the first jump course as a refresher on procedures.
What happens after AFF Level 7 is completed?
Following level seven, the student will be jumping without radio assistance and will begin to develop freefall and canopy skills beyond basic competencies as taught in the AFF program. Emphasis will be placed on meeting all skill sets required on the A license proficiency card. The main goal for a new skydiver is to attain an A-license which permits skydivers to jump with other, non-instructor skydivers. The A license also allows jumpers to jump at other dropzones.
What is required to attain the A license?
A minimum of 25 jumps is required to attain an A license. If the student has completed a tandem skydive, the tandem is included in this 25 jump requirement. The A-license proficiency checklist (you will receive one at the beginning of your First Jump Course) must be fully completed. Also the ability to pack a parachute correctly is a requirement when earning the A license.
Once I become an A licensed skydiver, what should I do about owning my own gear?
It is recommended that new jumpers purchase used gear before owning brand new gear. As you gain more experience, you’ll learn more about the discipline of skydiving you wish to participate in and eventually you will probably want a smaller canopy. It is always recommended to purchase used gear that has been properly inspected by an FAA certified parachute rigger to determine gear quality and airworthiness.

TITLE: Skydiving Safety Rules: What Every Jumper Needs to Know | Skydive Monroe

Safety Rules at Skydive Monroe
Skydiving Safety FAQs
Skydiving comes with inherent risk, which is why the sport is governed by extensive regulations, training requirements, and equipment standards. First-time jumpers must meet requirements involving age, weight, physical condition, and sobriety, while instructors and licensed skydivers must follow additional procedures for equipment, weather, airspace, and emergency situations. These rules don’t eliminate the risks of skydiving; they provide a framework for recognizing and managing them before and during a jump.
From the moment a skydiver arrives at the dropzone, there are requirements governing everything from who can participate to what equipment can be used, how parachutes are maintained, and when weather conditions are acceptable for jumping.
Skydiving is an extreme sport with inherent risks, and the rules exist to help manage those risks. Our top priority is skydiving safety.
Whether you’re considering your first tandem skydive or you’re curious about what goes on behind the scenes, here’s what you should know about the rules that govern the sport.
Before you can make a skydive, you have to meet certain basic requirements. These vary depending on the type of jump and the dropzone, but several are especially important for first-time tandem skydivers.
Age Requirements
At Skydive Monroe, you must be at least 18 years old and show valid, government-issued photo identification in order to make a skydive. Minors cannot participate even with permission from a parent or guardian.
Weight limits aren’t arbitrary. Parachute systems have maximum operating weights, and a tandem skydive involves the combined weight of the student, instructor and equipment. At Skydive Monroe, the current tandem
are 225 pounds for men and 170 pounds for women, including clothing and shoes. Exceptions may be considered based on fitness and other factors.
The fit of the skydiving harness is another consideration. Body shape and weight distribution can affect how a tandem harness fits and how the student experiences the jump under canopy.
Physical Condition and Sobriety
You don’t need to be an athlete to make a tandem skydive, but you do need to be physically capable of participating. Certain medical conditions may increase the risks associated with jumping, so anyone with concerns about their ability to participate should discuss them with a qualified medical professional as well as the dropzone beforehand.
Alcohol and skydiving
don’t mix, either. Participants need to remain alert and capable of following instructions throughout the experience. Skydive Monroe requires that participants are not under the influence before their scheduled jump, and alcohol is not permitted on the premises.
Many skydiving rules and regulations focus on what happens before the aircraft ever leaves the ground.
Follow Your Instructor’s Briefing
Tandem students receive a pre-jump briefing covering the basics they’ll need for the skydive, including aircraft procedures, exit position, freefall body position and landing technique. A tandem student isn’t expected to know how to skydive independently, but they are expected to listen and respond to their instructor’s directions. Paying attention matters.
Follow Weather Restrictions
Skydiving is weather dependent.
Wind, clouds, precipitation
, visibility and conditions at different altitudes can all affect
whether
(see what we did there?) a jump proceeds. A clear sky doesn’t necessarily mean conditions are suitable. Wind direction, gusts and winds aloft can also factor into the decision to jump. If conditions aren’t appropriate, a jump may be delayed or rescheduled.
Maintain Separation
Tandem skydivers aren’t the only people in the sky. Exit order, freefall groups, and canopy traffic are coordinated to provide appropriate separation between jumpers. At Skydive Monroe, tandem pairs generally leave the aircraft several seconds apart to create separation between groups.
Follow Camera Restrictions
Tandem passengers aren’t permitted to bring their own action cameras such as GoPros. A camera can become a distraction or create an entanglement hazard during a skydive. Professional camera flyers have the training and experience required to operate camera equipment around other skydivers. Which is why we offer awesome
video services
for our tandem skydivers to capture their skydiving adventure from start to finish.
Skydiving equipment is regulated with redundancy and accountability in mind, creating multiple layers of oversight throughout the system.
Reserve Parachutes
A skydiving parachute system contains both a main parachute and a reserve parachute. The reserve isn’t simply stowed and forgotten. Reserve parachutes must be inspected and repacked according to applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements by an appropriately certificated parachute rigger.
Automatic Activation Devices
AAD
monitors altitude and descent rate. If its activation parameters are met, it is designed to initiate deployment of the reserve parachute. An AAD is a backup device, not a replacement for training or emergency procedures.
Equipment Inspection and Maintenance
Parachute equipment
must be maintained according to applicable regulations and manufacturer requirements. For first-time tandem passengers, the technical equipment work happens behind the scenes. For licensed skydivers, equipment inspections and maintenance become an ongoing part of participating in the sport.
Tandem instructors
must meet extensive experience and certification requirements. Federal regulations establish requirements for tandem parachutists, while the United States Parachute Association (USPA) provides additional training and rating standards for instructors participating in the sport. At Skydive Monroe, tandem skydives are conducted with USPA-certified instructors and jumpmasters.
Students pursuing solo skydiving skills through the Accelerated Freefall (
) course are taught by certified AFF instructors. As jumpers gain experience and eventually earn
skydiving licenses
, responsibility for decision-making, equipment, and emergency procedures increasingly shifts to the individual jumper.
is a USPA member dropzone, meaning we operate under the standards and safety guidelines set by the United States Parachute Association. USPA membership requires adherence to nationally recognized training, equipment, and operational best practices designed to promote consistent prioritization of safety across participating skydiving centers.
At Skydive Monroe, we follow both USPA requirements and our own operational policies. First-time tandem students must meet our age and weight requirements, provide valid photo identification, and arrive prepared to participate. Weather conditions are evaluated before every jump, and we reserve the right to refuse a jump if conditions are unsafe or if a participant is not fit to skydive. All tandem passengers must also complete a
pre-jump training
session, and personal action cameras are not permitted during the skydive.
These safety rules at Skydive Monroe are designed to manage risk, maintain compliance with USPA standards, and ensure every jump is conducted as safely as possible.
What are the safety regulations for skydiving?
Skydiving in the United States is governed by applicable Federal Aviation Regulations (FARs), while USPA members also follow the organization’s Basic Safety Requirements (BSRs). These cover areas such as aircraft operations, equipment, student training, weather conditions, landing areas, and emergency procedures. USPA’s Skydiver’s Information Manual (SIM) provides the standards and recommendations used throughout the sport.

Lake Tawakoni information
Lake Tawakoni is the 4th largest inland lake in Texas. It's almost 40,000 acres and is the Best Fishing Lake in Texas. Tawakoni is incredibly diverse in its fishing it offers. From the black bass fishermen to the pickiest monster Blue Catfish fishermen, Tawakoni has it.
Lake Tawakoni is located on the Sabine River in Hunt, Rains, and Van Zandt counties. A permit for project construction was issued to Forrest and Cotton by the State Board of Water Engineers on December 20, 1955. Land acquisition was initiated in 1956 and completed in October 1960. Construction on the earth filled Iron Bridge Dam and concrete spillway began in January 1958 and was completed in October 1960. The water supply project is owned an operated by the Sabine River Authority and was funded through a water supply agreement with the City of Dallas to provide water for municipal and industrial purposes. The lake has a capacity of 936,200 acre-feet and a surface area of 36,700 acres. Crest elevation is 437.5 feet above mean sea level. The maximum depth is 70 feet. The 200-mile-long shoreline makes its way through Hunt, Rains, and Van Zandt counties.
Located some 50 miles east of Dallas and 12 miles south of Greenville, the reservoir's primary purpose is to provide water for the surrounding communities and the City of Dallas. In addition, the lake provides water-oriented recreation for much of central and northeast Texas. Fishing is the primary recreational sport with catfish being the lake specialty. West Tawakoni, located at the west end of the 2-mile Bridge, was awarded the distinction of being the Catfish Capital of Texas by the Texas State Legislature in 2001. In 1995, The Texas Legislature declared Wills Point the Bluebird Capital of Texas.
The lake has many parks and marinas including Lake Tawakoni State Park which is a 376.3-acre park in Hunt County with 5.2 miles of shoreline along the south-central shore of the main body of the reservoir.

TITLE: Winter Fishing Charters in Daytona Beach
Fishing Daytona Beach in Winter
Of course, the weather does not always cooperate during the short winter months here in Central Florida. The temperature is almost never too cold to enjoy a great day of fishing but the winds offshore can be another matter. Cold fronts, which are seldom cold by the time they reach Daytona Beach, can bring some high winds that make the seas too rough for fishing.

Northeasterly winds can create large choppy waves that can be downright uncomfortable or dangerous even in a fishing boat as large as 29 feet like Captain Corey’s.
All the same offshore bottom dwelling species including snapper and grouper are there to catch in the winter months of December, January and February as they are the rest of the year. However winter northeasterly winds can kick up the waves on any given winter day and make an offshore fishing trip impossible. Consult with Captain Corey about the possibilities of offshore fishing on a specific winter day!
They are found in every saltwater estuary in Florida from Pensacola to Key West. Redfish are also found in nearshore and offshore waters off the coast of Florida. They are popular for two simple reasons: They put up a good fight and they taste really good.
It was this good taste that got redfish in trouble back in the 1980s. Cajun chefs in Louisiana where redfish are also popular, made the dish “Blackened Redfish” a national craze and before long redfish were endangered around the country. Strict regulations helped bring them back but the result is commercial fishing for redfish is banned in Florida waters. But lucky for recreational fishermen in Florida, fishing for redfish is still allowed year round in Florida waters. Today they are the most sought after fish in Florida estuaries for Florida inshore fishing charters. The same goes for Daytona Beach inshore fishing charters and all inshore fishing charters in the Daytona Beach area including Ponce Inlet inshore fishing charters and New Smyrna Beach inshore fishing charters.
The best part is that Redfish are found in estuaries near Daytona Beach year round, they are biting year round and Redfish season is year round. Chilly weather does not bother Redfish. They are found as far north as Massachusettes. In fact the weather in the Daytona Beach area even in December, January and Februaruy, the coldest months of the year, is downright perfect for fishing redfish near Daytona Beach.
Redfish are also known as Red Drum, Spot Tails or just Reds. They are easily recognized by the dark spot on the tail which can sometimes be several spots in a small grouping. Juvenile redfish typically inhabit the estuaries until they are about 4 years of age, typically 28 inches and about 10 pounds. After that they are considered adult redfish and usually move into nearshore or offshore waters where they can grow much larger.
The Florida State Record for a Redfish is 52 lbs 5 oz, caught near Cocoa in Brevard County, the next county south of Volusia County where Daytona Beach, Ponce Inlet and New Smyrna Beach are located. These big bull redfish are a blast to catch and are beautiful specimens for a quick photo trophy. However these are the breeders and are strictly catch and release. But no loss, since every seafood chef in this part of the country knows that the best tasting Redfish are the smaller juveniles which are legal to keep within limits. Keeper size juveniles are typically between 18 and 27 inches long.
Juvenile Redfish can be found all around the Daytona Beach area in saltwater and brackish water estuaries. Daytona Beach fishing charter captains, including Captain Corey of On The Hook Charters, find juvenile redfish in the Halifax and Spruce River estuaries, canals, tidal creeks and around Ponce Inlet. The big bull redfish, which are a real challenge to land and a lot of fun to catch can be found in Ponce Inlet and just offshore. You can’t keep them but every fishing charter captain in the Daytona Beach area targets them as popular sport fish for their fishing guests.
Sheepshead are very plentiful around Daytona Beach during the winter months!In December, January and February they are stewing up around docks and bridges, along the Intracoastal Waterway and the inshore side of inlets. Sheepshead can be a challenge to catch as they have an uncanny ability to clean a hook without you knowing what happened. However, with their abundance around Daytona Beach during the winter months, you’ll get plenty of chances. They are also pretty good eating.
The Florida State Record for Sheepshead is 15 lb 2 oz, caught near Homosassa in Citrus County in Central Florida.
Spotted Seatrout, also known as Speckled Trout, are not a member of the trout family but of the drum family. They are a very popular catch on Daytona Beach fishing charters, especially inshore fishing charters during the winter months. Spotted Seatrout in the allowed length range of 15 to 20 inches for “keepers” typically weigh in at about 1.5 – 3 pounds but longer fish that weigh in at 5 pounds or more are not uncommon. Anglers may keep 4 Spotted Seatrout per day with one over 20 inches. Adult spotted seatrout can reach 19-25 inches in length and 3-17 pounds in weight.
The Florida State record for a Spotted Seatrout is 17 lbs 7 oz, caught near Fort Pierce, Florida, just down the coast from Daytona Beach.
They are typically found inshore or nearshore around seagrass, mangrove-fringed shorelines, deep holes and channels, above oyster bars and even in the surf of barrier islands near Daytona Beach. They are very abundant in the Daytona Beach area year round and the Daytona winter months of December, January and February are no exception.
Spotted Seatrout are often caught on inshore fishing charters in the Daytona Beach area including inshore charters in and around Ponce Inlet and New Smyrna Beach. They are not bothered at all by the cooler weather found in Daytona Beach during the winter. They are common much further up the Atlantic Coast all the way to Virginia and Chesapeake Bay and in the Gulf of Mexico up to Louisiana which has considerably colder winters than the Daytona Beach area. They can be found as far north as the coast of Cape Cod, Massachusetts. So you see, fishing for spotted sea trout in the Daytona Beach area during the winter months is not a problem at all. Plus they are extremely tasty fish. Fried, sauteed or baked, they are very good eating fish.
Along with Redfish and Spotted Seatrout, Flounder are one of the best tasting fish anyone can catch on a Daytona Beach inshore fishing charter. There is a limit of 10 Flounder per fisherman per day throughout the State of Florida. Considering that Flounder is one of the most tender, tasty fish that you can catch anywhere, the combination of good eating and high limits makes Flounder a sought after species for any Daytona Beach fishing charter.
Flounder inhabit a wide variety of coastal inshore and nearshore habitats from brackish water rivers and tidal creeks to nearshore waters off Daytona Beach. Although they are bottom hugging fish of shallow salt and brackish waters, they are comfortable in sandy, muddy or rocky bottoms. They are often found close to shoreline structure such as stumps and dock and bridge piles. A popular method of fishing for Flounder is gigging at night with the use of a lanterns. Flounder can get quite large for a shallow water species.
The Florida State record for a Flounder is 20 lbs 9 oz, caught in Nassau County just up the coast from Daytona Beach.
They can grow quite large and put up one heck of a fight when hooked. === PAGE: https://montereybayecotours.com/otter-guarantee/
TITLE: Otter Guarantee | Monterey Bay Eco Tours
WE GUARANTEE YOU SEE OTTERS OR YOUR MONEY BACK!
We know you love Otters because who doesn’t? That is why we are offering a money-back guarantee if you don’t see an otter on one of our daily tours. Of course, there are other animals including sea lions, harbor seals, and an abundant array of migratory birds in the Elkhorn Slough just waiting to be discovered. However, we guarantee you will see Southern Sea Otters or YOUR MONEY BACK!!!!
We can’t guarantee what the otters will be doing because this is an active bunch of sea otters in the Elkhorn Slough. We are also very proud to be certified Wildlife Stewards with Sea Otter Savvy. What does that mean? It means that we take great care in making sure we have the least amount of impact on these amazing creatures as possible. The otters of the Elkhorn Slough have pups all year long, so you have an excellent chance to see a mom feeding or playing with her pup. Since otters need to eat upwards of 25% (a nursing mother needs about 50%) of their body weight in food each day you will probably see otters diving and hunting for food. That also means it is very important to give them space as we are spotting them. When they reemerge they may be gulping their food down before their pups try to steal it or perhaps you will spot a mom training her adolescent pup how to forage for him or herself. Since otters don’t have blubber, they keep warm by constantly grooming their very dense fur. By trapping air bubbles in it, they create a sort of insulating effect. So you could spot them rolling around and doing all sorts of gymnastic maneuvers.
Another important activity for Southern Sea Otters in the Elkhorn Slough is sleeping. These otters need their beauty rest! We will generally see a raft or two of darling sleeping otters. We love watching these otters floating with their paws out of the water. Which preserves their energy and keeps them warm. It is so incredibly important they are not disturbed during this vital part of their daily routine. So bring your binoculars and come check out these amazing creatures while an experienced naturalist gives you a guided tour of this incredible ecosystem.

Utilizing the ancient design of the canoe stern below the waterline, the builders added modern design additions and materials to create an extremely light, efficient catamaran that can be powered by electric motors. This greatly reduces noise and eliminates emissions.

TITLE: Seattle's Tall Ship Sailing Tours
Seattle’s Tall Ship Sailing tours
Sail Seattle in Style
Book Your Tour
Discover Seattle Like You’ve Never Seen It Before.
Seattle’s Tall Ship operates the eye-catching sailing ship from Seattle’s historic downtown waterfront. We offer multiple public Seattle sailing tours daily, including our stunning sunset sailing tour. We also offer periodic special event tours and private charters. Browse our sailing tours below to see what we offer. We look forward to seeing you on the water!
Seattle Harbor Sailing Tour
Come aboard for a day sail on our classic schooner! Our Harbor Sailing tour is an excellent, family-friendly way to enjoy the beauty of Seattle’s waters! We will depart from our dock at Pier 66 Bell Harbor Marina, then set our sails for a 2-hour cruise in the Puget Sound.
Evening Colors Sunset Sail
An absolute “Seattle Must Do!” We will set the sails, turn off the engine, and relax as the cool sea breeze powers us through the Puget Sound. Enjoy a drink as the sun dips down behind the Olympic Peninsula and bathes the Seattle skyline in sparkling twilight colors.
Sailing Sunday Brunch Buffet
Enjoy a delicious brunch buffet aboard Seattle’s Tall Ship. Indulge in the perfect combination of relaxation, breathtaking views, and the included mouthwatering buffet prepared by .
Arista Catering
Private Charters
Our private charters are perfect for weddings, corporate events, private parties or any other occasion. Open bar and catering packages available as well. Contact us for more information or to book a charter!
Our Tall Ship Seattle Sailing Tours Will Leave You Breathless.
Sailing with Seattle’s Tall Ship is an experience like no other. Transport yourself to a bygone era, where mariners were the heart of trade and cultural prosperity. Aboard our twin-masted Schooner, guests will experience the thrill of sailing Puget Sound against the majestic backdrop of the Olympic mountain range. Take a turn at the helm, or simply unwind on deck with your favorite beverage as our skilled crew guides you on a journey you won’t soon forget.
No Sailing Experience Required
Sailing onboard this graceful, twin-masted ship evokes the romance of a bygone age. The harmony of a massive ship under sail and wind power is a truly unforgettable experience. Sit back and take in the beautiful scenery as our friendly, skilled captain and crew read the wind and let it guide the days sailing route. The Bay Lady is equipped with a powerful motor should the day demand it, but most tours will be done under wind power alone.
See More Photos
Meet the
Our pride and joy, the Bay Lady is an 85 foot traditional gaff-rigged schooner that can accommodate up to 87 passengers per tour. She is a family friendly ship, equipped with two onboard bathrooms, an onboard drink and snack bar, plenty of outdoor seating, and a cannon to salute our magnificent city!
85 feet long | 19 feet wide | 88 feet tall | 8 foot draft | 55 tons | 4500 sq ft of sail!

TITLE: A Glimpse Into History | Halifax Explosion Tour on the Water
Halifax Explosion Tour
On December 6, 1917, the face of Halifax was changed forever. While many explore this history through monuments on land, the true scale of the Halifax Explosion can only be fully understood from the harbour.
Join Halifax Harbour Tours for a commemorative journey into the past. This specialized tour traces the fateful path of SS Mont-Blanc before the collision with SS Imo, leading you through the Narrows to the epicenter of one of the most devastating man-made explosions in human history.
Tour Details
Sackville Landing (Next to the Wave).
Kara Gordon-Mackay (Maritime Museum of the Atlantic).
Local History, Maritime & Wartime Regulations, Post-Explosion Relief Efforts
Our quiet, comfortable boats allow for clear narration and an intimate atmosphere for questions and discussion.
From:
The Echoes of 1917: Halifax Explosion Historical Boat Tour
We are proud to feature Kara Gordon-MacKay as your expert guide for this experience. A long-time Halifax Harbour Tours guide and full-time staff member at the Maritime Museum of the Atlantic, Kara brings an unparalleled depth of knowledge to the tour. Her daily work at the museum is dedicated to preserving Halifax’s maritime legacy, making her the ultimate storyteller to guide you through the events, the heroes, and the heartbreak of 1917.
The Journey
Setting out from our dock at Sackville Landing, we head north toward the historic site of the collision near Pier 6. Along the way, you will:
Trace the Collision Course: See the exact stretch of water where the Mont-Blanc and Imo met.
Hear Untold Stories: Move beyond the basic facts with curated accounts of survival, the immediate relief efforts, and the resilience of a city that refused to stay down.
Experience the “Narrows”: Navigate the narrowest part of the harbour to understand the navigational challenges that led to the disaster.
Why See it by Boat?
The Halifax Explosion was a maritime event. To stand on the deck of our eco-friendly vessel and look toward the shore of the North End is to see the disaster as the sailors and dockworkers saw it that morning. It provides a sense of scale and distance that is impossible to replicate on a walking or bus tour.

=== PAGE: https://skydiveskylark.com/pages/faq
TITLE: FAQ
 – Skydive Skylark
FAQ
You've got questions, we have answers, let's see if they match up.
Collapsible content
Is there an age / weight limit to skydive?
Skydivers must be 18 or older to participate.
​We can take passengers that weigh up to 220 pounds . We can occasionally take bigger people depending on the weather and body composition. Max weight of the tandem pair and equipment together must remain under 500 pounds.
A $25 service fee if the passenger weighs over 200 pounds. This offsets the additional fuel, and wear on the equipment and instructor.
When are you open?
We take reservations
Fridays: 12 pm to 5 pm
Saturday and Sunday: 9 AM to 5 PM
We are also open on certain holidays, check the booking calendar or call for a specific date and time.
What should I wear to skydive?
Wear seasonally appropriate clean, comfortable clothes and lace-up shoes that you don’t mind getting torn, or dirty.
In the summer T-shirts and athletic shorts feel nice and cool at altitude and not too hot on the ground. Warm thin layers in the winter will keep the wind from making you uncomfortable. We have jumpsuits available at your request.
When should I arrive?
Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your appointment time. We will fill out the necessary paperwork, give you some brief instructions, and put on the necessary equipment prior to your skydive. Plan to be at the airport for 2-3 hours in case there is weather or other such delays.
How high do we jump?
We will exit the airplane at approximately 2 miles above the ground. During your freefall, you will get to speeds of around 120 miles per hour before we deploy the parachute. While we are under parachute you can direct your instructor to take a nice leisurely descent and enjoy the cool air and silence away from the hustle, or you can ask them to spin you up and do a bunch of speed-inducing maneuvers.
What kind of weather can we jump in?
There are times we have to delay due to rain, clouds, or dangerous winds. In these cases, we will send out a delay notification to the phone and email in the reservation.
​If you are worried about the weather please give us a call (254-947-3483) before you come out. We would be happy to discuss the current jump conditions.
I want to jump by myself, do I have to do a tandem?
Tandem Skydiving is by far the safest, least time-consuming and most affordable way to experience freefall.
To become a licensed skydiver please visit USPA.org for more information.

About US
Welcome to Skydive Skylark, where you can experience the sky and live the difference. Founded in 1988, we are passionate about bringing skydiving to the public and providing our personal attention to every skydiving experience.
Skydive Skylark began as Skydive Temple when a former Army Special Forces alum opened shop at the Temple Airport. As the years passed it was eventually moved to Salado and passed on to another famous skydiver Mark Polluck in the early 2000s. After many successful years as a skydiving center Mark also decided to retire and passed the legacy to Scott and Anthony Maschek who settled at Skylark Airfield and renamed to better fit the location. We have maintained a industry leading safety record and a commitment to providing amazing skydiving experiences to each and every customer.
Our Mission
Our mission is to elevate your experience to the highest standard. We know for many of our customers this will be the only time they experience our passion, and will put our best foot out the door every time. Our aim is to deliver you back to the landing area with a new and profound sense of living life to the fullest.
Our Team
Our team is made up of professional and dedicated tandem instructors, highly experienced commercial pilots and passionate and experienced support staff, who are all committed to your safety and happiness. We work together to deliver an amazing experience you will remember for the rest of your life.
Why Choose Us?
At Skydive Skylark, we offer the personal touch of a family owned and operated drop zone at the best possible price. Our customers choose us because we have a supportive staff, and incredible atmosphere, an untouchable safety record, and the experience you can trust.
Join Us
We invite you to join us on our journey. Whether you're knocking of bucket list items, facing your fears, celebrating a life event, or just want to experience something incredible. we are here to help. How do I book a tour?

What should I bring on the trip?
We suggest bringing sunscreen, a hat, swimwear, a towel, and your camera. Snorkeling gear and life jackets are provided by us.
Are the tours family-friendly?
Yes! Our tours are perfect for families. We welcome children of all ages and provide safety equipment for everyone on board.
Do I need prior experience for snorkeling or diving?
Not at all. Our crew provides instructions, and beginners are always welcome. Experienced divers can also enjoy deeper adventures with our guides.
What happens if the weather is bad?
Your safety is our priority. If conditions are unsafe, we’ll reschedule your tour or offer a full refund.
Can we bring food and drinks on board?
Yes, you can. Some of our packages even include refreshments. For private tours, we can also arrange catering upon request.

If you are wondering how to book a Chicago boat rental, the process is easier than it may look: decide what kind of moment you want, choose a vessel that fits your group, and reserve early enough to get the date and experience you have in mind.
Chicago boating is not one-size-fits-all. A romantic cruise for two calls for a different pace than a bachelorette party, family outing, or client event. A little planning helps turn a good day on the water into the one everyone keeps talking about.
Start With the Experience You Want
Before comparing boats or picking a time, get clear on the purpose of your charter. That decision shapes almost everything else, from your ideal route and rental length to the size of vessel you need.
For couples, a sunset cruise creates a polished, relaxed setting with the city lights coming on around you. Friend groups may want a daytime lake outing with room to socialize, swim, and enjoy the energy around the Playpen. Families often prefer scenic cruising with a comfortable schedule, while corporate groups may want a private setting that feels more memorable than another restaurant reservation.
Also think about the atmosphere. Do you want a calm Chicago River view, open-water Lake Michigan scenery, a fireworks cruise near Navy Pier, or a mix of iconic architecture and lakefront views? There is no wrong answer, but knowing your priorities makes booking much faster.
Choose the Right Date and Time
The best charter time depends on what you want from the day. Midday outings are great for sunshine, swimming, and lively group plans. Late afternoon and sunset cruises bring softer light, cooler temperatures, and picture-perfect views of the skyline. Evening cruises can feel especially special for date nights, celebrations, and fireworks viewing.
Weekends in peak boating season tend to book first, particularly for holiday weekends, summer Saturdays, fireworks nights, and popular celebration dates. If your group has a specific occasion in mind, reserve as soon as you have a few key details confirmed. Flexibility can help, too. A weekday cruise or a slightly earlier departure may offer more options while still delivering an incredible experience.
Weather is part of any on-water plan, but it should not stop you from planning ahead. Your charter provider can explain its weather policies, including what happens if conditions are not safe for boating. Ask about this before booking so everyone in your group knows what to expect.
Pick a Boat That Fits Your Group
A private rental should feel spacious and easy, not like everyone is squeezing in for a photo. Start with your headcount, then leave room for the way your group wants to spend the time. A quiet cruise may work well with a more intimate setup, while a birthday party or bachelor or bachelorette group benefits from extra room to move, lounge, and celebrate.
When looking at vessel options, pay attention to the details that affect your experience. Seating, shaded areas, onboard sound, restrooms, swim access, and space for food or drinks can all matter depending on the occasion. The best choice is not always the largest boat. It is the one that matches your guest count, vibe, and plans for the day.
If you are coordinating for a group, get a realistic count before reserving. A few last-minute additions can change what feels comfortable. It is also smart to ask about the maximum guest capacity and whether children count toward that number.
Decide How Long You Need
Hourly rentals give you flexibility, but the ideal length depends on your route and agenda. A shorter cruise works nicely for a date, an architectural sightseeing experience, or a quick celebration before dinner. If you want time to cruise, anchor, enjoy the water, take photos, and relax without watching the clock, a longer charter is usually the better fit.
Consider the full rhythm of your outing. Groups often need a little time to board, settle in, get photos, and enjoy the first drink before the day really gets going. If swimming, Playpen time, or multiple areas of the city are on your wish list, build in enough time to enjoy them properly.
Confirm What Is Included Before You Reserve
A premium boating experience should feel straightforward, but clear expectations make it even better. Review the rental details carefully before you book, including the vessel, rental duration, departure location, taxes or fees, and any security deposit or gratuity policies that apply.
You will also want to confirm whether a licensed captain and crew are included, what amenities are available onboard, and what you can bring with you. Policies for food, beverages, decorations, coolers, music, and swim gear can vary by boat and charter type. Asking upfront keeps your group from arriving with items that cannot be accommodated.
For special occasions, mention your plans early. A proposal, birthday, anniversary, corporate gathering, or bachelorette outing may call for extra coordination around timing, décor, photos, or a preferred route. The more the team knows about your vision, the better they can help shape the experience around it.
How to Book a Chicago Boat Rental Without the Stress
Once you know your date, group size, and preferred experience, booking is a simple next step. Select the boat and time that work for your plans, provide your contact and payment information, and review the confirmation details before finalizing. Direct online booking is ideal when your plans are set and you want to secure your charter quickly.
If you are deciding between boats or organizing a larger event, reaching out before you reserve can be worthwhile. A quick conversation can clarify capacity, available time slots, route possibilities, and the best rental length for your occasion. DorSea Tours can help match your group with an on-water experience that feels personal, elevated, and easy to enjoy.
After booking, share the essentials with your guests early: departure time, meeting location, what to wear, and what they should bring. Arriving on time matters because charter time is valuable, especially when you have a sunset window, fireworks schedule, or dinner reservation afterward.
Plan for Comfort, Not Just Photos
Chicago’s lakefront can feel warmer or cooler than the city streets, so advise guests to dress for the water. Layers are a smart choice for evening cruises, while sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat can make a bright afternoon far more comfortable. Soft-soled shoes are often the easiest option onboard.
Keep the guest list manageable and choose one person to handle day-of questions. For larger celebrations, that organizer can coordinate arrival times, collect any shared costs, and make sure everyone knows the plan. Small details like these protect the relaxed, carefree feeling you booked the boat for in the first place.
If your group plans to bring food or drinks, think practical. Choose items that travel well, are easy to serve, and do not create a major cleanup project. A boat day should feel festive, not like a catering operation.
Make Your Charter Feel Like Your Occasion
Private boating stands out because it gives you room to make the day your own. A couple may bring a favorite playlist and champagne for a quiet sunset. A birthday group can coordinate a theme, snacks, and plenty of photo time with the skyline. A corporate host can use the outing to create real conversation away from meeting rooms and crowded venues.
The key is to avoid overplanning every minute. Pick one or two highlights you care about most – swimming, sunset photos, fireworks, a toast, or a skyline route – then let the rest of the charter unfold.
