TITLE: FAQ - Ash Scatter - CAPTAIN BRUCE Hawaii
How should I bring the remains onto the boat?
In Hawaii, there are no strict regulations regarding the container for the remains. While some choose to bring them in a traditional urn, others prefer them already processed. At Captain Bruce, we highly recommend having the remains cremated into a fine powder (ashed) and placed in a water-soluble bag or a biodegradable urn for a smooth and respectful ceremony.
How do I transport the remains to Hawaii?
To prevent loss or damage, we recommend carrying the remains in your carry-on luggage rather than checked bags. Please be aware that customs or airline staff may request documentation. We mend preparing a “Cremation Certificate” or “Certificate of Pulverization” prior to your departure.
recom
Is there a dress code?
There is no need for formal attire. Please feel free to wear . Our goal is to provide a warm, comfortable environment where you can share fond memories of your loved one.
Can I bring beverages for a toast or flowers for the offering?
Yes, you are welcome to bring beverages for a memorial toast and flowers for the tribute. However, we kindly ask for your cooperation with the following:
If you bring a Lei, please remove the string and scatter only the loose petals into the ocean to protect the marine environment and sea life.
We can also prepare flower baskets for you. Please let us know in advance if you would like to arrange this.
Can we scatter the remains at a specific location?
While we primarily operate in designated areas such as Kaneohe Bay or off the coast of Waikiki, we can adjust the location within the boundaries of Hawaii State Law.
We also offer an optional “Certificate of Scattering,” which records the exact latitude and longitude of the site. If you would like this certificate, please select it from the additional options in the reservation form. It allows you to revisit the same location in the future to pay your respects.

What should I wear?
Your clothing for skydiving in Northern Virginia should be comfortable and loose-fitting. Athletic wear or activewear items like track suit, yoga pants, or t-shirts are our first choices for what to wear skydiving when the weather is nice. Jeans are not the most comfortable.
How old do you have to be to go skydiving?
The United States Parachuting Association mandates that all tandem students must be 18 years old in order to participate in a parachute jump. No exceptions! Please bring a valid government-issued photo ID as proof of your date of birth.
Not old enough to skydive? Or just not ready to jump? You can still take to the skies with our aviation brand, Front Royal Aviation. Try a discovery flight and see what it’s like to fly the plane yourself! Click the link at the bottom of this screen to learn more.
What height will I jump from?
We will jump up to 2 miles high.
What’s the weight limit?
Tandem students must be 220 lbs or less in order to make a skydive. Your height to weight proportions are also important in making sure the tandem harness fits properly for your jump. An additional fee may be applied for guests over 200 lbs. Each guest is subject to being weighed, fully clothed and with shoes on, at our facility prior to the skydive. Above all else, safety first.
Am I allowed to take my phone or GoPro with me during the jump?
The USPA requires a minimum of before a skydiver can carry a camera in freefall, and since our dropzone follows their safety guidelines, we strictly adhere to this rule.

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.
- Prices: copy the number. "from $85" means amount 85. A range means the low end, with the range in detail.
- Be terse. Values are short phrases or one sentence. No marketing copy. description is at most 3 plain sentences.
- Limits: at most 12 offerings, and at most 6 items in each list. Prefer the facts a guest needs to decide and to show up: price, duration, age, weight, licence, deposit, cancellation, weather, what is included, what to bring.

How do I book a tour?
You can book online anytime or call 1-800-622-3011 (US) / 808-833-3000. Our Reservations Team is available Monday–Friday from 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM HST and weekends from 7:00 AM to 4:30 PM HST. We are closed on Christmas Day and close early at 1:00 PM on New Year’s Eve and Thanksgiving Day. When our office is closed, you can still book online. For assistance, email .
What types of tours do you offer?
We offer land tours, one-day interisland tours, and helicopter tours across Oʻahu, Maui, Kauaʻi, and the Big Island. A valid photo ID is required for interisland flights.
Where do you pick up passengers for tours?
We provide pickup from designated locations on Oahu in Waikīkī, Maui, Kauaʻi, and Hilo. If your hotel is not listed, we will assign the nearest available pickup location. Pickup times and locations vary by tour—please check your confirmation details. Call 808-833-3000 at least 24 hours in advance to confirm your pickup location and time.
Can I meet my Pearl Harbor tour at the memorial instead of taking group transportation?
No, all guests must take the provided group transportation. Per National Park Service regulations, guests cannot join the tour at Pearl Harbor, and late arrivals will not be accommodated.
What is your cancellation policy?
Land tours can be canceled up to 48 hours before pickup for a full refund (Haleakalā Sunrise requires 72 hours’ notice). One Day and Helicopter Tours require at least 7 days’ notice due to airline and transportation policies.
Cancellations for medical emergencies or airline flight disruptions may qualify for an exception with written proof, such as a doctor’s note or an official airline cancellation notice. Refunds for weather-related disruptions or other unforeseen circumstances are not guaranteed.
If you booked through a travel agency or third-party website, you must contact them directly for cancellations or refunds.
Do tours operate on holidays?
Some locations we visit are closed on Christmas Day, Thanksgiving, and New Year’s Day. Please check our website to check tour availability on these dates.
Can I be dropped off at a different location after my tour?
You may get dropped off at a different hotel, however, we cannot accommodate luggage or provide airport transfers.
Are there any age, weight, or physical restrictions for certain tours?
Yes, some tours have specific requirements:
: This tour includes a visit to the Ford Island Control Tower at Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum. Children must be at least 42” tall; infants and toddlers are not permitted. : No bags are allowed; only small wallets or clutches measuring 1.5″ x 2.25″ x 5.5″ or smaller are permitted.

: Passengers over 240 pounds may be required to purchase an additional seat due to FAA regulations.
Do you offer special meal accommodations?
Yes. Gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian meal options are available upon request where meals are included. Dietary restrictions must be noted at the time of booking.
Will I see lava on the Volcano Adventure Tour?
Lava activity is unpredictable and changes daily. We do not guarantee lava sightings.
What languages are available for tours?
Tours are conducted in English. Haleakalā Sunrise Tours feature iPads with GPS-triggered narration in multiple languages, which must be requested at the time of booking.

Uncover The Rich History of Pearl Harbor: Arizona Memorial, Battleship Missouri, Aviation Museum & Bowfin Submarine.
Embark on an unforgettable journey through the pivotal moments of World War II with our comprehensive tour of Pearl Harbor. Immerse yourself in the stories of heroism and sacrifice as you visit iconic landmarks, including the USS Arizona Memorial, Battleship Missouri, Bowfin Submarine, Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, and more! Lunch is included at the Aviation Museum’s Hangar Cafe.
USS Arizona Memorial Pay tribute to the brave souls who made the ultimate sacrifice at the USS Arizona Memorial. Positioned directly above the sunken battleship, this solemn site serves as the final resting place for many of the 1,177 officers and crewmen lost during the infamous attack on December 7, 1941.
USS Missouri Battleship Walk in the historic footsteps of General Douglas MacArthur and Admiral Chester Nimitz aboard the USS Missouri Battleship. This mighty vessel, known as “Mighty Mo,” played a crucial role in WWII, the Korean War, and Desert Storm. Explore the decks where the instruments of surrender were signed, marking the end of World War II.
USS Bowfin Submarine, Step into history as you tour the USS Bowfin Submarine, aptly named the “Pearl Harbor Avenger.” Delve into the epic battles of the Pacific as you navigate through this remarkable vessel, which played a pivotal role in the war.
Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, Witness history come to life at the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum, housed in two WWII hangars that still bear scars from the December 7, 1941 attack. Spanning 105,000 square feet, the museum showcases a captivating collection of wartime aircraft, including an authentic Japanese Zero used in the attack.
Pearl Harbor Visitor Center Dive into history at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center’s galleries, featuring artifacts, impactful photos, and evidence of the 1941 surprise attack. Enrich your visit with a self-guided audio tour and the Pearl Harbor Virtual Experience, providing a unique and immersive perspective on the events of World War II.
Lunch included at Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum’s Hangar Café. Options are available for all dietary needs.

*Swimming at Waimea Falls may not be available if the waterfall-fed pool is dry, due to reduced seasonal rainfall. The valley remains a highlight of the tour with its beautiful botanical gardens and cultural sites.
Exclusive Kahala Avenue is known as “Hawai’i’s Beverly Hills”, and you’ll view the stunning multi-million-dollar properties in this affluent community while we travel toward the South Shore sea cliffs area.
Halona Blowhole acts like an ocean-driver geyser as the ocean breezes push waves into the cave below and a hole in the rock formation shoots sea spray jets high into the air. Accessibility to the overlook is dependent upon parking congestion situation at this popular stop.
Nu’uanu Pali Lookout is the location of the 1795 battle in which King Kamehameha I victoriously united Oahu under his rule. The epic battle claimed the lives of hundreds of warriors forced over the Pali’s sheer cliffs. At 1,200 feet above the green and blue views of Windward Oahu, the Pali Lookout is one of Oahu’s most breathtaking scenic points.
Byodo-In Temple is a stunning replica of a temple in Uji, Japan, Byodo-In. It is nestled in the Valley of the Temples on the slopes of the Ko’olau Mountain Range. Byodo-In commemorates the first Japanese immigrants in Hawai’i and was constructed entirely without nails. Its beautiful peacocks and hundreds of Japanese Koi contribute to one of the most peaceful and picturesque locations on the island.
Waimea Valley, is an area steeped in historic, cultural and spiritual significance. Located on the North Shore of Oahu it is a place you won’t soon forget. Soak in the magic of the valley and be in the quiet of nature surrounded by beautiful flowers, rare plants, cultural sites, and a delightful waterfall for swimming (weather-permitting).
Mokoli’i or “little lizard” in Hawaiian, an islet sits offshore in Kaneohe Bay. Mokoli’i will be viewed near Kualoa as your tour vehicle winds its way along the scenic coastline.
North Shore Surfing Breaks, including world famous Sunset, Waimea Bay, and others, are viewed from your tour vehicle as it crosses the island’s big wave territory. The region is known for its fabulously large wintertime waves and international surfing competitions.
Historic Haleiwa Town, with its preserved old plantation character and surf town image, makes its shops and restaurants popular among visitors and Oahu residents. It’s the gateway to the North Shore for those arriving from Honolulu and is the area’s largest commercial center.
Dole Plantation is “Hawai’i’s Complete Pineapple Experience.” Learn, see, and taste the fruit that is part of the island’s heritage and enjoyed throughout the world. Walk through Dole’s country store where delicious ice-cold Dole Whip treats are available. The quintessential brief and final stop before heading back to Waikiki.

Why Guests Keep Coming Back to Salty Bottom Boats
Captain Chad Harris didn’t set out to start a boat charter company. He came to Key West from Rochester, New York to help a friend move some stuff, the airline lost his return ticket, and he never looked back. Twelve years operating water tours, jet ski rentals, and charters across these waters earned him both a 100 Ton and 200 Ton Masters License and a deep understanding of what makes a day on the water unforgettable.

Why Do We Recommend Our Early Morning Tours?
The manatees are more active early in the morning and there are fewer boats on the water, so you have the best chance of a more interactive experience on our morning tours.
How Long Will the Trip Be?
Our manatee trips are 3 hours long but in water time varies from thirty minutes up to 2 hours, depending on the number of manatees and temperature.
What is the Age Limit on Your Tours?
We will take children age 3 and up on our tour, but we can accommodate all ages if you book a private tour.
Do You Have to Be a Strong Swimmer to Go on a Tour?
You do not have to be a strong swimmer since the wetsuit will keep you buoyant; we also have swim noodles and snorkel vests if needed.
Can I Bring My Own Gear?
You are welcome to bring your own equipment. We maintain dive quality gear for your use if you don’t have your own. We can supply everything you need!

The climb typically involves a 3 week expedition, requiring climbers to navigate through glaciers, crevasses, and steep ice and rock sections.
The West Buttress route is the most popular, offering a gradual ascent, but climbers must be prepared for extreme cold, high altitudes, and potential hazards.

It’s crucial to be well-equipped with appropriate gear, such as insulated clothing, mountaineering boots, and specialized equipment for glacier travel. Many climbers hire experienced guides or join guided expeditions to enhance safety and increase the chances of a successful summit.
In summary, while Denali’s climb is undoubtedly difficult, it offers a unique and awe-inspiring adventure for those with the necessary skills, experience, and determination.

Reviews
Private Sailing Charters on Hilton Head Island, SC
Whatever experience you choose, Anchors Away Sailing Charter's mission is to be one of the most memorable parts of your visit to Hilton Head Island. We are focused on giving your group a fresh perspective of this beautiful area through the wonderful world of .
What we Offer
private sailing charters
Join us for a beautiful morning sail to begin your perfect vacation day. See tons of wildlife and get close to some dolphins along the way.
Experience a generally breezy and exciting afternoon sail. Feel free to jump into the action and help handle lines, hoist sails, and steer the boat. It is pretty rare that we go out and do not see any dolphins, so, keep a look out as you never know what we will see out there.
Come and celebrate the end of a memorable day with our . Typically, great sailing is followed by a relaxing sail back in towards the end of the evening. Often surrounded by wildlife and majestic Hilton Head sunsets. This is a great photo opportunity and a wonderful way to immerse yourself in the beauty this area has to offer.
Sunset Sail
Want a longer experience on the water, no problem. Join us for a half day or a full day away from the dock. These trips are customizable to cater to the experience you desire. Stop and anchor for lunch and a swim, do some ocean sailing or visit a destination. Give us a call to set this trip up.
sailing tours
What Sets Us Apart
As evidenced by hundreds of five-star reviews from our satisfied guests, Anchors Away Sailing Charters distinguishes itself from the competition by providing unparalleled service from the first point of contact until we bid you farewell at the conclusion of your sailing excursion.
Our Reputation
We are not a "head boat" operation that packs tons of passengers that you don't know on the boat. The only other individuals besides your family and friends aboard your yacht will be the uniformed Captain and crew member who are committed to personalizing your experience and ensuring you are well cared for.
Our Service
Anchors Away Sailing Charters operates a fleet of the newest, best maintained and most luxurious monohull vessels on Hilton Head Island and the surrounding areas. The pride we take in our sailing yachts will be evident the moment you step aboard. In addition to all of the required safety equipment, our vessels are equipped with comfortable cockpit cushions, large "bimini tops" for shade, spotless restrooms, and many other amenities to maximize your comfort.
Our Yachts
What To Expect
Prior to your scheduled departure, you will be greeted by one of our friendly uniformed crewmembers, who will escort you to your vessel and assist you in boarding. You will be given a short safety briefing as you get comfortably seated aboard, after which the Captain and First Mate will slip the dock lines and your excursion will begin. While motoring out of the harbor, guests may choose to sit in comfortable deck chairs on the bow of the boat. Be sure to watch for dolphins! When safely in open water, the crew will raise and trim the sails. The boat may begin to "heel" (lean slightly to one side) as the sails begin to do their work. This is expected and completely safe.
And finally, the engine is switched off as the boat continues silently making way on sail power alone. You are sailing! Guests are welcome to assist with the sailing as much or as little as they like. The crew will give commentary, take photos, serve drinks, answer questions and do our best to keep you engaged and entertained…or fade into the background to the extent you prefer. Sit back, relax, and enjoy the beauty and serenity of Hilton Head Island on your own terms. Near the conclusion of your trip the crew will lower the sails, restart the engine, and make docking preparations. After the boat is safely secured in its slip, the crew will offer to take a picture of your group sitting on the boat, then, will help you to disembark and sincerely thank you for allowing Anchors Away Sailing Charters to help make your day special.
Weather Statement
It is our job to ensure your group is SAFE while onboard our vessels. It is also true that we never want to disappoint a group who has been looking forward to their sailing experience. A decision to cancel a charter due to adverse weather is never made lightly but is SOLELY up to the professional discretion of our very experienced Captains. We monitor the weather constantly with several advanced weather forecasting and radar products. If we determine there is a risk of unfavorable weather, we may delay the departure time, reschedule the trip if possible, or cancel the trip if absolutely necessary. In the event that we must cancel a charter, we will issue a full refund if we cannot reschedule.
If you do not hear from us prior to your trip, we are planning to operate and you should plan to be at the marina 15 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time. There is no need to contact us. If we need to contact you regarding a possible interruption, we will contact you at the telephone number provided on the reservation with as much advance notice as possible. However, final decisions regarding weather are often made just prior to departure time. Your safety and comfort are our highest priorities and you can trust us to make prudent decisions and communicate with you appropriately.

Unincorporated Towns & Communities
Boulder County’s unincorporated areas comprise the rural, mountainous and plains communities that are not a part of any incorporated municipality.
Unlike the which have a separately elected town board or city council, the unincorporated communities of Boulder County are governed by the ordinances and regulations adopted by the .
municipalities within Boulder County

Many distinct and unique communities exist within the unincorporated areas of Boulder County, among them:
Allenspark
Located northwest Boulder County, Allenspark was established in 1870 in the midst of the gold rush. Zip code: 80510 Population: 528
Coal Creek Canyon
Located partially in Southwest Boulder County, the Coal Creek Canyon community also resides in neighboring counties of Jefferson and Gilpin. Zip code: 80403 Population: Approx. 2,400 (not all in Boulder County) according to the 2010 Census tract for the Coal Creek Census Designated Place
Eldora
Eldora was established in 1896 as a gold mining camp and called Eldorado, which is Spanish for “the golden.” Eldora is located in southwest Boulder County within the Roosevelt National Forest and lends its name to Boulder County’s only local ski resort, Eldora Mountain Resort. Zip code: 80466 Population: 142
www.eldora.com
Eldorado Springs
Nestled in the valleys of the Flat Irons, Eldorado Springs was established in 1904 by a group of entrepreneurs who formed the Moffat Lakes Resort Company, creating the resort town of Eldorado Springs. Americans flocked to the springs in the early 20th Century for the rumored healing qualities of the water. Artesian water is still bottled and sold here. The nearby Eldorado Canyon State Park is famous for its rock climbing routes. Zip code: 80025 Population: 585
Gold Hill
Gold Hill is Colorado’s oldest continuously occupied mining town. It arose with the January 1859 gold discovery at Gold Run creek. Gold Hill is located about 10 miles to the northwest of Boulder, Colorado, perched on a mountainside above Left Hand Canyon at an elevation of 8,300 feet. Zip code: 80302 Population: 230
goldhilltown.com
Gunbarrel
Gunbarrel was established in the 1860s and named after Gunbarrel Road, the main stagecoach route between Boulder and Longmont. It is located northeast of Boulder and south of Longmont adjacent to Hwy 119 (along “the Diagonal.”) Zip codes: 80301, 80503 Population: 9,263
Hygiene
The community of Hygiene (Est. 1861) was named after an early tuberculosis sanatorium, Hygiene Home. Water for the sanatorium was piped from a spring on Rabbit Mountain and was claimed to have valuable medicinal properties. The community lies just west of the City of Longmont. Zip code: 80533 Population: Unknown
Niwot
The Town of Niwot (Est. 1872) was named for Chief Niwot, an Arapaho leader in the Front Range at the time of the gold rush. Niwot is located northeast of Boulder and south of Longmont adjacent to Hwy 119 (along “the Diagonal.”) Zip codes: 80503, 80544 Population: 4,160
www.niwot.com

TITLE: Boulder County Strategic Priorities - Boulder County
Boulder County Strategic Priorities
Board of County Commissioners 2024-2026 Strategic Priorities
2025 Progress Report
Boulder County is committed to meeting the needs of our community through clear goals and priorities.
The Board of County Commissioners sets strategic priorities every three years. These priorities guide our work, strengthen partnerships, and build public trust.
The Boulder County Commissioners’ Strategic Priorities provides an update on the progress we made in 2025 toward the 2024-2026 Strategic Priorities.
View the 2024 Strategic Priorities progress update
As Boulder County responds to key issues, our departments and offices continue to develop in-depth and complex strategies to address societal and environmental needs. Some of these strategies involve regional partnerships, collaborations with other community organizations, or integration of programs across multiple departments and offices in the county. Often these larger projects require the investment of the Board of County Commissioners’ (BOCC) time and resources alongside time from staff and resources from across the county organization. The three priority areas identified align with existing programs and projects within departments, work that has been developed using community input and feedback.
Strategic Priorities Report 2024-2026
Informe de Prioridades Estratégicas 2024-2026
2024-2026 BOCC Strategic Priorities:
Economic Security and Social Stability
Climate Action and Environmental Stewardship
Good Governance
Background
Setting and communicating the priorities of leadership within an organization is considered a best management practice. Identifying these priorities was intended to determine priorities that go above and beyond the statutory and core services and functions that we are proud to deliver in Boulder County. Going forward, the BOCC will use these priorities to provide clarity around the Board’s decision-making process in budgeting and other county management decisions.
Furthermore, we recognize that while the priorities identified are important, they will not – and are not intended to – cover the full breadth nor depth of services that the county provides and will continue to provide.

TITLE: Ron Stewart Preserve at Rabbit Mountain - Boulder County
Ron Stewart Preserve at Rabbit Mountain sits at the easternmost point of the foothills in Boulder County. The preserve is rich in human history, geology, and plant and animal life.
2.5 miles –
2.2 miles –

Live view of the parking lot
Elk & Vegetation Management Plan
Along Colorado’s Front Range, the grasslands of the Great Plains rise to meet the peaks of the southern Rocky Mountains. The foothills form where they meet. This transition zone reflects change in both land and life. The preserve covers 2,871 acres. Its grasslands, shrublands, and forests provide habitat for many kinds of wildlife.
Elk Management
Limited hunting was allowed at the preserve for eight years. The program met its goals, and hunting is not needed in the foreseeable future. Learn more about the .

About 140 million years ago, this area was a tropical lowland covered by rivers, swamps, and lagoons. An inland sea covered much of Colorado for millions of years.
The sea retreated around 65 million years ago, when forces deep within the earth began to lift the Rocky Mountains. These forces strained the rocks in the area and caused them to break. Movement along a break like this is called a fault. A major fault crosses the north end of the property. Slippage along area faults moved the preserve three miles east of the main hogbacks of the foothills. Because of this location, you can see Rabbit Mountain from three counties.
Native Peoples
Rabbit Mountain was an ideal winter home for the Arapaho people. It offered shelter from strong west winds, edible plants, water from natural springs, and plentiful game. Chief Niwot of the Arapaho may have spent time in the area.
In the mid-1800s, homesteaders claimed land in the area, hoping to find gold. Few found it, and many turned to farming instead. Their arrival displaced the Arapaho and other Native American peoples from Rabbit Mountain and across the state.
Western Water
In 1959, the St. Vrain Supply Canal across Rabbit Mountain was built as part of the Colorado-Big Thompson Project. The project still operates today. It carries water through the mountains from the wetter western slope to the drier Front Range.
Acquisition
Jack Moomaw, a forest ranger, wanted to preserve wild areas, including Rabbit Mountain. His granddaughter sold Rabbit Mountain to Boulder County in 1984. Because of this purchase, Rabbit Mountain will stay in its natural state for generations to enjoy.

TITLE: Lagerman Agricultural Preserve - Boulder County
Lagerman Agricultural Preserve
Lagerman Agricultural Preserve is a place enjoyed by birders, boaters, picnickers, bikers, runners, and dog-walkers. Lagerman Reservoir has something for the entire family. There is a picnic site, wetlands, and a seasonal osprey nest.
1.6 miles – The western section is closed to protect nesting wildlife
4.9 miles –
24 car parking spots
Restroom
25 person group shelter
6 horse trailer parking spots
The western end of the reservoir is closed annually April 1 through Aug. 31 to protect wildlife.
Swimming and wading are prohibited.
Fishing is not recommended due to poor oxygen levels in the reservoir.
Trailhead Construction
The trailhead construction project was completed on Dec. 18, 2025. Improvements include:
Redesigned parking lot with directional traffic flow.
Increased turning space for trailers.
Additional horse trailer parking spot for a total of six spaces.
Two van accessible, concrete, ADA parking spaces.
An ADA-compliant concrete walkway between the restroom and the picnic shelter.
Boating Regulations
What’s Allowed
Boats, canoes, kayaks, stand up paddle boards (SUP), and inflatables where you sit out of the water are allowed.
Sailboards and sailboats are prohibited.
Personal Flotation Devices (PFD)
A USCG approved Type I, II, or III PFD is required for each person on board.
PFDs should be readily accessible.
Boats 16 feet in length or longer require one additional Type IV PDF which should be readily accessible.
Children 12 years old or younger are required to wear a PFD.
All PFDs should be appropriately sized and in good condition.
Motorized Boats
Motorized boats require a current registration on board.
Fire extinguisher is required on board for permanently installed fuel tanks.
Motorized boats with electric or gasoline powered motors of 8 horsepower or less are allowed.
Any motorized boat with a motor larger than 8 horsepower shall have that motor’s propeller lifted out of the water at all times.
No-wake speed only.
The reservoir is not stocked with fish due to poor oxygen levels. Staff are investigating ways to improve water quality and restore fishing to Lagerman Reservoir.
Please fish at another property. .
Wetland habitats, nestled within the surrounding Great Plains, support aquatic plant and animal life and serve to lure in large numbers of migrating bird species. With grasses, wildflowers and trees surrounding the wetlands, these areas are biologically diverse both in and out of the water.

Swedish Heritage
Reverend Frederick Lagerman was pastor of the 1878 “Swedish Evangelical Congregation of Ryssby, Boulder County, Colorado” Lutheran Church. The church congregation purchased 160 acres of land near the current reservoir as a prastgard, or pastor’s garden. As was Swedish custom, church members farmed the land, giving the bounty to the pastor as his salary. The irrigation reservoir for the prastgard was listed on state records as Lagerman Reservoir.

TITLE: Cancellation And Weather Policy - Jersey Pirate Adventures
Our Weather & Cancellation Policies
Weather Policy
PLEASE KNOW THIS IS A RAIN OR SHINE EVENT! However, we do not sail in Thunderstorms. All decisions are made the day of the cruise as accurately as possible. This is the hardest part of our job, thank you for understanding. Please Do Not call about weather. We will call you if there are any issues. If you do not hear from us the trip is on as scheduled.
We sail in rain but we do not sail if the conditions are determined to be unsafe by the Captain (thunder, lightening, heavy downpours or damaging winds). All weather related decisions are determined by the Captain. Please keep in mind that a 30% chance of rain means there is a 70% chance of treasure.. Please review our cancellation policy. If it is raining where you are driving from it doesn’t mean that it is raining at our location. We do our absolute best that we can with all weather situations but sometimes weather can be unpredictable. We are always close to our docking area and safety is our top concern. Trips can be altered or changed if the captain determines it is necessary. Please know that Weather Channels and weather apps are frequently inaccurate and we do not pay attention to any long range forecasts but rather watch radars the day of only. Please do not call about the weather, we will call you approximately 1 hour prior to your scheduled arrival to notify you if we are not sailing we. We have up to 7 trips daily so calling at 10:00 am about a 6:30 cruise does not make sense.
Cancellation Policy
All reservations will be held to our cancellation policy without exception.
We reserve the right to cancel or modify any sail in the event of heavy rain, thunderstorms, high winds, or conditions deemed unsafe by the captain. We do sail in the rain. In the unfortunate event that we must cancel a voyage we will call approximately 1 hour prior to your scheduled arrival to notify you of the cancellation. If we cancel your trip for any reason you will not be charged.
Note: Tickets are required for every person on board from the smallest infant to all grown-ups who wish to join us. Please include all children, adults, and infants when booking your Adventure. This is a Coast Guard Regulation (law) and no exceptions can or will be made for safety reasons. Jersey Shore Pirates reserves the right to refuse entry to any passenger(s) for any reason. Safety is our top priority.

=== PAGE: https://jerseyshorepirates.com/faqs/
TITLE: FAQ - Jersey Pirate Adventures
Frequently Asked Questions
Why are there different prices for certain trips?
We offer a discount for early bookings so if you see a lower price for a certain trip you are one of the earlier reservations for that particular sailing. The early pirate gets the treasure.
How can I cancel my reservation?
For all reservations made online and for reservations that did not require a deposit, simply go to your confirmation e-mail and click the link that allows you to cancel the reservation. Please know that these reservations have a 72 hour cancellation policy as agreed to when booking. The cancellation link will disappear once you are inside the cancellation period and at this point you are responsible for the tickets.
Can I use my ticket for another time if I miss my sailing?
Unfortunately all tickets are non-transferable within the agreed cancellation period. You are responsible for all tickets within the cancellation window. These are tickets for a specific date and time. We have a very limited season and a limited capacity. If Jersey Shore Pirates has to cancel for any reason, then you will be either refunded or can move to another time if you prefer. We understand that situations arise which is why we allow the cancellations up until 72 hours.
What do you do if it rains?
We sail in rain but we do not sail if the conditions are determined to be unsafe by the Captain (thunder, lightening, heavy downpours or damaging winds). All weather related decisions are determined by the Captain. Please keep in mind that a 30% chance of rain means there is a 70% chance of treasure. Please review our cancellation policy. If it is raining where you are driving from it doesn’t mean that it is raining at our location. We do our absolute best that we can with all weather situations but sometimes weather can be unpredictable. We are always close to our docking area and safety is our top concern. Trips can be altered or changed if the captain determines it is necessary. Please know that Weather Channels and weather apps are frequently and intentionally inaccurate and we do not pay attention to any long range forecasts but rather watch radars the day of only. Please do not call about the weather, if you do not like the forecast, we encourage you to contact the person who made the forecast you follow. If we are not sailing we will call you. We have up to 7 trips daily so calling at 10:00 am about a 6:30 cruise does not make sense.
What if it's hot?
Yes, this is a seasonal business with a good portion taking place during the summer, the ship still sails when its hot. Bring water and dress accordingly.
What if it's cold?
Yes, we will be sailing. Feel free to bring a jacket and dress accordingly.
We are driving from far away, what do we do if our trip gets cancelled while we are on our way?
In the event of unexpected weather that can not be tracked on the radar (i.e. pop-up thunderstorms) cancels the trip, we recommend checking out The Gravity Vault in Brick, NJ or Jenkinsons Aquarium in Point Pleasant.
Can I bring a stroller on board?
Yes a stroller can be brought onboard. We recommend a smaller stroller with a cover or umbrella as it limits your movement on the ship and can not fit under the covered area.
Do I need a ticket for a baby?
Yes. The way the Coast Guard counts passengers, every single person onboard counts toward our limited capacity.
Something happened and we can't make the trip, can we use the tickets for another day or time?
Unfortunately no. We have a minimum of a 72 hour cancellation policy. We know unexpected things pop up but the tickets are for the time and day that you purchased them for much like for a flight or a sporting event. Please see the reservation/cancellation policy for more specific details. If you arrive at the dock with less members in your crew, we have no way to sell unused tickets at the dock.
Where do we park?
There is free parking inside our marina for your crew. You MUST Drive slowly inside the marina as other businesses and ours are operating with people present.
Do you take reservations for smaller families or do we need to be with a larger group?
Families of all sizes are welcome! You do not need to be part of a larger group to enjoy a trip on the Sea Gypsy II. Our trips are fun for families of two or families of twenty. All will take part in the adventure.
How do I make a reservation?
Book online for your crew on the home page or under reservations tab. The online option has an accurate availability and schedule. If you are looking for a Private Charter please call us at 732-899-6100 to make your reservations. Please know while we are very active on our Social Media Pages and e-mail throughout the day we can not constantly monitor it so please know the only way to make or talk about your reservation is over our phone lines.
Is there a bathroom on board the ship?
No, there is no true head onboard The Sea Gypsy II. We have an emergency potty onboard if a child really needs to go but we do have bathrooms at our check-in area for when you arrive and return.
Do I need to make a reservation?

=== PAGE: https://milwaukeepedalandpaddletavern.com/pedal/faqs/
TITLE: Party Bike FAQs | Tour Downtown | Milwaukee Pedal Tavern
Where do we board the Pedal Tavern?
All tours start and end at the Cooperage Building 820 S. Water St. (South Water and National).
You sure can, Bring Your Own Beer!! We have coolers or bring your own, each rider is allowed to bring up to 3 cans of beer. Cans must be 12 oz. or smaller.
21+, this is a pub crawl tour.
How does the pub crawl route work?
We have drink specials set up at 25+ bars in the 3rd Ward / Walker’s Point. We send you the list when you make the reservation, you pick the route. Groups typically make 3-4 stops on their tour!
How do we know if the Pedal Tavern is available when we want it?
Can we split the bill?
Check out eventpally.com, an excellent way to split the bill before you come. We recommend charging a few extra bucks per person so you can pool money for beer and snacks… the cooler fund if you will.
How many people can fit on the Pedal Tavern?
It can hold up to 16 people, there are 10 seats with pedals, 2 seats above the back wheels, and 3 bench seats on the back row, and one person can man the middle as the bartender and fetch the group drinks and snacks.
Who drives this thing?
We have an employee of ours drive and steer the unit – your group can relax and have fun.
Can I rent multiple bikes, and will we all go together?
Yes and yes! Please call us at to schedule multiple bikes (don’t schedule online)!
414-250-0339
Can we eat food on the Pedal Tavern?
Yes, you can! In fact, some groups even use the Pedal Tavern to do Progressive dinners. There are many great restaurants in the 3rd Ward and Walkers Point.
What's the music situation?
We have a sound system on each bike and can play your CDs, iPhones/iPods, and other music players!
Unless it’s really pouring, we will ride. It’s actually really fun when it rains, groups have a blast! Plus, there is a roof so you will stay pretty dry.
If you cancel 14+ days prior we will give you a refund. If you cancel 5-13 days, we will give you a rain check to use later in the season, or next season if it’s at the end of the season. Cancellations within 4 days of the tour will not receive any type of a refund.
10:00 AM to 10:30 PM. Yes, bars are open that early on the route. We can even start earlier upon request!
How fast does this bad boy go?
It goes about 5 miles an hour.
Are there height requirements to ride?
To reach the pedal, you need to be around 5’3″ or taller. If you are shorter, it’s not a big deal, take a bench seat, or bartend for the group!
Book online or call us at to book a tour. We accept cash, checks, debit, or credit cards. You must pay at the time of reservation. We can split the payment on multiple cards.
You can get it going with 2 or 3 pedalers, but it’s a workout. Ideally, you want at least 6 people.
Where did this thing come from?
Pedal Tavern is an import from Europe. It’s very popular in Amsterdam and Germany. Minneapolis was the first US city to have one. We rode it up there and realized that Milwaukee would love something like this!
Danza san lorenzello – l.c.a. Fitness association… the charlottetown fitness club

TITLE: Pedal Boat FAQs | Milwaukee River | Milwaukee Pedal Tavern
How many people can fit on the boat?
We can fit up to 16 people on the Paddle Tavern boats, 12 people on the Duffy boats, and 26 people on the Nauti Tiki Tavern boats. Need more? We have 3 Paddle Taverns, 2 Duffy Boats, and 1 Nauti Tiki Tavern. Call us to book two or more boats, . Need even more room? (414)
436-2709
Is Pedaling difficult on the boat?
No, it’s pretty easy, if you have done our bar bike tours before, you know that small hills can be a bit of a workout, the boats are considerably easier. The river is flat, and we have a 20 HSP motor assisting, bring Grandma along for the ride.
Alcohol / Food / Cooler / Music Situation.
Bring Your Own Bevs! We have 4 built-in bar coolers with ice to cool your drinks down. We recommend cans over glass.
Food is welcome too, the general rule of food is what can you eat one-handed without a napkin or utensil (pretzels, sandwiches = awesome; birthday cake = horribly messy). Plug your phone into our sound system, a good playlist goes a long way.
Where do we launch? How long are the tours?
Paddle Tavern trips are 1 hour and 45 minutes long. We start and end the trips from the docks behind the Harp, 113 E Juneau Ave.
Duffy Rentals launch from the Cooperage Building (new home of Boone and Crockett) @ 820 S Water St. and are 2 hours long.
We do allow for customization for the length of the tour, and custom drop off on non-peak days.
Do you provide the driver? Can we tip them?
Paddle Taverns are staffed with a licensed captain and even a first mate, you guys relax and have fun, we will take care of all the “boat stuff”. And yes they love tips.
Duffy Boats can be self-drive rentals, or you can hire a third party . Price is $40 per hour.
captain service here
How does the trip work? Do we stop at bars along the way?
The Milwaukee River is a gem and full of great river bars to make a quick pit stops. Most of our groups make one stop so they can maximize the “on water time”, but we will make stops determined the day of based on your preferences, dock availability and the river traffic that day!
Yes you can, Bring Your Own Bevs! We have 4 built-in bar coolers with ice to cool your drinks down. We recommend cans over glass, if you have extras at the end of the trip please remember you can’t drink them at the bar. You can tip them to your crew, or throw them in a car.
Our Public ticketed tours are 21+ since there is often drinking alcohol, and we do make a bar stop.
For our PRIVATE tours booked, the boat is yours to enjoy! We are family friendly and all ages welcome for those. Please note that anyone 12 or younger is required to wear a life vest for the whole duration of the tour. We do have some vests on site for all ages, but if you have more than a couple of children please reach out to us and we can help set you up with enough if you need to borrow ours!
How do we know if the Paddle Tavern is available when we want it?
How many people can fit on the Paddle Tavern?
The Paddle Tavern can fit up to 16 passengers, and up to 26 on the Nauti Tiki Tavern! We have 3 boats if you need more than one boat. Please call us @ to make this type of reservation!
(414) 436-2709
We have roofs and free ponchos. If it’s light rain we party on. If it’s a nasty weather day we will connect with you on the morning of your tour to game plan options: rain checks, delayed start time, or a refund.
Cancel 30 days prior to your booking for a full refund, no questions asked. You can cancel 15-29 days prior to your booking to receive your down payment as a credit to use with us any time in the future- never expires. If you do not cancel 15 days or more before your tour with us, there is no refund or reschedule.
If something comes up, give us a call/shoot us a text and we are happy to discuss options to reschedule your party before the cutoff date or issue a credit to rebook when you can.
We run 7 days a week from Mid-March through the end of October. First tours start at 10:00 AM and the last tours of the day go out at 8:30 PM.
Click the Book Now button to see open time slots – you can see them before entering payment. Our online booking option takes full payment or you can pay half over the phone and the other half upon arrival.
We like to have at least 6 on a boat so it’s not too hard to pedal!

Hopefully Our Faq Section Has Your Answer
How many people per boat?
We are only allowing 12 people per boat at this time.
My reservation only says 1 adult but I'm bringing more people, how do I change that?
Because our rental software is per unit(boat) and not per person, the sytem automatically puts 1 adult. There is no way to change the number but be sure to check your boat size and capacity to ensure you rented the proper size for your party.
Can we bring anything with us on the boat?
Yes. Food, drink, even your dog! We are very pet friendly! We work with many vendors that will deliver food/décor for your rental, please scroll on our homepage to see options! Feel free to bring your own cooler and we sell ice in the boat shop! If you like popcorn, it's always free too!
What if we need to cancel?
All sales are final. In the event of an act of God such as weather (gale wind, heavy rain, snow, hurricanes) terrorism, earthquakes; your rental will be moved to another day, or store credit will be issued. There are no refunds and this policy will be strictly enforced.
Will we get wet or cold?
All of our boats are fully enclosed and generally cozy. Windows can go up if a cool breeze is wanted or needed, or they can stay down to enjoy the scene warm and cozy. During the winter time blankets are always welcome.
Is it a fun experience for children too?
Absolutely! Alamitos Bay provides for plenty of wildlife, with the local sea lions making many appearances throughout the day. We also have a Coloring Contest for kids 6 yrs and below. Every month, we pick the winner and they win a boat ride. Make sure you ask for coloring materials when you check-in.
Are you pet friendly?
Yes! We love our Fido! In fact, our logo was inspired by our English bulldog Titus Maximus. Every now and then, you will see him manning the store or eating the leftover popcorn on the floor. :) For the safety of your pets, we recommend bringing their own life vests.
Is it hard to drive a boat, and what is the age limit to drive?
The boats are very simply to drive. Maximum speed is 5 mph. You must be 21 years old to drive. Before take off, our dock master gives the captain a very detailed description of the Bay, where to go, and what you can see.
Do the boats have a sound system?
The boats all have radios with CD player capability, also included is an auxiliary wire for your smart phone.
Is parking free?
Yes. The parking is free, on site, only steps away from your vessel. Guests may also arrive by Aqualink.
Are lifejackets provided?
Yes. All of our vessels have adult life jackets on the vessel, and our front office staff provides all children under the age of 12 with a life jacket. All children under the age of 12 are required to wear a life vest. We also provide life vests for infants. Infants in car seats or baby carriers are not required to wear a life vest, but one will be provided anyway. We do not provide life vests for pets.
What time should we arrive before our voyage?
Give yourself 15-20 minutes. This will give you time to park, unload, sign-in, and be on your way with no delay.
Help! I left something on the boat and I need it back. What do I do?
London Boat Rentals is not responsible for personal belongings, however, if you lost something please call or email with a description of the item(s) lost and we will contact you if it has been found.
If the tide is too high for me to go into the Naples Canals, where else can I go?
If the tide is too high, you may still travel around Naples island, into Jellyfish Cove, Spinnaker Bay, Marina Pacifica, and Mother’s Beach.
How old do you have to be to rent a boat?
You must be at least 21 years old to rent and operate the boat. You must be at least 18 years old to rent and operate a jet ski.

About Turnagain Pass

TITLE: The Trail to the Big Blue Ice - Alaska Wild Guides
The start of the 2026 snowmobile season has been one like I’ve not seen before. We didn’t have our first true snowfall, that stuck, until January, which is somewhat unheard of. However, as of March, we have received sufficient snowfall to get out to Spencer Glacier via the Placer River Valley.
Although we didn’t receive snow in the early season, we did receive very cold days that froze the water ways to the ground. This has made for excellent river crossings and with a bunch of hard work from our guides we shoveled snow onto these crossings to build bridges and get people out to Spencer Glacier.
I’ve received quite a few calls from skiers, fat tire bikers, and recreational snowmachiners asking what the conditions are like to Spencer Glacier. Although they are not like years past, there is a safe trail getting out to the Glacier. It is one of the longest trails we have ever built before, as it has to weave back-and-forth across the valley to avoid brush that is typically buried under several feet of snow.
I want to give a huge shout out to the Alaska Wild Guides crew for all their hard work in making this season happen. Without their hard work, river crossings would not be possible, as they required many hours of shoveling snow over ice to make them tour-able.
The Spencer Glacier Snowmobile Day Tour is one of the most popular winter activities out of the Anchorage area. Just a short 45 minute drive from Anchorage, this tour allows visitors and community members an unbelievable backcountry experience, not far from the town of Anchorage. If you want to make it a bigger experience, I strongly suggest staying a night or two in the great community of Girdwood. Combine snowmobiling with a day of skiing at the Alyeska Resort and you have yourself a true Alaskan winter adventure.

Do you want to miss out on some of the best red snapper fishing in the United States? Of course, you don’t!

Red snapper is one of the most delicious fish in the world, and it’s actually very hard to find fresh in the United States. On top of fishing for red snapper because it tastes fantastic (which, trust us, it does), it’s also a great challenge for even the most seasoned fisherman or woman. These tough fighters are big (up to 50 pounds) and are very rewarding to reel in.

Capt. Greg, can you briefly walk us through your story – how you started and how you got to where you are today.
How did you start Wave Dancer Galveston Fishing Charters?
I started fishing the Gulf of Mexico at a very young age at about 4 years old with my father Don Ball. He would take me on offshore fishing trips with him all the time. I loved fishing so much and growing up on the Gulf coast, at a young age I wanted my own boat. My dad told me when I was 12 years old that If I could make the money to buy my own boat that I could have one. So I started working for the newspaper as a paper boy and mowed grass and anything else I could do to make a little money and within a year at age 13 I had my own boat. Me and my buddies would fish lots of afternoons after school and weekends and I still fished at least once or twice a week with my dad all though high school. I graduated high school and worked selling cars for my dad at his new car dealership, then opened a used car lot myself and a new boat dealership. I had also been buying rental property all along and in 1995 I got out of sales and went into nothing but buying, remodeling and renting real estate and flipping houses. That was a great job until hurricane’s Rita in 2005 and Ike in 2008 came along and wiped out almost everything I had. I prayed about what to do and was led to sell everything I had and buy a big Hatteras sports fishing yacht and start fishing. One thing led to another and my Stepson Taylor Borel and I were talking one day and decided that we should go to captain’s school and get our license and start doing offshore fishing charters for a living and that would give us extra money to go fishing for ourselves too. He was 19 or 20 at the time and had gone fishing with me since he was a small child and we had plenty of sea time to get our 100 ton Master Captains License, so we did just that. We started our company in 2011 with that one boat and now we have 3 in our fleet and two are federally permitted to run up to 80 or so miles offshore with up to 6 fisherman on board. I have always been told that you will never work a day in your life if you love what you do. This is that kind of job, we work 7 long days a week 365 days a year (well we do take off for Christmas and Easter) but it is the most awesome job in the world, watching people fight and land lots of huge fish and see how happy they become and proud of themselves. We help people make their dreams come true and check fish caught off their bucket list. We get to do lots of charity events for the less fortunate, handicapped, disabled children and adults, and we get to meet the best people in the world while fishing.
Overall, has it been relatively smooth? If not, what were some of the struggles along the way?
It’s been fairly smooth with a few bumps along the way with expense of maintenance and upkeep on the boats. Because we run almost every day of the year and almost 500 charters a year on 3 boats you can imagine that we have lots of upkeep. In 2015 we bought all new motors for our boats and it’s been a lot easier and less expensive ever since we did that. The other problem is with anything you do, there are laws, state and federal and the same goes with Charter for Hire fishing. We have been battling the state and the federal government for years on fish stocks and leaving our seasons open longer or giving us some more days and let us fish them when the weather is good. It’s been a hard battle but we are starting to win and things are getting lots better. We joined the Charter Fisherman Association and they are on the right track to getting everything worked out for us to have more fishing days. The only other real struggle that we have is Mother Nature. We get trips booked and then can’t run them for bad weather and then we lose a day of work because of it. Other than those few things it’s smooth sailing most of the time.

TITLE: It’s Redfish Season! What You Need to Know About Catching Redfish
It’s Redfish Season again!
I love this time of year, and I have since I was a kid. As an adult, I enjoy providing my kids with the same experiences I had when I was younger. Fishing is a great way for the whole family to bond, have fun, and create memories that will last a lifetime.
One of my all-time favorite types of fish to catch is redfish. Red drum fish (also known as “redfish”) is a sportfishing staple—especially in Galveston Bay. Fall is the season for redfish fishing and, since fall is winding down, you’ll want to jump on the opportunity to get out on the water and catch a beautiful show-stopper!
Catching Redfish is a ton of fun! With that said, you may not be sure how to catch them. Whether you are a seasoned fisherman that isn’t used to fishing for red drum fish or you are new to fishing, there are a few things you can do to increase your chances of bringing home an impressive fish!
Here are some tips for catching redfish…

=== PAGE: https://wavedancercharters.com/going-deep-sea-fishing-here-is-what-you-need-to-know-about-rods-and-reels/
TITLE: Going Deep Sea Fishing? Here is What You Need to Know About Rods and Reels
Do you have a fun and exciting deep sea fishing trip coming up? If so, you may be wondering which rod and reel will be the perfect choice to help you reel in some of the biggest, most challenging, and most exciting fish out on the waters of Galveston, Texas.
Here are some tips for finding the best rod and reel for your deep sea fishing trip in Galveston, Texas.
Deep sea rods are strong, and they are intended to withstand the power of large fish like tuna, marlin, and sharks. These rods are often longer and can range from 6 to 8 feet. This provides the leverage needed to battle these immense fish. You’ll generally want to go with a rod that has a “heavy” or “extra heavy” power rating to help you lift these sea beasts out of the ocean—even while they are fighting back.
For action, you should go with a fast or moderate-fast choice. Fast will help you to control the tip better, while moderate-fast is great for flexibility and power.
The material is another consideration, as different materials have their advantages and disadvantages.
As for your reel, you should go with a reel that offers powerful drags, high line capacity, and durability. Features like a lever drag system will help with making precise adjustments. The frame should be made from stainless steel or aluminum.
It’s very important that your reel has a high line capacity of around 300 yards and a powerful drag system that can handle at least 20 pounds of pressure. Also pay attention to the gear ratio, as lower gear ratios allow for more cranking power, while higher gear ratios are better for fast retrieval.
Choosing the right rod and reel combo will depend on a few factors that include your budget, experience level, and what you are looking to catch. With that said, if you aren’t regularly out on the water and you decide to hire an outstanding charter boat company, you don’t have to worry about bringing your own rods and reels.

ONE MUSEUM, ONE MISSION, TWO LOCATIONS
Navy SEAL Museum Fort Pierce
Visit Fort Pierce

If You Got Any Closer, You Would Have to Enlist
The National Navy SEAL Museum is the only museum dedicated solely to preserving the history of the United States Navy SEALs and their predecessors. Located in Fort Pierce, Florida, the Museum resides on the training grounds of the original Navy combat divers, the Frogmen.
Built to honor the men who served with fortitude and dedication, the Navy SEAL Museum first opened its doors on Veterans Day in 1985. From humble beginnings, the facility has experienced tremendous growth, achieving national stature in 2007.
The main objective of the Museum remains the promotion of public education by providing the opportunity to explore the history of the United States Navy SEALs through interactive exhibits, while honoring the fallen at the Navy SEAL Memorial and caring for those warriors’ families through the Trident House Charities Program.
Like the Frogmen of the Forties to the SEAL Teams of the New Millennium, the Navy SEAL Museum continues to evolve to carry forth this mission. While these Special Operators have a tactical mission to maintain homeland security, the Museum is dedicated to educating the public about the invaluable role of SEALs as we continue our expansion to the West Coast in San Diego, California.
Our Mission
The National Navy SEAL Museum preserves and honors the legacy of Naval Special Warfare, strengthens our communities to create a lasting impact, and inspires multiple generations toward a stronger future.
Our Vision
Our vision is to build a legacy of honor, resilience, and service that extends far beyond the walls of our museums.
We bring this mission to life across four core pillars by:
Curating and preserving Naval Special Warfare history through our coastal campuses and monuments
Honoring our fallen
Providing adaptive support to our active-duty community to meet their unique modern need
Delivering life-changing resources to special operations veterans and families through the Navy SEAL Museum Charities.
By investing deeply in community engagement and public benefit programs at both the regional and national levels, we transform our historic legacy into a modern catalyst; inspiring the next generation to answer a higher call to service, strengthen their communities, and make a lasting impact on the world.
Values
The National Navy SEAL Museum is committed to the same values SEAL Teams are forged upon.

We’re all grown-ups here. Right? (Skydiving, after all, has an 18+ age limit in the good ol’ US of A, so we’re imagining that’s you, too.) Since that’s out of the way, here it is: Depending who you talk to, it could be said that we’re kinda-sorta in a golden age for marijuana availability. In Las Vegas, NV – marijuana is legalized for medicinal and recreational use. That being said: “recreational use” by no means refers to “use during any recreational pursuit you desire to undertake.” If you blaze up in the car and any staff member notices the act or its effects, you will definitely NOT be blazing up to altitude.
Why? Well: As a tandem student, you’re not going to be a passive passed-out passenger. You’ll be taking an active role on the skydive, which will require you to go through a training process, to learn new skills and to demonstrate them in the high-pressure environment of freefall. Most tandem skydiving students love this super-involved, all-hands-on-deck experience–it’s much more personal and much more satisfying than, say, strapping into a roller coaster–but it requires your 100% engagement. Weed or any drugs reduce your ability to do what we need you to do, which, of course, is what you need you to do in order to complete a safe, awesome skydive.
If you are suspected to be under the influence of drugs or marijuana, you will not be allowed to skydive! Yes, your jump ticket will be forfeited!
Some prescription drugs are allowed as long as they don’t affect your motor and mental abilities.
BAD IDEA #2: SKYDIVING DRUNK
Well, if there was a worse idea than skydiving high, it’s skydiving drunk. Not only does all of the above apply, but you’re putting yourself in danger of becoming a flying vomit bomb or passing out. If you’re drunk, you will not be allowed to board the shuttle, you will not be allowed anywhere near our top-notch team members and professional skydiving instructors and our gear, you will most likely be asked to leave the premises. Your jump ticket will be forfeited
Do you offer pick up / drop off?
No, you must arrange own transportation to the jump location: 1110 Airport Road Overton NV 89040 – Perkins Field Airport.
Can I bring my own Go Pro to record the jump?
We get this question A LOT. The answer is NO! Why? The answer is – Safety! Your safety and the safety of all people on the ground! All video equipment used by skydivers is highly specialized and tested to make sure that it does not interfere with the safety of the skydive and the people on the ground! Non skydive tested and certified equipment is a huge safety issue and it is simply – dangerous! Not properly secured video equipment WILL do huge damage to the people and property on the ground……… The list of why you CAN NOT bring your Go Pro or any other video and photo equipment non-skydive certified video equipment to film your own skydive is very, very, very long………..
Does Fyrosity® offer the Highest jump in Nevada?
Yes! Fyrosity® is the only Drop Zone in Las Vegas offering the highest jump and longest freefall time than any other! Why? Fyrosity® is located at the lowest elevated airport in the state of Nevada at only 1,365ft above see level. All other’s are located at much higher above see level elevations.
Fyrosity® – Overton Airport – 1,365 ft MSL
Mesquite Airport – 1,978 ft. (+613 ft)
Boulder City Airport – 2,201 ft. (+836 ft)
Jean Airport – 2,832 ft. (+1467 ft)
What does this means? It means that you get to free fall 10 – 12 seconds longer that any other location in the state, since the ground is further away from the exit altitude. If anyone else is claiming they offer the highest jump and the longest free fall in Nevada – they are making a false claim!
I have the Flu, head cold, nasal congestion and or sinus infection, can I skydive?
We at Skydive Fyrosity® DO NOT recommended that you skydive with Flu, head cold, nasal congestion, sinus infection or any other symptoms that restrict your body’s natural ability to equalize air pressure! It is a lot better, safer and a LOT cheaper to cancel your skydive and lose your deposit of $100 (if less than 48 hours or on the day of your skydive) than it would be to end up with permanent health damage and huge doctor’s bills. However, this choice is yours! Yes, we know it is your last day in Las Vegas and you can not reschedule, however skydiving is not the local fast food restaurant with a line of customers waiting to take your slot.
If you select to keep it a secret and not to disclose that you are sick and decide to make a skydive anyway, you will be exposing your personal health and the health of other helping you along the way to extreme dangers.
Here are the warnings!
The Flu congests the nasal and sinus passage! What that means? That means that your body’s natural ability to adjust and equalize for the air pressure differences when we get to altitude is not working. Skydiving is an activity that involves going to higher altitudes up to 15,000 feet.
Most people, thank heaven, have never experienced the abject misery of a popped eardrum. When the pressure on the inside of the eardrum is so much greater than the pressure on the outside of the eardrum–as can happen when a stuffed-up nose enters the thinner air of a jump plane altitude–it can pop like a balloon. The sensation of a popping eardrum is difficult to describe with any accuracy, but most people who experience it will tell you that it’s like having a tiny little dude shoot you in the ear from the inside, then pour gasoline on the wound and light it on fire.

TITLE: Sandhill Crane Kayak Tour | Chattanooga Guided Adventures
Sandhill Crane Kayak Tour at the Hiwassee Wildlife Refuge
Book your trip
The best winter kayak tour in the state of Tennessee running November through the last weekend in February to see and hear all of the calls and dances of the wintering sandhill cranes. Witness the cranes in their warmer winter environment as they escape the brutal cold of Alaska and Northern Canada. The shallow warm waters of the Tennessee River around Hiwassee Island provide excellent overwintering and feeding areas for the cranes. Use our binoculars and enjoy the sights and sound of the sandhill cranes on this eco kayak tour. Thousands or birds can be seen flying above and landing on the water surrounding the island.
This is a wildlife experience like none other in Tennessee. It is like paddling through Jurassic Park. Thousands of five foot tall 14 pound birds hanging out on the waters edge around the island flapping there wings and dancing. These social birds calls can be heard from over 2 miles away. These birds have come back from the brink of extinction from unregulated over hunting and are thriving on this overwinter adventure just outside Chattanooga, Tennessee. No kayaking experience needed, this is a beginner friendly trip.
Our winter neoprene paddle mittens (poagies), waterproof jacket, and drip skirt will keep you nice and warm out on the water.
We also provide hot chocolate or apple cider after your kayak adventure ends.
This trip is a fun way to meet new friends or get your old friends off of the couch to try something new.
The Tennessee Sandhill Crane Festival is held on January 13-14, 2024. This is a great time to join us on a kayak tour as there will be plenty of free activities after your kayak tour for you to participate in. The festival runs from 8 am to 4 pm daily.

=== PAGE: https://www.broadmoor.com/adventures/soaring-adventure/know-before-you-go
TITLE: Know Before You Go | Zip Line Excursion Tips | The Broadmoor
To help you make the most of your experience, here are a few tips and tricks so you can come prepared for your zip line excursion.
Plan Ahead
Soaring Adventure is limited to 8 people per tour, per hour.
Weight restrictions are between 90 and 250 pounds.
Participants must wear closed toe shoes where toes are covered in one solid enclosure, such as tennis or hiking shoes. Five Fingered Vibram shoes have each toe enclosed but they are separated; therefore, they are not acceptable.
Most of our zip lines are in the sun, so sunscreen and sunglasses are advisable.
Small pouches are available for wallets, cell phones, keys, etc. in case you want to bring them on the zip lines.
Large cameras or backpacks can be brought to Seven Falls Park but are not allowed on the course itself. Guests traveling with bulky items will have them transported to the end of the course by our ground support staff, where you can pick them up for the rest of your explorations within Seven Falls.
No outside food or beverages permitted inside the park. Snacks and bottled water can be purchased at the Seven Falls Shop.
Parking
Please note that The Broadmoor Soaring Adventure zip line tours do not take the Seven Falls Shuttle. Our zip lines start behind the park and end inside, so we take a different shuttle to where Soaring Adventure begins. All Broadmoor Soaring Adventure patrons will park at The Broadmoor’s East Lot just off of Lake Ave at 6 Lake Avenue, Colorado Springs, CO. 80906. Parking is free of charge.

TITLE: Soaring Colorado Adventures Courses at Broadmoor Outfitters
The Courses
Accompanied by two guides at all times, Seven Falls Zipline participants can choose the Signature Fins Course or upgrade to the Ultimate Seven Falls Zipline Experience. Each tour begins with Ground School and features zip lines that progressively increase in length and exposure, giving guests time to build confidence as the adventure unfolds.
Signature Fins Course
Soar above steep canyon drops, unique rock formations, and the rugged cliffs of Seven Falls Canyon. This high altitude adventure features five progressively longer zip lines, two custom built suspension bridges, and a controlled 180 foot assisted rappel to the canyon floor. (Approximately 3 hours)
Ultimate Seven Falls Zipline Experience
Experience the full mountain course with our most immersive adventure. The Ultimate tour expands your time on the course with eight zip lines ranging from 250 to 1800 feet, iconic rope bridges suspended high above the canyon, and a 180 foot assisted rappel finish. Designed for guests who want to see and experience it all. (Approximately 4 hours)

pet friendly
The Island Coastal Tour travels to the outer islands of the Cedar Keys National Wildlife Refuge. This scenic route often encounters dolphins and various birds, depending on the season of the year. Occasionally we will come across manatees, sea turtles, and even spotted eagle rays. This trip is an excellent choice for those who wish to experience a balanced overview of Cedar Key history and the natural aspects of our rich and diverse ecosystem. The route and activities vary according to the season of the year and the weather conditions. This is a 1½ to 2 hour Pet Friendly tour that departs multiple times throughout the week weather and conditions permitting.

$40 per person
02.
This evening cruise has been designed specifically to have our guests out on the water during the time of the sunset. This will include a relaxing ride, while looking for dolphins and other area wildlife, to an area of the Cedar Key waters where there is no land obstruction between our boat and the setting sun. Guests are welcome to bring and enjoy their own beverage (adult or otherwise, only lunchbox-size coolers permitted) while cruising and taking in the beauty of the setting sun and all the colors that can be on display. TITLE: Weight Limits and Policy — Cloud Chasers Skydiving
Weight Limits and Policy
Like most any extreme sport, there are weight limits to skydiving. While you do not need to read this entire page, please be sure to read the information in each weight range that applies to any jumper in your group. After going through the information below, if you have any questions or concerns at all, please give us a call.
All Weights
We discreetly weigh everyone for proper weight and balance of the aircraft. Having properly reported weights in advance of each jumper helps us properly prepare for our day of jumping. All weights are in reference to being fully clothed with shoes and prior to being geared up for ones jump.
The situations listed below are rare. However, having a written policy just maintains a good understanding for all parties involved.
An instructor always has the right to refuse service due to any safety concern. Regardless of weight, certain body types are hard or impossible to properly harness. This is obviously a safety concern.
In the event of an instructor refusing to jump with someone within our weight limits and who honestly reported their weight, a full refund will be issued for any payments made for this person.
Failure to accurately report your weight can cause a delay in your jump time or in extreme circumstances you may not be able to jump that at all. This will not be grounds for a refund.
Less than 80 lbs
You are likely smaller than our harnesses will safely adjust to. However we would still be very interested in helping to get you on a skydive. Please give us a call so we can go over some details.
80 - 200 lbs
No concern here. We would still appreciate you reporting your accurate weight when booking as this helps us prepare for our day.
201 - 215 lbs
No concerns here. Please be sure to report accurate weights in this range when booking. Especially if a group of two is both in this range.
216 - 250 lbs
We can normally make this work however there are a few key points to consider to please read the following carefully.
Many DropZones will not even offer you a jump so please bear with us here. We do charge a fee for this service ranging from $15 - $50 depending on your actual weight.
We take up 2 tandem jumpers per flight and we prefer the combined weight of the two passengers to be under 400 lbs.
We are normally fine with a flight of 2 tandems with a combined passenger weight of 401 - 430 but it is necessary to know this in advance. Be sure to include accurate weights of each jumper when booking and/or include any notes to help us be properly informed.
For a flight of 2 tandems with a combined weight over 430 lbs we will likely need to split you up into two flights. If you have a larger group, consider re organizing and sending up one of your heavier passengers with one of your lighter.
If you cannot organize your jumpers so that each flight has a combined passenger weight of less than 430 lbs, consider booking for 1 seat each on separate flights. Please be as accurate as possible on your reported weight and we will pair you with another odd number or fly the flight with just you and your instructor.
If you are a group of 1 or the odd number to a larger group, feel free to book just please be as accurate as possible on your reported weight and we will pair you with another odd number or fly the flight with just you and your instructor.
Failure to accurately report your weight can cause a delay in your jump time or in extreme circumstances you may not be able to jump that day at all. This will not be grounds for a refund. We do of course allow for a few pounds differential between your scales and ours. If you are right on that 250 lb limit and concerned, please give us a call.
Over 250
Cloud Chasers Skydiving has a hard limit of 250 lbs. However there is still hope. Larger DropZones have larger aircraft making it easier for larger people to get into, and more importantly out of. They also have more instructors working for them. This increases the odds that they have a smaller highly experienced instructor to pair you with and still remain under the max supported weight limit of the parachute. There are no such DropZones in Louisiana but it is worth the drive. Below are the nearest DropZones that might be able to help. Check them out and give them a call with your specifics before committing to the trip.
Skydive Spaceland Houston, TX
Skydive Alabama
