How many Jumps?
2 Tandems + 7 AFF jumps gets you to “self supervision” which qualifies you to make solo Jumps. A total of 25 jumps and completion of our training program earns you an “A” license.
What is AFF?
On an AFF jump you will be wearing a parachute yourself, not attached to anyone you will land this parachute solo. There is an instructor with you in Free Fall to train you and lend assistance with stability if needed.
What can I do with an "A" License?
With an “A” license and a current log book you can go to any DropZone in the U.S. and most of the world to make a skydive(s) with little to no headache.
Minimum time to get my "A" license?
After your tandems and ground school, and with proper scheduling, you could complete your AFF jumps and reach self supervision in a single weekend. Completion of your “A” license will take a minimum of another 2-3 weeks largely depending on your availability.
Maximum time I can take to complete the training?
There is no time requirement to complete, only a currency requirement between jumps. Once you start your training you are required to make at least one jump every 30 days. The learning curve is shorter if you can jump more but it is not required. Going beyond your 30days will require refresher ground training and repeating your last jump.
Is there a way to skip the 2 Tandem Jumps?
Not easily but if this is something you feel strongly about, keep reading. In order to do this we are required to use 2 instructors on your first few AFF jumps. We may be willing to do this depending on your performance in the ground training and instructor availability. Although our staff is highly experienced with a dual instructor AFF program, this is NOT our normal process. There will be an extra charge per jump which may vary depending on instructor availability.
Do I have to complete all my training jumps at one DZ
It is normally best to stick with one program, however any properly ran training facility can integrate an existing student into their program based on student experience. We will do our best to pick you up right where you left off with as little retraining as possible. Often the limiting factor is proper documentation from your previous school. Make sure you bring your log book and “A” license proficiency card if you have them.
More Questions?
Give us a call at 985-415-0289. Ask for Joe. As an instructor Joe has thousands of student training jumps and runs the program at Cloud Chasers Skydiving. He is always glad to talk to a student or potential student.

=== PAGE: https://www.cloudchasers-skydiving.com/faq
TITLE: FAQ — Cloud Chasers Skydiving
do i need any experience to skydive?
No! We specialize in first time jumpers making tandem skydives You will be paired with a highly experienced instructor and attached securely to the instructor during FreeFall and under Parachute.
WHAT TIME SHOULD I ARRIVE?
Your appointment time is your arrival time not your jump time. We do ask that you be on time and ready to focus on your paperwork and training. Of course you are welcome to be early and recommended if you are going to need extended personal time before the jump (bathroom, tiktok, etc). Being late can cause you to get bumped back in the schedule. We will normally still get you jumped but it might take a while to fit you in.
HOW MANY PEOPLE CAN BE IN A GROUP?
We schedule groups of 1 - 26. Our waiting area provides a good view of the landing area providing some group interaction.
CAN WE ALL JUMP TOGETHER?
We take up two tandem jumpers at a time and you will leave the plane one after the other with some separation between.
HOW LONG IS THE WHOLE EXPERIENCE?
We strive to keep a strict schedule and normally have you in and out within 2 hours. There are however many possible delays that are out of our control making It is necessary to budget 3 - 4 hours of your day to complete a skydive for 1-2 people. Add 30-40 minutes per pair for more than 2 jumpers.
What is the minimum age?
18 years old. If it were totally up to us we may lower this slightly however due to reasons out of our control this is non-negotiable.
What is the maximum weight?
There is no one real answer here as height, body type, and fitness all play a part if being able to safely wear a Skydiving harness. Typically if you are under 215 lbs and remotely fit there should be no problem. If you are over 215 lbs, please check out our complete .
Weight Limit Policies
Does cloud chasers offer training and can i become a licensed skydiver?
YES!! We offer complete skydiving training via Tandem Progression and AFF. All our instructors are licensed through the United States Parachute Association (USPA) and managed by a USPA Examiner. Tandem Skydiving may be the monetary back bone of skydiving, however training and giving back to the sport will always be a true passion at Cloud Chasers Skydiving.
what should i wear?
For skydiving you’ll need to wear close-toed shoes and form-fitting clothes. Tennis shoes or sneakers are ideal. We’ll provide you with a skydiving jumpsuit before you’re jump.
can i host a party at the dropzone?
Within reason. We have had birthdays, weddings, gender reveals, engagements, etc. From very small to renting the whole dropzone for a day is all possible. We offer skydiving perks for some of these, like gender reveal smoke from the parachutes. We are limited to space and number of guests so please call with as much notice as possible to work this out.
can my friends and family watch me land?
Absolutely. We have shaded picnic tables for your group to hang out at in sight of the landing area. We have water and soft drinks available at very reasonable rates. Please keep in mind you are on an active airport so all children MUST be accompanied by an adult at all times.
can i wear my glasses/contacts?
We will provide you with a pair of goggles to wear during your skydive. These can be worn with glasses or contacts.
are there any medical conditions that would prevent me from skydiving?
We strive to accommodate all jumpers to ensure and safe and fun skydive. Please let your instructor know if you have any medical conditions that they should be aware of.
Can I purchase a gift certificate?
Yes! Gift certificates make a great gift for friends, family, and loved ones.
Any other questions?
Please give us a call or send us a message if you have any other questions!

TITLE: Taxis, Access & Mobility Services | SFMTA
Traditionally, Taxis, Access & Mobility Services Division (TAMS) has represented a combination of two distinct functions of the SFMTA that substantially overlap in the regulation of the taxi industry. is a core support function for all modes of the agency to ensure that transit, pedestrian and bike facilities and taxi services are accessible to older adults and people with disabilities. This division also oversees the SFMTA Paratransit program. In order to provide a cost-efficient and customer friendly network of paratransit services, Accessible Services has leveraged the private taxi industry in a private-public partnership. ’ core function is to license and regulate the private taxi industry to ensure that drivers and vehicles are safe, that taxi service is accessible to the disability community, and service is available regardless of trip origin or destination at prices that are transparent.
Taxi Services
Over the past few years, transportation options in San Francisco have changed significantly, and the functions of TAMS have expanded as well. A variety of mobility services and technologies have emerged, from mobile applications that connect passengers with on demand service, shared ride van services, shared scooter services, to autonomous vehicles that are currently being tested on our City streets. These new mobility services present both opportunities and challenges to the safe and efficient movement of people and goods in San Francisco, which is mandated by City Charter in the Transit-First Policy.
In response to these changes, Taxis, Access & Mobility Services and the Streets Division (formerly Sustainable Streets) have partnered to develop and implement permit programs for services within the SFMTA’s jurisdiction to balance the drive for innovation with the goals of providing safe, reliable, accessible and equitable transportation in San Francisco. The Streets Division is the lead in incubating new mobility programs in collaboration with Taxis, Access & Mobility Services, and Taxis, Access & Mobility Services is the operational division and takes the lead in regulating and managing ongoing mobility permit programs.
The Accessible Services Program provides a dedicated focus on the needs of seniors and individuals with disabilities to ensure access to all transportation modes in San Francisco. This includes:
Muni Fixed Route: assuring that the Muni fixed route system is fully accessible and usable by people with disabilities and seniors
SF Paratransit: overseeing the administration of the city’s paratransit program through a contract with Transdev to provide more than 700,000 van and taxi rides to approximately 14,000 eligible individuals with disabilities
Clipper Access Discount ID card program (formerly Regional Transit Connection [RTC] Discount ID card program): providing qualifying individuals a Clipper Access card that allows them to access the discounted fare on all participating transit systems in the region
Technical Support: providing technical expertise on Muni, bicycle, and pedestrian projects to ensure compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act
Community Participation: staffing two active public advisory committees, the Multimodal Accessibility Advisory Committee, which provides feedback about disabled access to Muni, streets projects and other modes of transportation regulated by SFMTA, and the Paratransit Coordinating Council, which provides feedback regarding service quality for the city’s paratransit program
Emerging Mobility: ensuring that disabled access is considered and promoted as part of emerging mobility services evaluation, permitting and operations

=== PAGE: https://www.tikitimetours.ca/tiki-time-tales/top-questions-we-get-about-tiki-boat-tours
TITLE: Top Questions We Get About Tiki Boat Tours — Tiki Time Tours
Aug 19
So, you’re thinking about booking a Tiki Boat Tour? Great choice! Whether you’re in soaking up Okanagan Lake vibes or in cruising through False Creek, our floating Tiki bars are the ultimate way to celebrate just about anything.
Before you hop on board, here are the answers to the most common questions we get asked. Spoiler alert: yes, you can play your own music.
Is it safe?
Absolutely. Every boat carries Transport Canada–certified lifejackets for all passengers, along with first aid kits and all required safety gear. Our captains are highly trained through Transport Canada programs, including Small Vessel Operator Proficiency and MED3 Emergency Duties. In other words—you’re in very good hands.
Food & Drinks: What’s the deal?
We provide coolers, bottled water, and ice. You can bring your own snacks and beverages (alcoholic and non-alcoholic).
Our Tiki Boat is licensed! You can purchase refreshing drinks onboard, but no outside alcohol is permitted. Snacks and food are welcome.
Can I play my own music?
Yes! Each Tiki Boat comes equipped with a Bluetooth sound system so you can set the vibe with your own playlist. Whether that’s tropical island beats, sing-along classics, or your pre-party hype list, the boat becomes your stage.
Can I bring my dog?
Sorry, no pets onboard.
What if it rains?
Our boats are covered, so the party continues rain or shine. But your safety comes first—if conditions are unsafe, your captain may cancel or reschedule. (And yes, we’ll always work with you to find a new date if weather gets in the way.)
Are kids allowed?
Yes, kids love the Tiki Boat! Children under 12 must wear a lifejacket (we provide them, or you can bring your own). Just let us know ahead of time so we can make sure the right sizes are ready.
We’ve got you covered. Every Tiki Boat has a restroom onboard so you can relax and enjoy your tour without worry.
How many people can cruise together?
Each Tiki Boat holds up to 12 passengers plus crew (Transport Canada rules—no exceptions). If your group is bigger, you can rent multiple boats, like pairing the Tiki Boat with our . While boats can’t tether together while cruising, we can link up at swim stops.
How long are tours?
Most tours run 1–4 hours, but we can go longer depending on your booking. Some groups like a quick spin, others want to spend the afternoon on the water—it’s up to you.
Do you charge cleaning fees?
Normal cleaning is included in your tour cost, however we expect our vehicles to be left in a reasonable state at the end of your tour. We may charge up to $500 if additional cleaning is required. Keep it fun, keep it respectful, and you won’t need to worry.
Ready to Cruise?
Whether it’s a bachelorette bash, a family float, or just a reason to sip something cold with friends, a is the summer experience you won’t forget.

Yes Our Tiki Boats have a restroom on board.

Bookings are non-refundable within 10 days of booked tour date. We reserve the right to cancel any tour at any time due to weather, safety, mechanical, . If your tour is canceled, you will be given a rain check to re-book at another time*.
Can more than 12 people cruise at the same time?
Transport Canada regulations for our Tiki Boat is 12 people plus crew.... this includes children... NO EXCEPTIONS! For larger groups, you may rent a second Tiki Boat or our Pontiki as well and cruise together. We are NOT permitted to tether together while cruising, however if anchored on a swim stop we may tether together for larger groups.
Are children allowed?

Do your boats operate in the rain?

Can i play my own music on board?

: We provide a cooler with ice and water. We do not serve any food or other drinks, however you may bring any snacks, food, or alcoholic beverages you want.

Group reservations?

=== PAGE: https://courageoussailing.org/adult-community/faq/
TITLE: Adult FAQ - Courageous Sailing
Adult Program Frequently Asked Questions
Where should I park? What’s the easiest way to get there?
Nautica Garage: Most of the Charlestown parking near Courageous is metered or resident parking, so your best bet is is to park at the Nautica Parking Garage (88 Constitution Road, 02129). Remember to ask the Courageous Front Desk to validate your ticket; discounted rates are available for 1 – 4 hours. Unfortunately, for all stays longer than 4 hours regular rates apply. Make sure to allow an extra 15 minutes to stroll through the Navy Yard to Pier 4, and take a look at the map so you know where to walk. From the Nautica, leave the water and piers on your right and walk into the Navy Yard. Pass the Constitution Museum on your right, then Pier 3 (where the MBTA ferry leaves from). Turn right at the next pier, walking along the U-shaped inlet of water on your right and a park on your left. Walk past the round brick building and onto Pier 4–you’ll see the masts of our boats on the left of the pier. Go to the left side of our boathouse, which is a little white building with a flag on top.
Flagship Wharf: You may also park at the Flagship Wharf Garage (197 8th Street, 02129), which is closer but more expensive. Street parking is an option if you’ve got extra time to look for it. There are 2-hour metered spots on 1st Street (free and unlimited on Sundays), free Sunday parking in residential spots on the far side of Chelsea Street, and very rare free spots on Terry Ring. No guarantees on this information–make sure to check the signs!! Do not park on any of the piers, including Pier 4.
Public Transportation: Buses and Trains- Green Line, Orange Line, 93 bus Ferry- The Charlestown Ferry from Long Wharf drops off at the base of our pier. Keep in mind that the last departure from Charlestown is 6:15 pm. Water taxis are also available on call and will pick up from the ferry dock (note: water taxis may not pick up or drop off passengers at our docks due to liability restrictions.) Biking- There is a blue-bike station in the Navy Yard
Ride share/Taxi If you take a taxi or a ride share service, verify that the pickup location is in the circle at the base of Pier 4 Charlestown. Vehicles are not allowed to drive on Pier 4.
When should I plan to arrive?
Please arrive at Courageous about 10 minutes early, and check in at the Front Desk. Make sure to allow extra time for parking and the walk over. If you’re running late, please give us a call and let us know. If you arrive late for a 2-hour sail, we may not be able to give you the full two hours.
What should I bring? What should I wear? What about food?
Bring a water bottle, sunscreen, and a few extra layers, including a waterproof jacket. Sunglasses and a hat are good ideas, too. Cameras/phones are welcome–we love to be tagged in photos. If you’ve bought an online deal, make sure to bring your voucher code if you haven’t provided it already.
Feel free to bring snacks or lunch. Coffee, snacks, and sandwiches are available at several locations near Courageous. Our full-day weekend courses incorporate a half hour lunch break. You may leave to purchase lunch, or bring your own; our refrigerator is available for the use of members and students. You’re also welcome to use our grills and bring beer or other drinks to enjoy after sailing (no alcohol before or during sailing). We often host cookouts for members, students, and racers on weekday evenings (Saturdays in the fall)–feel free to join in.
Dress comfortably–jeans and sneakers are just fine. Wear a few layers, since the weather is often hotter or chillier than you expect, and bring an extra layer or two. We recommend wearing closed-toed shoes with good traction and non-marking soles, such as sneakers or boat shoes–no flip flops or heels. Life jackets are provided.
What if there’s bad weather or strong wind?
Well, that depends on what you mean by bad weather. Sailing is fun even when the weather isn’t perfect, and we can’t guarantee sunny days for everyone. So if it’s overcast or raining a bit, we will sail (we have raingear you can borrow, if necessary). We monitor the radar and wind speed closely, so that we can predict when heavy rain or unsafe conditions are likely to pass through.
2-hour sails and private lessons: If Courageous decides to cancel due to likely thunderstorms, heavy rain, dangerously strong winds, or any other reason, we will reschedule your 2-hour sail or lesson free of charge. If the weather is looking bad, give us a call before heading to Charlestown if we haven’t contacted you already.
Courses: We almost never cancel a full day of our courses, as the curriculum includes plenty of onshore material that can be covered when the conditions aren’t safe to sail.
How will I know if my course is canceled or there are restrictions on member sailing?
If your course is canceled, we’ll send out email notifications to students by approximately 8:30 AM, as well as posting an alert on our homepage. If you’re concerned about the weather and need notification before 8:30, please let us know a day in advance.
It’s always a good idea to check the Courageous homepage for weather alerts and restrictions before heading over to Pier 4, especially if you’re a Red or Yellow Flag skipper–sometimes it’s windier than you realize! Alerts are usually posted half an hour before we open, and may change throughout the day. If you’re a member who’s not sure if you’ll be allowed to sail (or if you WANT to sail!), give us a call and we’ll give you the latest scoop on the wind and radar.
What if I need to reschedule?
2-hour sails and private lessons As long as you give us 48 hours notice or more, rescheduling or canceling is no problem at all, just give us a call at 617-242-3821. If you need to reschedule or cancel within 48 hours of your lesson, we will try our best to accommodate, but cannot guarantee availability. Cancellations within 48 hours, that are not weather related, are subject to a $60 cancellation fee, and no refunds shall be offered.
Courses All courses must be scheduled within the calendar year of purchase, and no refunds shall be offered. Students may reschedule up to 2 weeks before the start of their course. Within 2 weeks of the scheduled course, the booking may not be rescheduled and no refunds shall be offered.
Students must attend all dates of their selected course. If a day is missed, it is the student’s responsibility to schedule make-up sessions. Private lessons may be purchased for this purpose at the discounted member rate.
If Courageous cancels all or part of your course due to weather or any other reason, we will do our best to reschedule at a convenient time for the students.
What kind of boat will I be sailing? Could we capsize? Will I get wet?
For our 2-hour sails and most of our courses, you’ll be sailing a Rhodes 19. Rhodes 19s are keelboats, which means that there is a big heavy metal fin on the bottom that prevents the boat from capsizing. On windy days, you may get a bit wet from the spray, but there is a compartment where you can stow items and keep them dry.
What should I do with my belongings and valuables?
Your cellphone will fall out of your back pocket! Make sure it is zipped into a safe place. If you’d like to store your valuables on land, we can hold them for you behind the Front Desk. The boats are usually dry enough to bring your bag, etc. along with you–just stow your things in one of the side bins. If you’d prefer to leave your things ashore, bring a lock and use one of the lockers in the hall on the way to the bathrooms. Please don’t leave your belongings out in the boathouse or in an unlocked locker, or leave anything overnight.
When is the best time to sail on Boston Harbor?
Some of the best sailing of the year is in May, June, and September…and don’t be afraid to book a course or 2-hour sail in October! We love fall sailing because the harbor tends to be less crowded, the wind is often excellent, and a warm jacket is all you need if it’

=== PAGE: https://courageoussailing.org/events/corporate-outings/
TITLE: Corporate Pier Rentals - Courageous Sailing
Corporate Outings
Pier 4 is a prize venue for an active group of any size.
Courageous offers a wide array of customized outings staffed by our professional instructors that are getting rave reviews. Designed to meet your specific needs, events at Courageous can include relays, regattas, or harbor cruises.
Corporate Events are a vital source of general operating funds for Courageous Sailing making it possible to open the sport of sailing to thousands of Boston-area kids and programs.
The Fun Regatta
The Fun Regatta lets groups learn about sailing and racing, build a sense of teamwork, and enjoy some intramural competition.
Your trip to Courageous begins with a quick welcome and an explanation of how a race works, before heading out on the water. Each boat will have a Courageous instructor aboard, to teach the team how to work together to control the boat; if you’re out on the water for more than two hours, each sailor takes a turn learning to steer, as well. During the last hour, everyone can put their new skills to the test in a series of short races. Usually, the team will take charge of controlling the sails while the instructor steers, but after a few races, everyone may get a chance to take the tiller. We’ll follow up with a casual awards ceremony at the end of the day, so that teams can claim their bragging rights. If you’d like to set up catered event or cookout afterwards, we’re happy to help you arrange it.
The Harbor Island Cruise
This event is great for executive level or smaller groups interested in a more personalized experience
Set the sails and take in the skyline as you cruise past the city and out to the Historic Boston Islands on our J80s. With high booms, open cockpits, and a large keel for stability, the J80 makes for a fast and social sailing experience. As with all things in sailing, our Island cruises are dependent on conditions.
The Leisurely Harbor Sail
This is the most casual type of outing.
Participants can spend the day learning to sail or tour points of interest in Boston Harbor. A Leisurely sail is an option for groups big and small. Take a turn at the helm or just sit back, relax, and let us do the work.

TITLE: FAQ | Discover Water Adventures Today — Seakart Adventure SC
Frequently asked questions
Age requirements and how many guests per Seakart?
Drivers must be 18+ with a valid driver’s license. Riders must be at least 6 years old.
Each Seakart accommodates up to three people—one driver and up to two riders.
Are there any physical requirements or restrictions?
Each Seakart has a total weight limit of 500 lbs. Guests may not participate if they are under the influence of drugs or alcohol, cannot swim, or have medical conditions that could put themselves or others at risk, including pregnancy. These guidelines help ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for everyone.
What is your riding zone?
Your adventure will be led by a security boat through the inlet and ocean (weather permitting). Our riding area will generally cover a total distance of 15 miles. The crew on the water will assist with boundaries and departing/returning to the dock. They are here to ensure safety and enhance your experience.
How does safety and instruction work?
Before heading out, every guest participates in a safety briefing with thorough instructions, so you feel confident riding, understand the area, and know how to operate the Seakart. Our crew explains all safety procedures and is happy to answer any questions.
In accordance with South Carolina law, life jackets are provided and must be worn at all times while underway. A security boat accompanies every adventure, and our crew are CPR and First Aid certified. Your safety is our top priority, so we ask all guests to listen carefully to instructions and request clarification if needed—we want you to have a safe, fun, and unforgettable experience on the water.
How early to arrive?
You arrive 15 minutes early for your reservation. We will depart as to not interfere with the other Seakart guests.
The tour will begin immediately following our operating instructions and safety briefing.
What to wear & bring?
You may get wet when driving and riding the Seakart! Water and sun protective clothing and sunscreen recommended. Flip flops and water shoes are permitted. All other shoes must be stored in the lockers provided at the dock. Cell phones are strictly prohibited on the Seakart.
Where to park?
Free parking is available in the adjacent lot. Visit our for more info/maps.
Scan one of the QR codes located around the lot and follow the steps. The Seakart crew will provide the validation code when you check in at the dock.
Do you take photos?
The Seakart crew loves taking photos of our guests. Following your adventure, you will receive a complimentary digital album with pictures that you can share and post!
Cell phones are strictly prohibited on the Seakart.
What is your inclement weather policy?
Shore weather can be fickle and isolated, causing forecasts to often be inaccurate. We suggest booking your preferred date/time and in the event of inclement weather, we will contact you to reschedule for later that day or another day. The team at Seakart Adventure SC constantly monitor the weather (in real time) to ensure a safe and memorable trip!Seakart Adventure SC reserves the right, at their sole discretion, to cancel any rental due to inclement weather or other unsafe circumstances. Refunds or discounts are not guaranteed for rentals that end early, including due to inclement weather.
What is your cancellation policy?
Reservations must be cancelled at least 24 hours prior to the rental start time to receive full refund. No call/no shows are charged 100% of their reservation. If you arrive after your rental start time, we reserve the right to cancel without refund. If you need to cancel, please contact us as soon as possible. Do not wait until your rental time to cancel.
What if we damage the Seakart?
A major credit card matching the reservation name is required at check-in and will be held during your ride. Before and after every rental, we inspect each Seakart and its equipment. If damage occurs during your rental, you are responsible for the reasonable cost to repair or replace the damaged property. We document any damage and provide an itemized repair invoice, which may include reasonable loss of rental revenue while the Seakart is unavailable for repairs, where permitted by law. Damage invoices may be sent electronically and paid using the payment methods accepted by Seakart Adventure SC.
Should we tip?
The Seakart crew is here to ensure safety and enhance your experience. They pride themselves on customer service and appreciation is welcome. If you enjoy your ride, please feel free to tip your guide!

3. Deep Sea and Inshore Fishing Charters – Reel in the Fun
Murrells Inlet is known as the and one of the best ways to experience it is by heading out on a . Whether you’re a seasoned angler or it’s your first time holding a rod, local captains know exactly where the fish are biting.
Choose from:
🎣 Calm waters, quick trips, and catches like redfish and flounder — ideal for families with kids.
🌊 For those who want a full-day experience chasing snapper, grouper, and even mahi mahi offshore.
Fishing trips are a classic Murrells Inlet tradition and a fantastic way to bond as a family while learning about the local waters.
4. Kayak and Paddleboard Tours – Explore the Marsh at Your Own Pace
If you prefer something a little more peaceful, through the tidal creeks is a must. It’s an up-close way to experience the area’s rich ecosystem, from salt marshes to oyster beds, and you might even spot egrets, herons, or dolphins along the way.

Many sunset cruises also include live music, snacks, and drinks on board, making them a fun and relaxing outing for couples, families, or groups of friends.

For families looking to add a little extra excitement, is another unforgettable experience. Welcome aboard the Super Hawk
Nestled in the south waters of Point Lookout, Long Island is the home port of the Super Hawk — a 100% family-operated business celebrating its 37th season.
Every trip is extremely beginner and family friendly. We take the extra time to teach you the fun and enjoyment of fishing, whether it's your first cast or your thousandth.

Beginner-friendly

Half-day trips daily

Private charters & cruises
Birthdays, family reunions, corporate events, proms and moonlight cruises on Long Island's south shore.
What is the best fishing charter on Long Island?
The Super Hawk is consistently voted Long Island's #1 family-friendly fishing charter — 37 years out of Point Lookout, NY, with bait, tackle, rod and reel all included and a crew that teaches first-timers and kids how to fish.
How much is a Long Island party boat fishing trip?
Half-day party-boat trips on the Super Hawk are $65 adults / $62 seniors / $42 children 15 and under on weekdays, and $67 / $64 / $45 on weekends. No rental fees — rods, reels and bait are included.
What time do the trips sail?
Two half-day sailings every day: AM runs 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM, PM runs 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM. Arrive at least 30 minutes early to park and board.
Do I need a fishing license?
No. New York covers recreational saltwater anglers on a licensed party or charter boat under the vessel's permit — you do not need a personal license to fish with us.
Is the Super Hawk good for families and beginners?
Yes. We're a family-operated business and family-friendly fishing trip — the crew helps kids and first-timers bait up, cast and reel in. There's a clean restroom, an enclosed cabin and a small snack bar on board.
Can I book a private charter or moonlight cruise?
Yes. The Super Hawk hosts private fishing charters, moonlight party cruises, birthdays, reunions and corporate events. Call (516) 607-3004 to check date availability.

TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions | Deep Sea Fishing Charters | Reel Intense Fishing
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
What if the weather is rough the day of our charter?
On windy days, we can fish in the intercoastal waterway where it is geographically protected from the wind and rough seas. If the weather is too extreme, the captain reserves the right to cancel; therefore a full refund of your money will be given.
Can I keep the fish I catch?
Feel free to keep any fish of legal size and limit that is edible. All other fish will be returned as unharmed as possible to the ocean. I will be more than happy to clean and filet the fish you want.
Can I mount my fish?
We are a representative of Gray’s Taxidermy of Fort Lauderdale, the largest taxidermy in the world. We would be more than happy to get you a mount of your fish, delivered right to your home.
Do I need to bring any fishing equipment?
No, we supply all necessary equipment, but feel free to bring any of your own.
Do I need a fishing license?
No. We have all necessary licenses for up to 6 people.
What do I need to bring on board for my day of fishing?
You will want to bring food and beverages, sun block, a camera, polarized sunglasses, a light jacket just in case), and something to bring your catch home in like a freezer Ziploc baggy or cooler.
How long are the charters?
A half-day is four hours, usually 8 a.m. to 12 Noon or 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. A full day is eight hours, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Trip departure times may vary to fit your schedule depending on other charters for the day.
Is rain gear necessary?
Ponchos are sold at the marina’s ship store. It is always a good idea to bring rain gear just in case. As we all know, the weather here in South Florida can be sudden and unexpected.
What payment options do you accept?
We take all major credit cards including American Express, Visa, and MasterCard. However, WE DO NOT take Discover. Checks are welcome, and of course cash.
How do I schedule a fishing charter?
Call us to make sure the day you would like to reserve is available. You must send a deposit via check or credit card in the amount of $100 to ensure that time slot is yours.
Is tipping necessary?
Tips are definitely appreciated, but not mandatory. Normal tips are around 15-20% of the trip cost.
What level of experience is necessary?
We enjoy anglers from age 5 to 105, any experience level. We specialize in teaching kids and inexperienced anglers. When you are done with your fishing trip, We will send you home with knowledge of many secret fishing tips.
Do you offer head-boat (shared) trips, or are all your trips private?
We're a . When you book with Reel Intense Fishing, you reserve the entire boat and captain for your group exclusively. We do not offer head-boat/party-boat trips where individual anglers buy per-person tickets and are paired with other parties. Private charters are a flat rate for the boat (not per-person) and include a customized experience - targeted species, pace, and instruction tailored to your group. If you're looking to join a shared trip, please note we do not coordinate rider matchups.
private charter only
GOT A QUESTION OR CONCERN?
Not a problem! Contact us TODAY and a Reel Intense Fishing expert will get back to you as soon as possible!

=== PAGE: https://www.reelintensefishing.com/excursions
TITLE: Affordable Rates | Reel Intense Fishing Charters Palm Beach, FL
EXCURSIONS
The most exciting fishing adventures at the palm of your hand! Whether you're looking for wreck fishing, inshore fishing, or even kite fishing - Reel Intense has you covered! Each private excursion offers something different including a unique catch, like our shark fishing adventure or our run & gun offshore trip. But an awesome day of fishing isn't all you have to look forward to. A day of adventure in the Bahamas is also on the menu as is an exciting scuba trip or even a Peanut Island Boat Party!
Inshore Fishing Palm Beach
Looking for light tackle action in calm waters? Inshore fishing is the name of your game! The Palm Beach inlet and beaches hold many opportunities. Tarpon, jack crevalle, and barracuda are some of the many free swimming fish to be caught. This is an awesome charter for all ages. There are opportunities to see gentle manatees and check out the monster mansions of Palm Beach Island and Peanut Island. Enjoy!
Kite Fishing for Sailfish, Tuna, Dolphin and Kingfish
Want to feel like a kid again? Come fly a kite with reel intense! Kite fishing was discovered in the early 1980’s. This technique allows you to hang your fishing line off a break away clip attached to the kite rod. When a fish bites, the line breaks away and allows you to fight the fish free and clear. The purpose of kite fishing is to get the bait far away from the boat with no line in the water for fish to see. This method is fun and cool for all ages.
So… go fly a kite!
Bottom Fishing
Hungry? Like action? Bottom fishing is for you! The reef system out in front of Palm Beach, Singer Island and Jupiter, Florida have some of the best bottom structures in south east Florida. This is one of the only places where the gulf stream meets the reef. Mutton’s, yellowtails, mangrove and vermillion snapper make their home here. This private excursion is easy and hands on. Also fun for all ages. Come get some!
Shark Fishing Adventure
You want to catch a shark? Well Reel Intense has you covered. The waters off Palm beach, Singer Island, and Jupiter, Florida are infamous for sharks. “Shark week” is filmed in our waters. We offer the man eating bull shark, majestic lemon sharks, wild looking hammer heads and the high jumping spinner shark. Most of these animals can be targeted all year. It takes a strong will and a strong back to land these bad boys. Are you ready?!
Run & Gun Offshore
Take your private charter to the next level! We offer run & gun fishing. What is run and gun? Well, this method is running far offshore and looking for floating structures in the famous Gulf Stream waters. This could be anything from a floating 5 gallon bucket to massive weed lines. Dolphin, sailfish, wahoo, and blue marlin will be the fish of choice. Trolling and chumming is the method. Be ready to be surrounded by deep blue water. You may even see whales and porpoises, along with sea turtles. Wow!
Bahama Adventure
Ready for adventure! The islands of the Bahamas are just 52 miles away from West Palm Beach. We would literally be traveling to another country so bring your passport and your sense of adventure. Hop aboard one of our custom 35’ center consoles and make the epic crossing of the Gulf Stream to the crystal clear waters off West End, Bahamas. We offer day trips and over night stays. The fishing methods involve trolling for wahoo, dolphin, tuna and blue marlin. Also, we go deep dropping for delicious snapper and grouper to help fill the cooler. These trips are offered in summer months when the waters of the Gulf Stream are calm and tranquil. 4 person max.
Trolling Trips
Trolling is a method where we drive at a slow speed and set lines out of the back of the vessel. Moving around allows us to cover more surface area. Many different sport fish can be caught this way. We use a spread of lures and natural bait. This is a great technique for mahi mahi, sailfish, wahoo and tuna. It’s great on calm hot days of summer, keeping a constant breeze in your face. Fun for all ages and experience levels.
Wreck Fishing
What is wreck fishing? This fishing technique entails dropping a live bait down 200-300 ft. South Florida has hundreds of man made and natural reef systems. What’s good about deep water wrecks is that they’re deep! These structures will hold huge fish. Anything from monster grouper & snapper to rod bending amberjack. We use a heavy rod and reel. When they bite, you better be ready!
Discover Scuba & Snorkeling
Looking for something other then sport fishing? Get adventurous and get under the water! Reel intense has a dive master onboard: her name is Somerville and she is a certified PADI Dive Master. She will teach you the basics and have you feeling like a pro in no time. This is a very safe sport and fun for all ages. This excursion includes all the gear and a private tour exploring the famous “ Blue Haron Bridge with Somerville”
Please Call for details.
Sword-fishing Daytime Charters
Its head! Swordfish are world renowned for their aggressive behavior, when hooked they will actually charge the boat while making acrobatic jumps and deep dives. If you hook a monster, the fight could last hours; This is not for the beginner. It’s an all-day charter beginning with a 20 mile ride out to the swordfish grounds. We use Diawa’s epic 3000 electric reel with a handle for manual reeling. The conditions have to be calm for this type of private charter and we take a maximum of 4 people on this adventure.
Peanut Island Boat Party
Spend a relaxing day out on our beautiful 35ft seavee center console boat, anchored just a few feet from famous Peanut Island. Peanut Island is located just a hundred yards from the ocean. Its waters are clean and clear at high tide. We think it’s the closest thing to being in the Bahamas! Listen to music and lounge in the clean water on a float and let the crew cater to you. Food and drinks are provided. We cook hamburgers and hotdogs for a boat BBQ, it’s a picnic on the water. Wow! Relax, unwind and have fun. Great for all ages.

How long does a half day Royal Gorge rafting trip typically last?
A half day Royal Gorge rafting trip generally lasts for 3-4 hours in total, with approximately 2 hours spent on the river. Performance Tours’ half day Royal Gorge rafting trips allow guests to experience the thrill of whitewater rafting while still having part of their day free for other activities.
Is the half day Royal Gorge whitewater rafting trip appropriate for beginners?
The half day Royal Gorge whitewater rafting trip navigates through adrenaline-pumping class IV+ rapids on the Arkansas River and is considered an advanced rafting experience. First time paddlers and Royal Gorge beginners who are strong swimmers, in good physical condition and ready for a thrilling adventure are welcome to experience the world-class rafting in the Royal Gorge with our experienced raft guides. Guests who are not strong swimmers and/ or are looking for a more relaxed rafting experience, can opt for one of our class III trip options, like
What is the best time of year to experience a half-day Royal Gorge rafting adventure?
While specific dates can vary year to year, the prime season for experiencing a half-day Royal Gorge rafting adventure typically runs from late spring through the summer months. May through early September provides the optimal balance of water levels and weather conditions for Royal Gorge rafting.
Are there age or skill requirements for participating in a half-day Royal Gorge rafting trip?
Yes, there are age and skill requirements for participating in a half-day Royal Gorge rafting trip due to the advanced nature of the whitewater rapids. Participants are usually required to be in good physical condition, and strong swimmers capable of self-rescue. In addition to the rafting skills requirements, we also require that all Royal Gorge guests are at least 16 years old in most conditions, though the minimum age may drop to 14 years during lower flows.
Can you raft the Royal Gorge if you are staying in Breckenridge?
Absolutely! Many of our whitewater rafting guests travel to the Royal Gorge from Breckenridge while on vacation. It is about a two hour drive to the Royal Gorge from Breckenridge, and the drive is very scenic and enjoyable.

Frequently Asked Questions
First time sailing in Newport? Don’t worry. We have compiled everything you need to know to ensure you are ready for a comfortable and memorable experience.
Where do we park?
We’re located on Bowen’s Wharf, an 18th-century wharf and pedestrian thoroughfare. You cannot drive onto Bowen’s Wharf; you need to park and walk onto it.
Bowen’s Wharf is on America’s Cup Avenue. A good address to put into your GPS is 49 America’s Cup Ave which is the address for The Newport Hotel which is next to Bowen’s Wharf.
Once you’re at 49 America’s Cup Ave., you will see the Seamen Church Institute. Just past the Institute, look for the very tall flagpole with all sorts of colorful flags on it. Walk to that flagpole, follow the bricks onto the wharf, and at the foot of the small parking lot you will see our small house and big blue awning which says Sightsailing! Easy!
If you’re driving, there is a small parking lot at Bowen’s Wharf just past 49 America’s Cup Ave that holds about 20 cars. It’s first-come, first-served, and fills up fast.
The largest and least expensive parking garage in Newport is at the Discover Newport Visitor Bureau at 23 America’s Cup Ave. The lot is less than a 1/4 mile or about an 8-minute walk from Bowens Wharf.
The Mooring restaurant located at 1 Sayers Wharf, Newport RI has a large parking lot. There are many other lots and meters along Thames St and America’s Cup Ave. There are also parking meters. These have a three-hour limit which is strictly enforced.

When do tickets for public sails go on sale?
Tickets for Public Sails on Aquidneck go on sale
Once tickets for public sails go on sale for Aquidneck, the dates and times appear in the Book Online section. If you don’t see a boat’s schedule for the season in the Book Online section, look in the Schedules & Rates menu on the website.
What should we bring and wear?
Soft-soled shoes, sneakers, or sandals are fine. If you wear high heels you may need to go barefoot. Bring appropriate gear for going out on the water. In the spring and fall, we recommend a lightweight jacket and a pair of pants. In the summer, unless it’s really hot, you’ll want a jacket or sweatshirt for sunset sails. If you’re sailing during the day, bring sunblock (not tanning oil which makes the decks slippery), and wear a hat.

TITLE: Van Bibber Park | Jefferson County, CO
Van Bibber Park
Van Bibber Park offers an urban get-away as well as a home and migration stop for wildlife. The Van Bibber Creek wetlands provide wildlife habitat, which can be viewed from an observation deck. Visitors enjoy mountain vistas from soft-surface trails that meander through open meadows and a 1.5-mile concrete trail that travels the length of the park and offers accessibility for strollers and wheelchairs.
The new trail segment will connect the Van Bibber Park - Indiana Trailhead, located between W 56th Drive and W 55th Drive in the Golden/Arvada area, to the Fairmount Trail at the base of North Table Mountain Park. This east-west segment is just under two miles long.
This project was highlighted in Goal 9 of the , as an opportunity to connect visitors to 24 miles of trails in Van Bibber and North Table Mountain Parks as well as the Fairmount Trail. This project also supports Goal 8 of the Conservation Greenprint, which provides more equitable and easy access to greenspace within a 10-minute walk or drive from home.
JCOS 2020-2025 Conservation Greenprint (PDF)
Construction on the trail began in August 2025 and will continue for approximately two years. The project timeline is largely subject to the design approval and agreements with local, state, and federal entities, as well as weather conditions, private encroachments, and seasonal construction restrictions. For safety, the project area will be closed to the public during construction.
Three New Bridges Along the Van Bibber Park Corridor
On July 28, 2026, three steel bridges were installed across Van Bibber Creek as part of the Van Bibber Trail Extension project. All three bridges were fabricated in Greeley and were installed using two different cranes. The 63 and 78-foot-long bridges will be part of the regional concrete trails, and the 50-foot-long timber-decked bridge will provide a creek crossing for the adjacent soft-surface trail. There are four more bridges to install and more trail work to complete before opening this regional connection to the public next year.

FAQ
Are The Prices Per Person?
Yes, our prices are per person. Please note that weight restrictions apply. $99 is only applicable per person on the Lakeshore Panorama flight when you are booking for a group of 3 people.
What Do "Weight Restrictions" Mean?
We ask all clients to please provide ACCURATE passenger weights. Our team uses these weights to determine maximum fuel load. Inaccurate reporting of weights may result in a cancellation of the flight due to aircraft availability. Maximum total capacity is 500lbs.
What If The Weather Is Bad?
Your safety and comfort always come first. If we cannot fly due to safety considerations (strong winds, low visibility, or heavy snow), we’ll reschedule your flight at no extra cost.
Is There A Minimum Age For Children To Fly?
Children of all ages are welcome, including infants from 0+. We want your family flight experience to be both safe and memorable, so for our youngest passengers we provide a child seat when needed. During the flight, all passengers (including children and infants) are required to occupy a a seat with seatbelt and aviation headphones.
What Should I Bring?
For your comfort, we recommend close-toed footwear, light jacket, sunglasses, cap, sunblock, and of course, a camera for all the amazing views!
I Received A Gift Certificate But I Don’t Know The Expiry. How Long Do They Last For?
Experience gift certificates are honoured for one (1) year from the date of purchase. If you purchased a monetary value card, there is no expiration date.
I Want To Fly Over My House. How Can I Do It?
We can help organize a custom flight over your home. Contact our team, and we will do our best to plan a personalized flight route for your experience.
What Is The Pilot Experience, And Do I Need Flying Experience To Join?
No experience needed! The Pilot Experience lets you feel what it’s like to be a pilot during a real scenic flight. You’ll sit up front with a professional pilot, enjoy breathtaking views, and even hold the controls. It’s a smooth, safe adventure — and an unforgettable Christmas gift idea for anyone who loves flying or trying something new.
How does the pricing work?
All prices are per person. For example: the 99$ per person Lakeshore Panorama price applies only when you book for a group of 3 people. In that case every person pays $99 and fly all togetehr on one flight. If you only have 2 poeple, the price per person on the Lakeshore Panorama flight will be $149 per person. For one person, the price will be $299. All flights are private, there will be no strangers onboard and it is not possible to join another group.

Corporate Event Is Different.
Does your team roll their eyes when you bring up the idea of a corporate event? The typical “team building experiences,” company picnics, and office parties have largely lost their appeal at most organizations. What you need in order to boost morale, strengthen relationships, and make your team better at what it does is an event that everyone can get excited about. That’s where Charleston Yacht Tours comes in. We guarantee everyone will sit up and listen when you start talking about a trip on the Charleston harbor aboard your own private yacht!
Draw
Inspiration From the Sea
There’s just something about the ocean and the breeze that blows across it that seem to take away all the problems in the world. Has it been a tough year for your business? Thank your team for sticking it out and working long hours by giving them a few hours to feel the waves rocking under them, enjoy a cool drink in the salty breeze, and even jump off the boat into the ocean if they’re so inclined! And there’s no better way to celebrate a milestone than watching the dolphins together from your private boat.
An Outing
They Won’t Forget
The best corporate event is the one that your team can’t stop talking about even weeks after it takes place. The memories that your employees create together on the water will become a powerful force to bind them together, improve their spirit, and show them just how much you appreciate the work they do every day.
Are your boats fully equipped?
Whichever of our four boats you select for your corporate event, you will find that it holds all of the amenities necessary for your group’s comfort. There is a full bathroom on each of our yachts, and we even offer a spectacular speaker system that you can plug your custom soundtrack into. You bring the drinks, and we’ll bring the cooler full of ice to keep them chilled.
What route will our yacht tour take?
Your captain will customize your trip out on the water to perfectly fit your group’s preferences! Perhaps you’re from out of town and you want to be sure to get a great view of all the historical landmarks in the harbor, such as the USS Yorktown and Fort Sumter. Or maybe your priority is simply to enjoy the gorgeous sunset with the backdrop of the Charleston area’s natural beauty. === PAGE: https://charlestonyachttours.com/faqs/
TITLE: Frequently Asked Questions - Charleston Yacht Tours
FAQ's
Whats included?
All of our charter are private, just you and your friends or family. We have a Captain and Mate who assist with everything you need. The boat, fuel, taxes, fees, cooler, and ice are all included in the price.
Where do we park?
Our marina has a free guest lot for parking.
What sights can we see on a Charleston boat tour?
You’ll enjoy views of Charleston’s most famous landmarks, including The Battery, Ravenel Bridge, the USS Yorktown, Fort Sumter, Fort Moultrie, Fort Johnson, Castle Pinckney, Waterfront Park, the South Carolina Aquarium, and beautiful historic homes and churches—all from the water. Plus, there’s plenty more to discover along the harbor!
Do the boats have bathrooms?
YES. All our vessels except the Skiff have bathrooms on board.
Do you provide food and drinks on the boat?
We do not serve food or drinks directly, but we work with trusted catering partners who can deliver meals to the boat before your trip. You are also welcome to bring your own food and beverages. Coolers and ice are provided on board for your convenience.
Are glass bottles allowed?
We allow glass but recommend other options for your safety.
Can we bring additional guests?
No. For safety reasons, Coast Guard regulations determine the maximum capacity for each boat, and we cannot exceed these limits.
Where are the boats?
All boats except the skiff are at Ripley Light Yacht Club. Less than 2 minutes from Downtown.
What happens in bad weather?
Weather conditions in Charleston can shift quickly. Short rain showers usually pass within 15–20 minutes, and we often adjust departure times to avoid them. The Captain will make the final safety decision on the day of your charter. If the trip cannot run due to weather, you will receive a full refund.
Can we swim during the charter?
Yes—swimming is allowed on charters that are 3 hours or longer. The currents in Charleston Harbor can be strong, so we only stop at designated safe locations. For safety reasons, we cannot allow swimming just anywhere in the harbor.
Are guests allowed to bring floats on the boat?
Absolutely! You’re welcome to bring your own floats, and we also have floats available on board for guests who want to use them.
Are there extra taxes and fees?
The price advertised is the price you pay. We include a 15% tip that goes entirely to the crew.
How do we pay?
You can book and pay right on our website at Our Fleet, email us, or call and we can book you. We accept all credit cards.
Do you take deposits?
Yes. You can pay in full or make a deposit. The balance is due the week before the trip.
Is there a stereo on board?
Yes. All Charleston Yacht Tours boats are equipped with high-quality Bluetooth stereos that you can easily connect to.
Can you pick us up at a different location?
Yes. We have several pickup locations available around Charleston. Please note that we charge for the additional travel time required for the boat to get to and from your chosen location.
Do you have a phone charger?
Sometimes you may luck out. But most Charters you will not be able to charge your phone.
How early should we get to the marina?
Plan to arrive at least 15 minutes before your charter starts. The walk down the dock takes a few minutes, and arriving early makes boarding easy and stress-free.
Can we book your boats for a wedding?
Absolutely. We host a wide range of wedding charters—ceremonies, photos, celebrations, and more. Give us a call and we’ll help you plan the perfect experience.
Whats the craziest thing that has happened?
All our charters are private we don't share with others. Your secrets will be safe with us.

Weather

Cancelation

Damage

Common Offshore Species Near Dania Beach
Snapper
Snapper fishing is excellent year-round in our area. We bottom fish around wrecks and reefs, frequently catching yellowtail, mutton, and vermilion snapper—each offering great action and even better table fare.
Wahoo
Wahoo are a top-tier catch for sushi lovers, offering some of the best-tasting fish in the ocean. Although they’re available year-round, October and full moon periods are especially productive. We catch them by high-speed trolling near wrecks.
Sharks
We catch a variety of BIG shark species, including bull, tiger, nurse, lemon, and hammerhead sharks. These waters are especially known for seasonal migrations of very large hammerhead sharks, offering exciting opportunities for sport fishing.
King Mackerel
King mackerel, or “kingfish,” are available year-round and are most abundant in the spring. These fish patrol the shallow inner reefs close to the beach and are popular for smoking into delicious fish dips.
Sailfish
Sailfish are a prized catch in our waters. We target these stunning, high-speed predators with live bait. Known for their acrobatics and beauty, sailfish offer an unforgettable fishing experience.
Grouper
Fort Lauderdale offers outstanding grouper fishing during the open season May - December. We target these powerful bottom dwellers while wreck fishing, most commonly catching black and gag grouper.
Blackfin Tuna
Blackfin tuna fishing is excellent in the winter and spring. We typically target them on afternoon trips, as they rise in the water column as the sun sets. Fast trolling near wrecks is our go-to method for getting on the bite.
Mahi Mahi
Mahi Mahi are among the most sought-after fish for both their taste and vibrant appearance. The peak season is during the summer when offshore schools are most active.

All offshore fishing charters depart from Dania Beach, Florida. This location offers quick access to offshore fishing grounds and is convenient for guests staying in Hollywood and nearby Fort Lauderdale.

Nature-based education teaches us how to be good stewards of our environment and the natural world around us. In Action
Healthy coastal habitats play a critical role in all our lives by protecting us from storms, helping to keep our drinking water clean, and supporting the economy through boating, fishing, and tourism.
Marine Discovery Center believes in conservation-in-action where YOU play a key role in helping to protect biological diversity, maintain and restore critical habitat and help prevent loss of species, no matter where you live, work or play.

Discover Amazing
Repeated, meaningful experiences in nature help develop a sense of place, a sense of connection, and a sense of community. These experiences reveal the relationship we have with the natural world and the importance of conserving it.
Marine Discovery Center invites you to explore the diverse wildlife and beauty of the Indian River Lagoon on one of our expertly guided boat and kayak eco-tours. Led by a certified Florida Master Naturalist, these excursions will give you an up-close and personal look at one of North America’s most biodiverse ecosystems, which is home to more than 4,000 species of plants and animals, including the Atlantic bottlenose dolphin, Florida manatee, horseshoe crabs, coastal birds, and a wide variety of fish and other important organisms.

What are your hours of operation?

Can I save money if I want to rent frequently?

Do you provide life jackets?
We will provide life jackets for every member of your party (except any four-legged friends you choose to bring).
Do I need boating experience?

Fish Species We Catch
Sailfish
Sailfish live in colder areas of the seas. They are predominantly blue to gray in color and have a characteristic dorsal fin known as a sail, which often stretches the entire length of the back.
Tuna
Atlantic bluefins are native to both the western and eastern Atlantic Ocean, as well as the Mediterranean Sea. A close relative of the other two bluefin tuna species—the Pacific bluefin tuna and the southern bluefin tuna.
Mahi
The mahi-mahi or common dolphinfish is a surface-dwelling ray-finned fish found in off-shore temperate, tropical, and subtropical waters worldwide. Also widely called dorado and dolphin.
Wahoo
Wahoo is a scombrid fish found worldwide in tropical and subtropical seas. It is best known to sports fishermen, as its speed and high-quality flesh makes it a prized game fish.
King Mackerel
The king mackerel or kingfish, is a migratory species of mackerel of the western Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico. It is an important species to both the commercial and recreational fishing industries.
Bonito
Bonitos are a tribe of medium-sized, ray-finned predatory fish in the family Scombridae – a family it shares with the mackerel, tuna, and Spanish mackerel tribes, and also the butterfly kingfish.
Grouper
Groupers are fish of any of a number of genera in the subfamily Epinephelinae of the family Serranidae, in the order Perciformes. Not all serranids are called ‘groupers’; the family also includes the sea basses.
Barracuda
A barracuda is a large, predatory ray-finned fish known for its fearsome appearance and ferocious behavior.
Spanish Mackerel
The Atlantic Spanish mackerel is a migratory species of mackerels that swims to the Northern Gulf of Mexico in spring, returns to south Florida in the Eastern Gulf, and to Mexico in the Western Gulf in the fall.
Sharks
Sharks are a group of elasmobranch fish characterized by a cartilaginous skeleton, five to seven gill slits on the sides of the head, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
Blue Marlin
The Atlantic blue marlin is a species of marlin endemic to the Atlantic Ocean. It is closely related to, and usually considered conspecific with, the Indo-Pacific blue marlin, then simply called blue marlin.
Cobia
The cobia is a species of carangiform marine fish, the only extant representative of the genus Rachycentron and the family Rachycentridae. Other common names include black kingfish, black salmon, ling, lemonfish, crabeater, prodigal son, codfish and black bonito.
Amberjack
Amberjack is an Atlantic and Pacific fish in the genus Seriola of the family Carangidae. They are a game fish, most often found in the warmer parts of the oceans.

The Reef · 4 NM Offshore
Alligator Reef Lighthouse by boat from Islamorada.
A working screw-pile lighthouse from 1873 standing in four feet of water on Alligator Reef, one of the most beginner-friendly snorkel spots in the Florida Keys. Our marina at Breezy Palms is the closest rental dock to the reef.
Alligator Reef sits just offshore of Islamorada, outside the Hawk Channel reef line. From our dock at Breezy Palms, it's a 10-minute run in any of the fleet. Open Atlantic water, so we check the wind forecast with you before you head out.
The lighthouse is named after the , a schooner that grounded on the reef in 1822. The current and is the second-tallest lighthouse in the Keys. Three mooring buoys sit directly around the lighthouse for snorkelers, maintained by the . We mark them on the chart for you before you leave the dock.
USS Alligator
structure was built in 1873
Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
Around the base: hawksbill turtles, parrotfish, sergeant majors, the occasional nurse shark. Visibility runs 30 to 80 feet most days. Bring fins, mask, and snorkel. We sell basic kits at the dock, but most guests bring their own.

The Sandbar · 15 Minutes Out
The Islamorada sandbar. Bay side, anchor up, get in.
A wide shallow flat off Holiday Isle, about 20 minutes from our marina. The sandbar is where Islamorada spends Saturday: boats anchored stem to stern at slack tide, coolers out, music going. Weekdays are quiet enough to bring kids.
From Breezy Palms, the sandbar run is about 20 minutes and suitable for any boat in the fleet. At low tide the bottom is firm enough to stand on. At high tide you'll want a noodle or a tube.
Bring sunscreen, water, food, and drinks for the cooler. A Bluetooth speaker is nice if you want music; most boats in the fleet pair fine. The boat comes with an anchor and line, life jackets, and a basic cooler. Cell service is spotty on the bay, so set everyone's location-share at the dock and bring a waterproof case for your phone.
Larger groups (bachelorette, birthday, family reunion) usually book the 25-foot Hurricane deck boats: #03, #04, #07. Twelve guests, shade, a table, and a swim ladder. Reserve early. These book first on summer weekends.

=== PAGE: https://marker26boatrental.com/blog/how-boat-clubs-work-in-florida-fees-reservations-and-what-to-ask/
TITLE: How Florida Boat Clubs Work: Fees & Reservations | Marker 26
Boat clubs have spread across Florida fast over the past decade, and the pitch is easy to understand: all the boating, none of the ownership. If you’ve never joined one, though, the model raises fair questions. What does a actually include? What do you pay beyond the dues? And how do you avoid a club that promises the water but delivers a waiting list? This guide walks through the whole model, including the one number that separates great clubs from frustrating ones.
boat club membership
The Basic Model
Every club runs on the same trade. The club buys, insures, stores, and maintains a fleet of boats. Members pay a one-time entry fee to join, then monthly dues to stay. In return, members reserve boats from the fleet and use them as their own for the day.
You skip everything that makes ownership expensive and tedious. No slip fees, no repair bills, no depreciation, no trailer, no storage decisions. You book a boat, show up, and go boating. When you return, the staff handles cleaning, fueling, and upkeep for the next member.
What You Pay
Costs come in three layers. The entry fee comes first, a one-time payment that buys your place in the fleet. Across the Tampa Bay area that number typically runs $3,000 to $7,000, though it varies widely by club. Marker 26 sets initiation at $1,250.
Monthly dues come second, usually $250 to $400 depending on the club and the tier. Our own tiers sit at the bottom of that range, at $200 per month for weekday access and $250 per month for full seven-day access. Dues cover insurance, storage, maintenance, cleaning, and safety equipment. Many clubs also include orientation and basic training, so new boaters leave the dock with real confidence.
Fuel comes third, and it stays separate almost everywhere. You pay for what you burn on your trips, and nothing more. Some clubs also offer an optional damage waiver for a small monthly add-on, which caps your out-of-pocket exposure if something goes wrong on the water.
How Reservations Work
This part varies more than anything else, so read any club’s policy closely. Typical systems let members book online within a rolling window, often two to four weeks out. Many clubs separate prime time, meaning weekends and holidays, from off-peak weekdays, then limit how many prime slots a member can hold at once.
On paper, every reservation system looks reasonable. On the water, the experience depends entirely on one thing: how many members share each boat.
What About a Boating License?
Florida law requires anyone born on or after January 1, 1988 to carry a boating safety education ID card to operate a powered vessel. Clubs and rental operations handle this in a couple of ways, so ask how yours does it. Some accept a temporary certificate, which involves a short test you can complete before your first trip. Others walk members through the full course as part of onboarding. Either way, a good club never hands the wheel to someone unprepared. Orientation on the specific boats, the local channels, and the no-wake zones should come standard.
What Your First Trip Looks Like
Joining a club feels abstract until the first reservation, so let’s make it concrete. You book a boat online for Saturday morning. You arrive at the dock 10 to 15 minutes early, where staff have the boat clean, fueled, and loaded with safety equipment. You get a quick rundown of conditions, tide timing, and route suggestions based on where you want to go.
Then you leave the dock and the day belongs to you. Beach at Caladesi, sandbar at Three Rooker, lunch on the Intracoastal, whatever the plan calls for. When you return, you tie up, grab your cooler, and head home. The staff handles everything after that. No trailer line at the ramp, no engine flush in the driveway, no Sunday spent scrubbing.
The Number That Makes or Breaks a Club
Ask any club one question before you sign anything: what is your member-to-boat ratio? Large national clubs commonly run ten to fifteen members per boat, and some push higher. At those ratios, the math turns against you every sunny Saturday. Too many members want the same handful of weekend mornings, and somebody loses. Usually the newest member.
A low ratio changes everything. Fewer members per boat means real availability, shorter booking windows, and the freedom to boat on impulse instead of by appointment. It costs the club more to run, which explains why so few clubs commit to it.
Questions to Ask Before You Join
Bring this list to any club you’re considering, ours included:
What is the member-to-boat ratio, in writing?
How far in advance can I book, and how many reservations can I hold at once?
What are the prime-time rules for weekends and holidays?
What happens if weather cancels my day?
What do I owe if a boat gets damaged, and can I add a damage waiver?
How long is the contract, and what does it take to leave?
Which boats does my tier include, and can guests join me on board?
A quality club answers every one of these without flinching. Hesitation on the ratio question tells you where the availability problems live.
How Marker 26 Does It
We built our club in around the availability problem, because we’d heard the same story from too many boaters burned by oversold clubs. Our club caps the number of members across the fleet, which guarantees fast boat access instead of a lottery. Membership costs $1,250 to join, then $200 per month for weekday access or $250 per month for all seven days. Fuel is the only other cost.
Members boat from a dock that sits minutes by water from Honeymoon Island, Caladesi Island, Three Rooker, and . Our team has lived and boated here for decades, so route suggestions, tide guidance, and weather calls come from people who know these waters channel by channel. A boat club membership here works the way the model was always meant to: reserve, show up, boat.
Is the Model Right for You?
A boat club membership fits boaters who get out regularly, want zero maintenance in their lives, and value their weekends too much to spend them at a service counter. It fits new boaters especially well, since training and staff support remove the intimidation factor that keeps so many people off the water.
It fits less well for daily boaters, tournament anglers, and anyone who wants to customize a hull. Those boaters should own, and we’ll tell them so.
If you’re near Palm Harbor and want to see how a boat club membership works in person, come by . We’ll show you the boats, hand you the ratio in writing, and let you judge the model from the dock instead of a brochure.

=== PAGE: https://tremblantnautique.com/en/rules-for-rental-of-all-motorized-boats/
TITLE: Nautical Centre Regulations | Tremblant Nautique
RULES
Rules for rental of all motorized boats
Inspection of the boat and the engine will be done in your presence upon departure and at your return.
Credit card security deposit of $1000. On-site you must present the same credit card used to make your reservation and show a matching piece of government ID with the same name.
All damages to the boat, the engine or any of its components are the sole responsibility of the renter. Smoking is forbidden on all boats.
Approaching the shore will cause damage to the boat and its engine, watch for shallow waters!
Stay at least 100 meters (350 feet) from shore.
Stay at least 100 meters from all buoys. Never pass between the channel marker and the shore line. Respect the buoys on your left on departure and arrival at the dock.
When returning to the dock, reduce speed to minimum in the no wake zone. An attendant will help you dock the boat.
It is strictly forbidden not to dock on the banks. All grounds, beaches, docks, trampolines and water games are private. You will be charged a fine, if we receive a complaint from the owners and if we have to go to the lake to warn you.
Respect the environment. Do not throw garbage overboard, a garbage can would be at your disposal upon arrival.
For safety reasons, glass containers are not recommended on the boat.
Pleasure Craft Operator Card
In Quebec and the rest of Canada, all operators of a motorized pleasure craft must have proof of competency in their possession. Proof of competency is mandatory, regardless of the age, length of the boat or the strength and type of engine used.
Protection of Tremblant Lake
The Watersport Center is actively committed to preserving the water quality of Tremblant Lake and promoting respect among all lake users. We believe it is essential to encourage responsible boating practices in order to ensure harmonious coexistence between boaters, swimmers, athletes, and nature enthusiasts.
Promoting ethical navigation and the responsible use of our watercraft is one of our top priorities. We encourage our guests to adopt respectful and safe boating habits adapted to the different areas of the lake, with particular attention given to reducing wake near shorelines, respecting speed limits, and protecting natural environments.
Our support for the Association of Tremblant Lake is especially important to us. Many environmental and community-related challenges affecting water quality and the preservation of this exceptional ecosystem require constant attention and collective involvement.
By working together with the community and local organizations, we hope to actively contribute to protecting this magnificent lake so that future generations may continue to enjoy the natural beauty and unique character of Tremblant Lake.
Recommandations
The good practices of boaters
Make sure you have an appropriately sized PFD for each person on board. Your PFD can save your life. Wear it!
Do not consume alcohol or drugs. Driving while impaired is illegal. Did you know that you could lose your driver's license? We suggest a designated driver who can ensure your safety.
Check your safety equipment with our team. Before each departure, make sure that the required equipment works properly.
The WaterSport Center checks the weather conditions before your departure, however we ask you to be vigilant. On the water, the weather can change quickly. Don't be surprised!
The good practices
Reduce your speed near the shores and on your departure and arrival at the quay of the Water Sport Center and respect the speed zones imposed on the bodies of water.
Please be aware that you are legally responsible for the impact of the wave produced by your boat.
Respect the safety distances with swimmers and non-motorized boats or standing boats.
Be courteous: respect local residents and other boaters by reducing the noise and waves produced.
Nautical sports
The practice of nautical activity generating large waves is recommended more than 100 meters from the shore and in an area that is more than 5 meters deep in order to limit your impact on the environment and other users.
Rely on the recommendations of the Nautical Center regarding the speed of your boat when practicing a towed nautical activity. When you are less than 30 meters from another boat: reduce your wave, refrain from acrobatics, repeated circling, intentional capsizing and jumping using the waves of other boats.
When practicing a towed nautical activity (wake, surf, ski, Tube , trippe), make sure you have a lookout, a place on board and enough PFD at all times for each person towed.
Environment
Avoid navigating and anchoring in sensitive natural areas to preserve endangered or protected species.
Respect water bodies, it is strictly forbidden to throw your products or waste into the water of Lac Tremblant. Trash and recycling bags are offered to you during your rental.

Seating

Coming from Anchorage?

Gear
