Have you ever been on a lake and the wind comes up only to find you’re going the wrong way or can’t keep the boat into the wind? Our instructors will teach you how to steer the boat so this is never a problem again. You’ll remember this for the rest of your life.
Our guides are first aid certified, certified in their sports and carry industrial quality VHF portable radios should we require assistance.
WHAT SHOULD I BRING TO GO CANOEING OR KAYAKING?
Depending on the weather and activity we
recommend
Short sleeve t-shirts
Short pants
Comfortable shoes
Suntan lotion
Sunglasses
A hat
A camera
As mountain weather changes quickly a warm sweater or wind shell and shell pants are a good idea. Food is not included in the tours unless prearranged so consider bringing a light snack and some water.
Learn More
WILL THE RIVER BE HARD FOR ME TO PADDLE?
One of the great aspects of the River of Golden Dreams is you’re going with the flow of the water, not alot of paddling, some steering yes but it doesn’t have to be a workout unless you want it to be. Always check the before you go.
river conditions
HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO PADDLE THE RIVER?
We list the River of Golden Dreams as a 3 hour round trip. Water time is 2 to 2.5 hours. This all depends on river water flows and how much you paddle. Our trip starts out on Alta Lake which allows you to ‘warm up’ and get used to your boat’. Typical guests cant’ wait to get out on the water, paddle like crazy for a few minutes then kick back and enjoy the view, then paddle a bit more. It takes 20-30 minutes of easy paddling to get to the river entrance. River time is about 1 ¼ to 1 ¾ of an hour. This all depends on how fast or slow the river is flowing. Guests who are keen for a work out and are actively paddling will do the trip much faster. We have lots of options for them to maximize their trip time. i.e. Paddle down to the south end of Alta Lake and around the far shore or out and around Green Lake. Spring and fall paddlers get unlimited time out on the water, bring a lunch and speak to us for more details on this.
DO YOU OFFER CUSTOM OR SPECIAL TOURS?
Backroads Whistler has provided customized experiences and memories ever since we started in 1985. We have refined our list of activities to what most of our customers do most of the time. Have a fun idea? Let us know and we will try to make it happen!
DO I NEED A GUIDE?
Do you have some paddling experience? If not you need a guide. Do you find that when you are paddling on a lake you get blown around in the wind? Yes you need a guide. Our guides will teach you paddling techniques that you will enjoy on the river and wherever you may paddle. Little or no paddling experience – Yes you need a guide. Family with small children – Yes you need a guide.
“I am so glad you recommended the guide for us. It really made the tour special” is the feedback we regularly receive from guests!
WHAT IF I CAN'T SWIM?
All our guests are provided with life jackets that are approved by the Canadian Department of Transportation. In the unlikely event that you should fall in the water our jackets will bring you to the surface. Our are trained in boat handling and safety as well as some that are trained life guards and instructors in these types of sports
Please let our staff know before departure if you or anyone else going on the trip cannot swim.
WHAT IF I HAVEN'T BEEN IN A CANOE OR KAYAK BEFORE?
Hiring one of our will get you straight in the canoe or kayak and quickly up the learning curve. Backroads offers tours and instruction for all abilities.
DO I HAVE TO PADDLE BACK UP THE RIVER?
No. You do not! When you get to the end of the River of Golden Dreams, we have a shuttle bus to take you back to Lakeside Park or Whistler Village.
WHAT'S THE BEST TIME OF YEAR TO PADDLE THE RIVER?
vary every day. Up here, high in the mountains the winter snow pack and spring/summer/fall temperatures combine to change water levels in the river up to a meter (3 feet) in 24 hours.
River conditions
In early summer the water can be running quite well, guides are definitely recommended.
Once the winter snow pack has melted (early August) water levels drop considerably and the river becomes very mellow. Still, you never know what’s around the next corner, whether it be a beaver dam to swhoosh over, birds bursting off the water in front of your boat or a bear on the river bank. This is one of the fun aspect of this river, it’s different every time you paddle it and people come back year after year to paddle this river.
ARE THERE BATHROOMS AT LAKESIDE PARK?
There are bathrooms at
Lakeside
park. The bathrooms are to the lookers left as you walk into the park located beside the concession building.
CAN YOU PURCHASE FOOD AT LAKESIDE PARK?
You can buy pre-packaged snacks, ice cream, and drinks at the Backroads Whistler concession building. In addition to food, you can rent canoes, kayaks, and paddle boards.
WHAT IS A PADDLEBOARD?
A paddle board or SUP (Stand Up Paddleboard) is similar to a surfboard but is much larger. Paddle boards are usually 10-14 feet (3-4 meters) or longer and very wide and stable. This makes it easier to stand up and paddle around on the board, making it a great way to spend a day on the water.
WHAT IS A PEDAL BOAT?
A pedal boat is a boat in which you use your legs to propel the boat through the water with a pedaling motion. The pedals turn a propeller that then pushes you forward in the water. Pedal boats are very stable in the water and are easy to operate.
ARE MOTORBOATS ALLOWED ON ALTA LAKE?
Yes, only electric motorboats are allowed on Alta Lake. There is a 12km/h speed limit, so anything larger than a trolling motor is overkill.
ARE SAILBOATS ALLOWED ON ALTA LAKE?
Sailboats are allowed on Alta Lake. The
Whistler Sailing Association
has lessons and learn-to-sail programs.

History
In the early 1900s when Whistler was known as Alta Lake, Rainbow Lodge was the premier fishing resort west of the Rocky Mountains. Guests would come in great numbers just to experience the incomparable summer hiking, swimming, fishing and down the River of Golden Dreams.
boat trips
To this day, the river has remained one of Whistler’s unspoiled jewels. Little to no development has occurred on its riverbanks, lending a great opportunity for resort guests to see how Whistler balances its human development while preserving nature.
The river is alive with fish and critters such as beaver and mink playing in the water. The riverbanks are lined with wildflowers and birds that burst off the water in front of your boat and dart across your path from tree to tree. If you look up you’re likely to see an osprey or bald eagle soaring high overhead with the glacier-capped mountain peaks in the background.
If you stay on the lake, most guests go out for an hour. Alta Lake remains a summer paradise for recreation. It is primarily a non-powered recreational lake (no water skiing or wakeboarding); so there is no noise from engines, smoke on the water or oil slicks. In fact, Alta Lake is much like it was back in the 1900s.
We have a variety of boats specifically designed for the water ways you’ll be paddling on. Quality equipment and great staff. Yes, Life Jackets are included. The views of the ski hills and surrounding mountains is spectacular. And yes if you are just over an hour no problem we’ll prorate your time so you only pay for time used.
Step back in time and join our adventure for a day, a week or a lifetime and make your stay in Whistler an unforgettable experience.
We hope to see you soon.

Is tandem skydiving safe?
.Tandem Skydiving was designed to introduce the general public to our sport in the safest way possible. Statistically, Tandem skydiving is far less dangerous then every day activities such as driving on the highway.
How long is the freefall?
Once you are geared up and loaded into the aircraft, you can expect a scenic through the Columbia valley. Once the door opens be prepared for about . Your Canopy flight is approximately 5 minutes.
What if my parachute doesn't work?
By regulatory standards, when equipment is made for skydiving it must have two parachutes: one is your primary parachute and the second parachute is your emergency backup.
What is the difference between AGL and ASL?
(Above Ground Level) and (Above Sea Level) are terms used to measure altitude in aviation. AGL refers to the height of an object or aircraft above the ground directly beneath it, providing a local perspective. When a Skydive business advertises 13,000 feet, you may want to ask is that AGL or ASL, as this can make an appreciable difference in your skydive experience.
What are the Dos and Don'ts of Skydiving?
: Wear comfortable, flexible athletic gear (yoga pants, sweatpants, t-shirts).: Have a normal meal 1-2 hours before and drink water to stay hydrated.: Arrive on time to complete paperwork and training.: Arch your back into a “banana” shape for stability.: Goggles can fit over glasses.: Skip restrictive clothing, like jeans, or loose items that can catch the wind.: Do not drink or consume drugs for at least 24 hours prior; your jump will be cancelled.: Leave jewelry, hats, and scarves at home.

Rules:

TITLE: Bonnie and Clyde Guide: Movies, Books & TV Series
Bonnie and Clyde Media Guide: Movies, Books, and TV Series
Explore the Legacy of Bonnie and Clyde Through Film, Literature, and TV
Last Update: Aug 06, 2025
7432
Few stories from America’s past capture the imagination like that of Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow. The infamous criminal duo, active during the Great Depression, remains iconic figures in pop culture. Their two-year crime spree of bank robberies, small-store hold-ups, and occasional murders turned them into legends, earning fascination for their daring escapes and tragic end.
For decades, Bonnie and Clyde have inspired countless adaptations across movies, TV series, books, and documentaries. This guide provides an in-depth look at the significant media exploring their lives, offering a resource for fans, researchers, and anyone intrigued by their story.
Movies and TV Series About Bonnie and Clyde
Bonnie and Clyde's story leapt from real-life headlines to Hollywood screens, creating some of the most memorable crime dramas in film history. The following are standout representations of the duo in cinema and television.
One of the first dramatizations of Bonnie Parker's life, this gritty film focuses on a fictionalized version of her criminal rise in the 1930s. Set in the Southwest, the movie portrays Bonnie (played by Dorothy Provine) as a ruthless gang leader. While less historically accurate, it offers a sharp noir-style take on her story.
Directed by Arthur Penn, this award-winning film is a cultural milestone. Starring Warren Beatty as Clyde and Faye Dunaway as Bonnie, the movie follows their ill-fated romance and crime spree. Known for its innovative storytelling and groundbreaking depiction of violence, won two Academy Awards and cemented the duo as legends in Hollywood.
This comedic take on the Bonnie and Clyde narrative provides a satirical, light-hearted parody of the original 1967 film. Set in Italy, it gives a playful nod to the tale while diverging significantly from their real-life story.
This documentary-style TV episode focuses on the romantic and tragic elements of Bonnie and Clyde’s lives. While short, it highlights their public fascination as a star-crossed criminal couple.
Starring Emile Hirsch and Holliday Grainger, this two-part TV mini-series offers a dramatization of the outlaw’s lives. Known as it attempts to balance accounts of their personal lives with the crimes that cemented their infamy.
This PBS documentary steps away from Hollywood glamorization, exploring the historical and societal context of Bonnie and Clyde’s crime spree. The protagonists are examined from a more human and documentary-based perspective.
Featuring Kevin Costner and Woody Harrelson, this Netflix film tells the story from the perspective of the Texas Rangers who hunted the couple. Rather than glorifying Bonnie and Clyde, the movie shines a spotlight on Frank Hamer and Maney Gault, the lawmen leading the chase.
This 57-minute documentary provides an insightful recounting of the duo’s life, complete with analysis and historical context.
A concise, 44-minute documentary examining the couple’s mysterious allure and their place in Depression-era folklore.
Books Featuring Bonnie and Clyde
The literary world has also explored Bonnie and Clyde’s story from multiple angles, creating in-depth narratives based on historical research, personal accounts, and fresh insights. Below, we highlight the most notable books revealing their lives.
by Karen Blumenthal
Award-winning journalist Karen Blumenthal peels back the myths to uncover the duo’s real lives. Through meticulous research, her narrative chronicles their upbringing, romantic connection, and notoriety. Both historically rich and highly engaging, it’s ideal for readers wanting an authentic account of the couple.
by Phillip Steele and Marie Barrow Scoma
Written with input from Clyde Barrow's youngest sister, Marie Barrow, this book dives deep into the familial side of Bonnie and Clyde. Offering rare photographs and diary entries, it gives a unique inside view of the Barrow gang’s life.
by Paul Schneider
Schneider brings depth and drama to Bonnie and Clyde’s story by grounding it in archival research and first-hand interviews. A detailed, non-fiction account, this work portrays the duo in a more raw, humanized light.
by Jeff Guinn
A vivid, well-researched biography, Jeff Guinn’s book challenges the glamorized versions of their lives. Readers gain a nuanced picture of Bonnie and Clyde as flawed, ambition-driven individuals defined by desperate ambition and poor decisions.
by John Neal Phillips
This account focuses on Ralph Fults, a key member of the Barrow gang. It provides not only a look at the duo but also insights into their accomplices, showing the web of relationships that shaped their story.
by Blanche Barrow
Blanche Barrow, the wife of Clyde’s brother Buck, presents her firsthand account as part of the outlaw crew. Her memoir offers a raw, personal perspective of life on the run. Supplemented by historical research, this is a crucial read for anyone wanting firsthand insight.
Bonnie and Clyde FAQ

The Lasting Legacy
Whether you view Bonnie and Clyde as folk heroes, criminals, or tragic figures, their story continues to resonate almost a century later. Through Hollywood films, in-depth biographies, and documentaries, their legacy remains a fascinating blend of myth, romance, and reality.

Departing from Lake Washington Park
Dont be misled! This is not a boat ride around a lake! This tour departs from the east side of Lake Washington and proceeds north as you enjoy the beauty of the lake as you look for gators on the bank. We continue to the north end of the lake to our airboat trails through the reeds to the northwest corner of the lake into the river basin proceeding up over the airboat slide at the dam to the vast swamps and marshes to the north.

A Little Bit About Us...
At Airboat Rides Melbourne, we offer unforgettable guided tours through Florida’s breathtaking wetlands—starting with sunrise adventures and continuing through the sunlit day. Whether you’re watching gators bask in the heat or spotting rare birds in flight, every ride promises thrilling wildlife encounters and stunning scenery. Our modern, 13-passenger airboats glide into places other boats can’t reach, giving you a front-row seat to nature’s wonders. Located just a short drive from Orlando and the Space Coast, we’re your perfect escape from the theme park crowds.
FAQ
What makes our tours outstanding?
Our tours are personal and privately narrated with no more than seven of your family members or close friends! (They’re not just another boat ride down the middle of the river with a bunch of strangers!) All of our Captains grew up on the local marshes and wetlands and will take you on a TOUR of Florida`s real outback. We stop along your TOUR to tell you about the history of the river, the Florida alligators life cycle, their mating rituals, how we hunt them, the different birds on the marsh and to take pictures of the wildlife and of your group with a swampy background! We do the cheapest 30 minute “boat rides” on the Spacecoast but our specialty is small personal and privately narrated TOURS catered to your specific desires from one to four hours. We provide hearing protection, water, and a camera (in case you forget yours).
Is there a guarantee we'll see alligators?
Since our tours are in the wild (not an alligator farm) we cannot guarantee you that you will see alligators during your airboat tour but we can guarantee you that we will make every effort possible to show you alligators. Our Airboat captains have many years of experience and normally know where to go to find them, but since alligators roam the wild each tour is unpredictable and unique. Since alligators are cold blooded reptiles they are very temperature sensitive so there are certain months and days that we see more than others. If your only goal is to see an alligator ask before booking and we’ll be glad to tell you what their recent activity has been.
When is the best time of year to take an Airboat Tour?
Anytime of the year is a great time to take an airboat tour in Central Florida! The Spring is incredible with all of the trees and plants blooming (adding vibrant colors to the already phenomenal landscape) and the alligators sounding off and displaying their mating rituals. Summertime is warm and humid which brings the alligators out early in the morning and late in the evening along with the Great Blue Herring and the beautiful White Egrets. Fall is spectacular with very pleasant weather with cool mornings and evenings and an abundance of animals and beautiful foliage. Florida`s mild winters are a great time of year as well bringing out the fur-bearing (fuzzy) animals, like deer, otters and the migratory birds. Being cold blooded, the alligators stay in the water on the bottom as long as the water is warmer than the air but as soon as the sun comes up and the air temperature gets warmer than the water temperature they begin to crawl out on the banks to warm their bodies. This is the best time of the year to get up close for some great pictures of the gators on the bank as they are somewhat lathargic. The mornings and evenings can be a bit chilly so midday tours are a bit more comfortable and the gators are up on the banks warming up!
Are mosquitoes a problem in the swamp?
No, not really. Normally, at dawn, the mosquitos find a place to hide in the foliage and they stay there until dusk. As long as the airboat motor is running the propeller moves enough air to keep them at bay. However, it is recommended that you take precautionary measures by applying mosquito repellent as necessary.
How old do you have to be to ride on the tours?
All ages are welcome on our tours! (However, we don’t recommend that you bring infants unless your group rents the whole boat as we cannot turn around and come back if the child becomes unhappy.) Captain Mike really enjoys having the children and taking pictures of them in the drivers seat with his cap! Seniors also enjoy our tours as the boat is easy to board, very stable and dry. We do a lot of “bucket list” tours!
Will I get wet?
You might get an occassional light spray.
What should I bring?
Sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat or cap if you desire, bottled water, camera, a light jacket or windbreaker it the temperature is below 75 degrees.
Where do we go?
On our Lake Washington tours we usually tour to the north end of the lake (where we often see gators lounging on the surface or on the east bank of the lake) and through the reeds in the airboat trail on the north end of the lake. We often stop a time or two to share with you the kind of plants or trees that you see and what the alligators are doing. As we work our way to the northwest corner of the lake into the river itself we often see gators cruising in the river or jumping off the banks. Depending on water levels and the size of the boat we’re in at the time we may go over the weir and up the river a mile or two before heading back south down the river around the west side of the lake and back to the landing.
Our Three Forks Conservation tour is a totally different experience than our Lake Washington tour. We travel south through the the incredibly unique eco system as we slide across the acres fo lily pads and weave between the submerged trees and stumps of what was once a cow pasture before it was diked in to make it a reservoir. The Florida Wildlife Commission in conjuncion with the Saint Johns River Water Management Distrct has worked tirelessly for over ten years to make this a future fishing mecca until they ran into legal issues with the Semnole Indian Tribe of Florida and the Miccosukee Indian.s This is a real swamp boat ride experience but we don’t usually see as many alligators because of the expansive swamp environment with so many places to hide.

TITLE: FAQ - Island Marine Rentals
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need to bring my own cooler?
No you do not need to bring a cooler. We will provide one free of charge for every boat. We also offer ice and water by the bottle at our office.
Can I fish off the boat?
NO, fishing is not allowed as of this moment.
What type of stand up paddle boards do you have?
We have 12’ paddle boards with a max weight limit of 300lbs. They come with safety gear (life jacket, whistle and paddle). Our staff will train you free of charge as well. You can use these on the Gulf of Mexico and the bay. We also offer Go Pro video camera rentals to catch all the memories as well.
Do I have to wear a bicycle helmet?
If you are under 16 years of age you are required to wear a bicycle helmet – 16 years old or older you are not required to wear a helmet – However we strongly recommend every person operating a bicycle wear a helmet!
What type of Bicycles do you have?
We have beach cruisers – single speed coaster brake bikes for the sand (beach) “Giant Simple Single” and speed bicycles “Giant Cypress DX” hybrid bikes.
What type of Kayaks do you have?
All of our kayaks are “sit on top” ocean kayaks. We have 9ft and 13ft single kayaks and 13ft tandem kayaks. We also have dollies available to wheel them over to the Gulf of Mexico and transportation straps available if you want to strap them to your vehicle and take them to the Parks.
Are there any Scooter restrictions?
Scooters are motor vehicles – they are not allowed on the beaches, sidewalks, bicycle lanes or pedestrian trails and no freeways.
What type of Scooters do you have?
We have 1o Yamaha fuel injected, water cooled, 4 stroke scooters.
Do I have to wear a helmet when riding a scooter?
If you are under the age of 21 you are required to wear a helmet. If you are 21 years old or older it is your option to wear a helmet. We strongly recommend everyone wear a helmet! We provide them free of charge.
Do you have a 2 person scooter?
Most of our scooters are 2 seater models.
Will the scooter keep up in traffic?
Yes! The Yamaha scooters go 35 to 40 MPH.
What are the requirements to drive a scooter?
You must be 18 or older and have a valid automobile driver’s license (no temporary or permits) and have previous scooter or moped or dirt bike experience. Sorry, we do not train.
What are the requirements to rent a scooter?
You must be 18 years or older to sign a scooter rental contract. Fees are the rental price plus 7% FL sales tax plus a $200.00 deposit per scooter.
Can we drink alcohol on the boat?
Everyone on the boat can drink except the driver, zero tolerance, you can lose your automobile driver’s license
Are there any boating limits?
Our limits are Ft Desoto Park (15 miles South) and Three Rooker Island (19 miles North). Also the deck boats are allowed to go 3 miles out in the Gulf of Mexico.
Are there any boating restrictions?
The Pontoon boats and the 19' and 20 ' Hurricane boats are not allowed in the Gulf of Mexico. They stay in the Bay Areas. The 23 ' and 24' Hurricane Deck boats are allowed in the Gulf of Mexico up to 3 miles offshore.
How far ahead do I need to reserve a boat?
We recommend as soon as you know for sure what day and time you want to go to call for a reservation. Holidays and weekends usually book up 2 weeks ahead, week days 3 to 7 days ahead in season.
How do I reserve a boat?
When you know what day and time you are planning to go, call us at and we can tell you what boats are available and can reserve one for you with a major credit card; Visa, MC or Discover.
Does the rental price include the gas?
The rental price does not include fuel. All of the boats have the most fuel efficient engines on the market.
What is "Off Season?"
March 1 to Labor Day is our ON SEASON.
Day after Labor Day to the end of February is our OFF SEASON
What are your hours of operation?
We are open 9:00 am to 5:00 pm every day, all year.
We close early on major holidays, please call to confirm times.
We are not open on Christmas Day.
What about bathrooms on the water?
There are plenty of restaurants and parks that have restrooms plus most of our boats have built in bathrooms for your convenience.
Do I get a chart?
We do have charts of the area free to our customers and we give a full orientation as well. We also have brand new Garmin GPS navigation systems with depth finders on every boat. All the boating attractions are preprogrammed into these units for you.
What are the requirements to drive a boat?
You must be 25 or older to rent a boat. If you were born before January 1, 1988 – you need an ID and all drivers must have prior boat driving experience.
If you're born after that date (and are at least 25) you must have a .
Lifetime Safe Boaters Certificate
We do not train.
What are the requirements to rent a boat?
You must be 25 or older to sign a rental contract. Rental fees are the rental price plus 7% FL sales tax plus fuel (the boat is full when you leave the dock. We fill it back up when you return and you pay for the fuel that was used) and a $500.00 security deposit that is refunded at the end of the day (providing no damages or loss of equipment).

TITLE: Above All ATV Tours and Rentals | Frequently Asked Questions
FAQS
ATV Guided Tours, UTV Excursions & More – Frequently Asked Questions & Tips
We offer Private Family Tours
Our ATV Tours range from 2 hours to 6 hour rides.
ATVs are easy to ride, and we’ll show you how. If you’ve never ridden on an ATV before, we’d be happy to get you started. All our Guided Tours come with a safety instruction course from our professional guides before your ride. We’ll make sure you’re ready to go on our ATVs to make sure everyone’s safe.
Get plenty of sleep the night before. Riding ATVs is an active sport and having a good nights sleep will help you enjoy the time better.
Eat a good meal. Active sports use a lot of energy. Since Las Vegas is desert country, you will also want to make sure you hydrate your body before the tour.
Bring extra clothing. You will want to bring an extra set of clothes in case of weather changes and also to change into after the tour. Your clothes will get dusty when riding on the trails.
Bring comfortable shoes that will also protect your feet. No open-toed shoes or sandals are allowed on the tours. Rocks and debris could get kicked up and hurt your feet. Wear thick comfortable cotton socks.
If you sunburn easily, consider wearing a cool, long-sleeve shirt or bring sunblock. Sunblock should be water-based if possible so you do not collect the dust on your skin.
Don’t drink alcoholic beverages or take medication that makes you sleepy before riding ATVs. This can lead to accidents and we don’t want anyone to hurt themselves or others.
If you bring your own beverages to take along, make sure they’re in plastic containers with good sealing tops. Glass WILL break and insecure tops WILL vibrate off during the tour.
Chocolate will melt, you may want to consider another type of pocket snack if you should want to bring something along.
Be aware of your surroundings when walking about during breaks. There are just as many snakes and critters in the mountains as below in the desert.
And most of all, be ready to have a lot of fun!

Rules:
- Only what the text states. Never add outside knowledge. Never guess, round or convert prices. Empty is correct, invented is a failure.

TITLE: Kelowna café and museum offer families a taste of aviation this summer! - KF Centre For Excellence
Kelowna café and museum offer families a taste of aviation this summer!
June 2, 2025
The Convair Café and KF Centre for Excellence aviation exhibit launch Summer Saturdays, featuring a free kid’s meal and passport activity for participating families.
June 2, 2025 –KELOWNA – Make sure your summer bucket list includes savouring the incredible aviation legacy the Okanagan has to offer. Starting June 7, the Convair Café and KF Centre for Excellence are joining forces to bring you Summers Saturdays—an aviation themed café experience for the whole family, paired with a journey through the KF Centre’s award-winning interactive exhibit.
Located along the Okanagan Rail Trail just north of the Kelowna International Airport, the Convair Café is a one-of-a-kind aviation themed coffee shop. Guests can sit back and relax in real aircraft seats, immersed in an airplane cabin design. With hand-crafted seasonal beverages, house-made pastries and gourmet lunch fare, the café appeals to all appetites and modes of transport, offering an exciting spot to rest and refuel.
As part of the Summer Saturdays promotion, children ages 10 and under can receive a free kid’s meal at the Convair Café (with a $10 minimum adult purchase). The meal includes a grilled cheese sandwich, apple juice and paper airplane along with a special passport activity to help kids spread their wings. The passport invites them to complete their journey at the KF Centre for Excellence aviation exhibit, where they will receive a free cookie upon entry and a stamp for their passport!
“During the week we serve a variety of customers including Rail Trail users and local staff working in the airport community. By extending our opening hours to Saturdays and adding some new menu features, we’re introducing a budget-friendly option for families that will treat little ones to a first-class experience,” says Amber Estlin, Convair Café Manager.
Families visiting the KF Centre for Excellence can explore vintage aircraft, hands-on exhibits, and inspiring stories from the Okanagan’s past designed to engage visitors of all ages. “This partnership with the Convair Café is a great opportunity to welcome families to the Centre in a relaxed, engaging way”, says Chris Lapointe, Executive Director of the Centre for Excellence. “We invite visitors to enjoy some of the Convair Cafe’s delicious cookies on the Centre’s patio and experience the excitement of aviation with family and friends.”
is open Saturdays from 9:00am to 3:00 pm and weekdays 7:30am – 4:00pm. It is located at 5655 Airport Way, Kelowna (beside KF Aerospace). Street parking is available beside the café along Airport Way. TITLE: Odyssey 86 - 90 Years of the DC-3
Odyssey 86 – 90 Years of the DC-3
June 9 @ 6:00 pm
$38
Film Premiere & New DC-3 Exhibit Launch
Celebrate 90 years of one of the most iconic aircraft in aviation history at a special premiere event hosted by the KF Centre for Excellence. brings together aviation enthusiasts, community members, and history lovers for the premiere of a new short documentary film featuring Barry Lapointe and original crew members from the legendary 1986 around-the-world Odyssey flight.
The evening celebrates both the 90th anniversary of the Douglas DC-3 and the extraordinary Odyssey mission created to promote Expo 86 around the globe. In June 1986, the Odyssey DC-3 departed Canada on an ambitious international journey celebrating Expo 86’s theme: . Travelling through 28 countries and dozens of cities worldwide, the aircraft became a flying symbol of connection, innovation, and adventure during one of Canada’s most memorable international celebrations.
Nearly 40 years later, the aircraft now serves as a living tribute at the KF Centre for Excellence – preserving the stories, people, and pioneering spirit behind the mission for future generations.
About the Film
Produced in partnership with award-winning director Ryan Tebbutt of Edge Digital Media, the approximately 30-minute documentary shares firsthand stories from the crew behind the Odyssey ’86 mission while exploring the lasting legacy of the DC-3 aircraft – from wartime operations and commercial aviation to one of Canada’s great aviation adventures.
Featuring interviews, archival storytelling, and reflections from those who lived the journey, the film offers audiences a rare opportunity to hear the story directly from the people who experienced it.

TITLE: Board of Directors - KF Centre For Excellence
Board of
Directors
Barry loves aviation! He started flying at the age of 16 and has since logged over 18,000 flying hours (fixed and rotary wing); is an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer by trade; and the Founder & CEO of a leading Canadian aerospace company. Barry Lapointe’s passion for flight has resulted in a lifetime of dedication to the aerospace industry in Canada.
Starting as a small aircraft repair business servicing the BC Interior from a panel van, Barry has spent the last five decades building KF Aerospace (founded as Kelowna Flightcraft) into a leading Air Cargo operator; an Engineering (DAO), Maintenance and Modification provider; a Pilot Training organization for the Royal Canadian Air Force; and an aircraft leasing company.
Over those 50 years, he’s led and shaped a truly Canadian success story—KF Aerospace. KF is a multifaceted and highly integrated aviation company—and Canada’s largest commercial Aircraft Maintenance Organization. Employing nearly 1,100 dedicated staff across the country, Barry has them delivering exceptional quality, reliability, and on-time delivery. KF is respected by airline brands and cargo operators worldwide, competing with the industry giants while maintaining its Canadian roots.
Barry has served on dozens of public and private boards over the years, including Purolator Courier of which he is minority owner. His passion for aviation continues unabated and embodied in the creation of the Centre for Excellence to be built in Kelowna as a legacy to the importance of aerospace in Canada. “It will be a place where our community can rub shoulders, where kids get to see old airplanes up close and where we can get people excited about the history and the future of aviation,” he says.
Lapointe is an honorary lifetime member of ATAC and the AME associations and has been recognized by AIAC, AIABC, BCIT, Rotary, and many other organizations for his contributions and accomplishments in aerospace and the local communities. He has supported AME Community Colleges across Canada including Okanagan College and Mohawk College, and supported the University of British Columbia – Okanagan. Through the KF Charitable Foundation he actively supports causes across Canada including the Heart and Stroke Foundation, the Kids’ Cancer Care Foundation at KGH and Girls Fly Too. Barry was appointed the Order of British Columbia in 2015 and inducted into Canada’s Aviation Hall of Fame in 2019.
DAVID BURKE
David is a CPA and an accomplished executive with an entrepreneurial spirit and extensive experience building successful, growth-driven companies. In 2016, he sold StarDyne Technologies, a privately held software company he co-founded. Before StarDyne, David was CFO at Western Star Trucks Holdings and for 17 years held various senior financial and information technology positions with subsidiaries of Alcan Aluminum. David currently serves as a director for a large international family trust with significant interests overseas as well as Advisory Board Member for the KF Capital and KF Aerospace group of companies.
ALAN BUDDE
Alan has extensive government experience at the federal, provincial and municipal levels, taking on a range of leadership roles. He served with the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) for 22 years in a variety of domestic and overseas posts including responsibilities for helping secure the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver and Whistler. In 2014, Alan moved on to the Independent Investigations Office of BC (IIO) to assist this newly formed organization with the important mandate of police oversight. He now enjoys life in the Okanagan and has joined the City of Kelowna as the Security and Business Continuity Manager. Alan also serves as a Board Member for the Barry Lapointe Foundation.
Dylana Bloor
Dylana is a retired lawyer whose career focused on litigation and dispute resolution. Prior to her retirement, Dylana was a partner in a leading and well established regional firm.
Dylana, who was called to the B.C. bar in 2002, holds a Bachelor of Arts in Communications from the University of Calgary and a Bachelor of Laws from the University of British Columbia.
Dylana is experienced in arbitration, mediation and has appeared as counsel at both the trial and appellate levels of the British Columbia court. She has also appeared before the Supreme Court of Canada.
Sally Dennis
Sally is a lawyer. She earned her law degrees at Oxford University, the University of British Columbia and the University of Victoria. She practised as a business lawyer at a major Canadian law firm for many years before switching her focus to private client work, including trusts, private corporate governance, and personal and business succession planning. After a stint as general counsel to Intrawest PLC - the then owner and operator of multiple ski resort developments including Whistler Blackcomb - and serving in a law firm senior management role, in 2008 she joined a full-service regional BC law firm and resumed her private client practice. She retired from private practice in 2022 and now serves as a part-time legal consultant to KF Aerospace.
Sally was a director of Rugby Canada for seven years and was the chair of its board until 2024. She serves as Canada’s representative on World Rugby’s Council and is a member of its Executive Board. She is a director of Lion’s Gate Hospital Foundation and the chair of its governance committee, and a director of the KF Aerospace Centre for Excellence Association. She joined the advisory board of the KF Aerospace Group of Companies in early 2023 and became a director of KF Capital Ltd. in October 2023.
Sally divides her time between Deep Cove and Kelowna. She is married with three adult children and enjoys collecting cookbooks and cooking from them. She is an avid reader, loves to travel and is always planning her next foreign vacation.
Brad Imrich
Brad Imrich is a CPA with extensive experience in growth-oriented companies, and he currently manages all financial aspects of the Callahan Property Group (CPG) with a focus on operational excellence. Prior to joining CPG Brad was the President of StarDyne Technologies, a privately held software company. He has served in senior financial roles at Pacific Insight Electronics, Western Star Trucks Holdings Ltd. and Placer Dome Inc. Brad graduated with a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of British Columbia and obtained his CPA, CA designation while with Ernst & Young. He is a past Director of both the Economic Development Commission of Kelowna and the Okanagan Science and Technology Council.
Management
CHRIS LAPOINTE
Born and raised in Vancouver, Chris joined the newly created Kelowna-based Flair Airlines in 2005, relocating to Kelowna in 2008 with his wife Mary and son Matthew as the business expanded. In his role as Vice President and General Manager of Commercial Operations for Flair, Chris was pivotal in the successful growth and management of the B737 charter airline operation, guiding it from inception through its sale as a commercial passenger carrier in 2018.
Chris’ diverse career also includes senior roles within destination resort management, tour and travel, special event management, and consumer show production companies. His life-long dedication to volunteering with community organizations and industry associations has fostered a strong understanding of local dynamics and excellent community connections. When is the Best Time to Go Kayaking in Cocoa Beach? Seasonal Tour Information
When is the best time to go kayaking? It depends on what you want to see and what kind of weather you like. Cocoa Beach has warm weather all year round, but each season brings its own magic to the water. Our guided kayak tours are always full of amazing things to see and do, whether you’re visiting in the summer to see the glowing waters of bioluminescence or in the winter to enjoy the crisp, wildlife-rich air.
Daytime Tours
Our daytime tours are available throughout the summer; however, we advise taking the early tours due to the high temperatures that can occur in Florida during the summer. You can see dolphins, manatees, birds, and a lot of other wildlife during our day kayak tours.
Bioluminescence Tours
Our bioluminescence kayak tours are busiest in the summer. When the sun goes down, the water glows with a magical blue-green light. Summer nights are unforgettable, whether you’re paddling through the Thousand Islands or near the Banana River. Make your reservations early because these tours fill up quickly!
June-AugustDaytime Highs: 87–88 °F (31 °C)Nighttime Lows: 76–78 °F (24–26 °C)
Fall is the best time for daytime eco-tours because the heat and crowds go down. Animals like manatees, dolphins, and birds that migrate are often active. In calm, breezy weather, you can explore the mangrove tunnels or take a guided paddle through the Indian River Lagoon.
Average Temperatures During Fall Season
September–NovemberDaytime Highs: 82–85 °F (28–29 °C)Nighttime Lows: 66–73 °F (19–23 °C)
In the winter, the weather is cooler, and the best time to see Florida manatees is in the warmer backwaters. Birdwatchers love this time of year because they can see herons, egrets, and roseate spoonbills. Come with us for a relaxing paddle in the calm winter weather on a sunny day.
December–FebruaryDaytime Highs: 70 °F (21 °C)Nighttime Lows: 55–60 °F (13–16 °C)
In the spring, the weather is mild, the winds are calm, and there are many opportunities to see wildlife native to the Thousand Islands in Cocoa Beach. There are dolphins that play and plants that bloom along the shore. It’s a nature lover’s dream. Spring is also an excellent season for family-friendly tours.
March-MayDaytime Highs: 80–83 °F (27–28 °C)Nighttime Lows: 60–68 °F (15–20 °C)

Check the weather in advance and dress appropriately.

Bring water or sports drinks to ensure you stay hydrated.
Before launching, your guide gives a quick safety briefing and shows you basic paddle strokes. Everyone is fitted with a comfortable life vest and a properly sized paddle. Beginners are welcome—no experience required.
Even strong swimmers need one—it’s your best safety net in deep water.
Skip the trip if conditions look rough. Calm, sunny days make for the best paddles.
Match your kayak to your skill level—some are built for beginners, others for pros.
Kayaking is more fun (and safer) with friends who’ve got your back.
Sunscreen for day tours, mosquito repellent for all tours, and water or a sports drink to stay hydrated. Depending on the weather, you may also want to bring a jacket.
So grab your gear, your friends, and your sense of adventure. A little preparation—and a lot of enthusiasm—will make your Cocoa Beach kayak trip unforgettable. Stay safe and have fun!
Once on the water, glide through calm channels surrounded by mangrove tunnels and open lagoons. Watch for dolphins, manatees, herons, and other coastal wildlife as your guide shares fun facts about the local ecosystem.

Whether you bring a waterproof camera or use a phone pouch, you’ll leave with photos and memories that truly capture the magic of the Space Coast.

About the Turkey Creek Sanctuary
The Turkey Creek Sanctuary is a small nature reserve in the city of Palm Bay in Brevard County, Florida, and incorporates both salty hammock and sand pine ridge habitats. The sanctuary is part of the Brevard County Environmentally Endangered Lands (EELs) program, consisting of 130 acres of wonder, biodiversity, and natural resources.
Turkey Creek Sanctuary is the pride of Palm Bay and is known for its gorgeous foliage that includes sand pines, oaks, and saw palmettos. Established in 1981, the Sanctuary offers a 1.85-mile boardwalk passing through hydric (wet) hammock, mesic (moist) hammock, and sand pine scrub communities, both excellent for viewing a multitude of wildlife. The creek is an important breeding ground for both salt and freshwater fish.
The Turkey Creek Sanctuary is also part of the East Florida section of the Great Florida Birding Trail.
A Fantastic Location for Kayaking
Paddling down the black water creek you’ll enjoy seeing manatees, alligators, Florida cooters (turtles), dolphins and you may even see an otter or gar. The tannin-stained waters are full of bass, and birds abound in the old pine canopy, including ospreys and owls, woodpeckers, purple martins, and many other migratory species.
The sanctuary is also covered with glorious sand dunes said to date back over 2,000 years and there is a 4,000-foot boardwalk from which you can take in all the sights in this amazing protected space.
Adventure Kayak Tours Departure Location
Kayak Tours leave from the west end of the sanctuary, located on the beautiful and unspoiled Turkey Creek. This is the perfect launch spot so all you have to do is enjoy the beauty and wonders of the natural environment as we float downstream.
You’ll take a leisurely paddle into the captivating, primitive, meandering Turkey Creek Sanctuary. You will learn about a forest of trees that grows directly from the creek floor as well as along the banks. Your skilled, experienced guide will explain why thriving estuary is so important to protecting the inland environment and to support so many species of wildlife throughout the river and bays, including manatee, dolphin, tarpon, turtles, and many more.

Location: Palm Bay, Florida
Class: Flatwater Creek with a typically light current.
Distance Paddled: 4 miles downriver.
Water: fresh to brackish.
Wildlife: Manatees, birds (Egrets, Herons, etc.), alligators, turtles, Water Moccasins, Mangroves, salt marsh grasses, scrub oaks.
